This  document,  the  Owner's  Technical  Specification  Part  B  (OTS  Part  B)  defines  requirements  for  the engineering, procurement and construction of each of Rumah and Nairyah IPPs that the Contractor shall comply with, which are in addition to those specified in OTS Part A.
In addition to the technical requirements of this section, the selection of the technology, the design and the arrangement of the Power Units shall be based on the site conditions as described in OTS Part A.
The Plant shall be designed, manufactured and configured in such a way as to optimise Plant performance, thus providing  a  competitive  least  cost  electricity  generation  taking  into  account  the  design  and  operation requirements of this OTS, Part A and Part B.
The Plant shall be designed, manufactured, installed and be suitable in every respect for continuous operation at the Guaranteed Net Contracted Power Capacity 1,800 MW ± 5% (GNCPC) at part loads, under the anticipated transient operation as well as the climatic conditions and the site environmental restrictions and shall exhibit high availability and reliability. Please refer to  section 6.4 for the Availability Reliability and Maintainability statement. In order to demonstrate the availability and reliability, the Contractor shall perform a RAM study.
The Plant shall be designed to permit unconstrained operation over the full range of ambient conditions. The Plant  shall  have  operationally  flexible  power  capacity  that  will  play  a  key  role  in  providing  flexible  power generation.
All the sections below (this documentPart B) define the Owner's requirements for the configuration of the Plant in addition to that specified in OTS Part A. OTS Part A shall generally have the priority over OTS Part B. In case of any requirement specified in OTS Part B found to be in contradiction with the requirements stated in OTS Part A,  the  conservative  and  stringent  requirement  of  them  will  prevail  in  addition  to  the  compliance  of  the requirement stated in Part A.
label: text

Starting from the (Limited) Notice to Proceed up to the end of the Warranty Period all parties to the Project (in particular, EPC Contractor, Owner, Owner's Representatives) shall consequently use a Project Communication & Document Management System (PC&DMS): ' Think project '.
This system shall, in general, manage the following tasks:
- Archiving and distribution of all Project-related documents (engineering and non-engineering)
- Collaboration between parties to the Project and the related workflows, e.g., during design review (e.g., uploading, reviewing, commenting, approving, revising of documents)
- Project correspondence (by e-mail), incl. connection to Outlook (it shall be made sure that all Project related correspondence is stored at one central place: PC&DMS). This connection should allow to bring over preliminary correspondence pieces exchanged prior to the start of the PC&DMS.
The PC&DMS shall be implemented (set-up) in such a way that the following Project basic requirements are satisfied:
- Project-specific documents attributing (numbering)
- Project-specific correspondence attributing (numbering)
- Project-specific correspondence distribution matrix
- Project-specific security (access control).
Please refer to Appendix W of the EPC Contract for detailed requirements are regarding PC&DMS. The PC&DMS shall be ready for use at the date of Contract signing or Limited Notice to Proceed, whichever occurs first).
Contractor shall be responsible for consequent and obligatory use of the PC&DMS, incl. proper attributing and upload of documents and correspondence, training all users as well as any maintenance activities, if required. All costs related to the use of the PC&DMS, including but not limited to the software license, hardware, costs for system administration, training, user support, shall be borne by Contractor.
There will be Owner's PC&DMS' Administrator overlooking all activities related to the use of PC&DMS who will be in close contact with the Contractor's Document Controller.
Contractor shall provide an uninterrupted dedicated high speed Internet access for every PC&DMS user group (e.g., in particular document controllers, design review team, Project Management team) allowing PC&DMS to manage even an extreme workload without delay. Only in case of sudden technical problems (e.g., sudden interruption in internet  service)  and  urgent  cases  (e.g.,  urgent  distribution  of  documents)  the  Contractor  may  use  other communication means. After the normal situation has been restored, all parties shall continue using the PC&DMS and parties are responsible to retrospectively upload all documents into the PC&DMS which were transmitted offline.

The Contractor shall also allow the Owner, and the Owner's Representative and any third party nominated by the Owner unhindered access to all parts of the Work in progress and where normal access is obstructed he shall provide temporary alternative access at its own cost.

The Contractor shall provide fencing and barriers  to segregate the construction areas from  operational areas within the Plant.
label: text

The Contractor  shall  make its  own  arrangements  for  the  supply  to  site  of  all  materials,  plant  and  resources necessary for the execution of the Works. The Contractor shall accordingly employ agents as necessary to secure the appropriate authorizations from the Authorities for entry into the Saudi Arabia.
The  disposal  of  excess  material  excavated  soil,  disposal  of  demolished  items  shall  be  within  the  scope  of Contractor based on their due diligence and ESIA requirement.
The amount of the EPC Contract price will be deemed to include all costs associated with the importation and clearing  of  such  goods  and  materials  and  the  Contractor  shall  be  responsible  for  all  costs  and  arrangements necessary in order to transport all plant and materials to site safely, economically and on programme, including offloading and transporting to the required positions on site and shall obtain all necessary approvals from the relevant highway/maritime authorities and others as necessary.
The Contractor shall advise the Owner of the movement of abnormal loads and shall provide full details of such loads to the Engineer. In addition, the Contractor shall identify any limits on the weight and/or physical size of plant that can be delivered to the site and shall be responsible for any additional costs associated with modification or upgrading required to the transport route to make it suitable for abnormal loads.
The transport route to site shall be agreed with the relevant authorities and shall take account of local restrictions. The method of transportation shall be suitable for the materials, plant and resources carried without causing nuisance from dust, spillage, etc. or damage to the existing roads etc. The delivery of materials etc. shall not be permitted outside site working hours.
The Contractor shall inform himself fully as to all transport facilities, requirements and loading gauges to ensure that all equipment as packed for transport shall conform to these limitations of Services During Construction Period
label: text

Following EPC Contract award, the Contractor shall provide, as a minimum, the following services during the Plant construction period:
- At laydown areas and work faces, temporary fencing, lighting and guarding and all other materials and services necessary for the safety and security of persons and property;
- Permanent marks from which the principal centre lines will be established will be provided by Contractor in agreement with the Owner together with level marks at suitable places on the Site. These beacons and benchmarks shall be the sole points of reference for setting out and levelling purposes and shall be carefully maintained by the Contractor. The Contractor shall provide for the sole use of the Owner's Representative all equipment required for the checking of the setting out of the Works. Equipment sha ll be complete with all accessories, all to the satisfaction of the Owner's Engineer, and shall be maintained in good working order. The Contractor shall provide the Owner's Representative with all assistance necessary for checking the setting out of the Works;
- Temporary roads, parking areas, etc.
- Warehouse
- Compressed air supply
- Telephones and fire-fighting equipment
- Waste disposal facilities
- Sanitary facilities and sewage disposal (septic tank and fecal suction truck will be used for sewage treatment of construction facility area); and
- Site security e.g. Gate House, badge access system, CCTV, key and master key system
- Temporary Storage Facilities for spares when the warehouse is not operational
Notwithstanding the above, the Owner reserves the right to request the Contractor to provide any additional services reasonably required to safely and effectively complete the Project until the whole of the Works has achieved Commercial Operation.

The Contractor shall be responsible for ensuring that all waste including contaminated or hazardous soil or sub soil arising from the Works is deposited, treated, kept, disposed of and carried in accordance with the provisions of all applicable environmental regulations. The Contractor shall ensure that the methods employed in handling, storing and disposal of all dangerous or noxious substances are such that pollution or contamination of the Site or surrounding areas shall not occur. The Contractor shall include for the provision of training for the operation and maintenance staff.
Training is to cover all aspects of Plant, equipment and system, and operation and maintenance requirements, as  required to  run the Plant in a safe and efficient  manner. Training shall take place early enough to allow operation staff to participate fully in the commissioning process.
The training package and programme shall be agreed with the Owner at least six months before the start of commissioning according to 3.4 requirements. Details of the training proposed, including DCMS OEM training, shall be provided.
For further details regarding the requirements please also refer to the Appendix W of the EPC Contract.
label: text

chunks.text:
The Contractor shall develop and implement a Training Programme for the Owner's designated personnel that shall be site based. This Contractor training shall complement and be integrated with Owner's long -term training programme in order to optimise the total training package.
The overall objectives of the Contractor's Training Programme shall be to:
- Deliver thorough training to introduce, instruct and supervise the Owners technical staff to the essential aspects  of  the  Plant  for  proper,  safe  and  efficient  operation  and  achieve  a  high  standard  of  awareness, knowledge and understanding of the Plant and Plant systems.
- Provide an effective contribution to the overall training and development of the Owner's personnel.
The Contractor shall ensure adequate training in all aspects of its codes of practice and safety rules including the training of the Owner's staff engaged in plant commissioning. Training of the Owner's staff in the application of the Owner's safety rule system will be provided by the Owner.
The timing of Contractor's training activities shall be co -ordinated with the Owner's training activities. The aim is for the Owner's personnel to be trained early enough such that they can fully participate in the commissioning process under the direction of the Contractor's commissioning engineers.

- All  junior  staff  will  have  reached  such  a  degree  of  competence  to  allow  understanding  and  practical application in their specialised field.
All expenses for Owner's and Operator's personnel e.g. living accommodation, travelling expenses, visa, daily allowance etc, will be at Owner's cost.

The Contractor will be obliged to utilise Good Practice in preparing the design of the Plant.  Good Practices means those practices, methods, equipment, specifications and standards of safety and performance (as may change from time to time) employed by experienced international contractors or operators in the electricity generation industry engaged in the same type of undertaking under the same or similar circumstances and conditions which, in  the exercise of reasonable judgement in light of the facts known at the time the judgement was made, are considered good, safe and prudent practice commensurate with standards of safety, performance, dependability, efficiency and economy. Equipment proposed shall be from reputable manufacturers with sufficient experience accumulated on the particular units and equipment proposed.
The Contractor, if unable to perform the engineering, design and construction supervision activities within their own resources, shall engage reputable engineering consultant(s) with specific international experience to engineer, design and supervise erection and commissioning of the Project.
The engineering, construction, testing and commissioning of the Project shall be in-line with the documents/drawings submitted by the Contractor and approved by Owner. Modifications, if required, to the approved documents/drawings and corresponding change in construction, testing and commissioning of the Project shall be brought to Owner's notice and such modifications shall be carried out only after the written approval of Owner. Wherever there is a considerable change in the scope of work, the same shall  be mutually discussed and agreed between Owner and the Contractor through a Change Notice document. The Change Notice document shall specify the proposed technical modifications, reasons for the same, its commercial impacts, related schedule of activities along with timelines and responsibilities of all the parties involved.
label: text

The  EPC  Contractor  shall  submit,  before  starting  the  engineering  activities  as  such  the  functional breakdown  of  the  project  and  the  services  of  the  general  engineering  activities,  along  with  the corresponding design documents.

- o Surveys  and  verification  at  the  site  of  the  exact  position  and  characteristics  of  equipment  and networks at the limit of the batteries to which the Contractor shall provide his connections
- o Checking of information appearing in the documents and drawings supplied by the Project Owner to the Contractor.
- General process engineering activities
The Contractor shall be responsible for the definition and engineering of the general process and the special processes employed for reaching the objectives fixed, handling the functions of the Plant and ensuring the best availability, reliability and maintainability.
For this purpose, the Contractor shall not limit himself to assembling the parts supplied by his Subcontractors, but he shall:

This document shall contain all the information required for the operation and maintenance of equipment during the operation phase, as well as all the procedures required to carry out any necessary repairs during the lifetime of the equipment.
Manuals shall include, but not limited to, the following:
- Equipment storage requirements
- Erection instructions with drawings. Commissioning and initial test instructions
- Operating instructions, including but not limited to safety precautions and operating limits
- Maintenance procedures, routine adjustments, preventive maintenance schedules and any predictive maintenance recommendations
- Parts  illustrations,  including  parts  lists  adequate  for  the  purpose  of  identifying  and  ordering replacement parts and designation of the number required per component and lists of recommended spare parts
- Detailed descriptions of the functions of each principal component of a system
- Safety precautions
- Preservation  requirements  for  equipment  covering  initial  preservation  measures,  and  during operations which may arise because of different operational schemes that put equipment / units in idle conditions for extended period. Examples include provision of nitrogen blanketing, flushing lines etc.
- Provision  must  be  provided  for  preservation  of  equipment  which  is  susceptible  to  corrosion  in extended periods of standby / idle. The preservation strategy for assets susceptible for short 1-6 months, medium 6-12 months, long term >12months should be specified in the O&M manual but NDZ (notice to deviate from 0 MW) should remain at <6hrs as a minimum. For equipment supply and storage on site prior to construction specifically rotating plant, humidity shall be controlled to <30%RH at all times, passive or active systems are acceptable but provision for monitoring humidity should be provided

chunks.text:
The  Contractor  shall  apply  the  Reference  Designation  System  for  Power  Plants  (RDS-PP)  equipment  numbering system for identifying plant and equipment. The system shall be clear, concise and systematic and shall be applied by the Contractor and its sub-contractors consistently across all the Plant areas and shall be easily incorporated into an Asset Management System. Equipment identification in the External Facilities shall be in accordance with the existing installations.
Instruction plates, nameplates and labels shall be provided for all equipment, valves, cabinets and panels of the Plant giving particulars of duty, size, serial number and full information for identification and operation in English language only. Where considered appropriate for safety/emergency purposes (such as caution plates and emergency exists etc.),  the  Contractor  shall  agree  with  the  Owner  and  provide  as  part  of  its  Work  scope  a  reasonable  number  of instruction plates, nameplates and labels in both the English language and Arabic.
Labels  shall  be  of  sufficient  size  to  carry  a  full  description  of  the  plant  item  and  a  unique  item  alpha-numeric identification. Abbreviations in the plant description shall only be used with prior approval of the Investor.
Labels shall be fitted such that they are not readily lost or broken during routine operation and maintenance.
Any labels damaged or defaced during installation or Plant start-up shall be replaced by the Contractor prior to Taking Over by the Investor.
label: text

chunks.text:
Platforms  shall  be  provided  around  equipment  as  required  for  maintenance  work,  testing,  inspection  and  safe operation. Platforms shall be sized to facilitate safe ergonomic operation of manual valves and equipment between waist and shoulder level of a standard man. Relief valves shall be grouped together and an access platform provided. Operating valves which cannot be serviced from a platform shall be operated by other approved means.
All platforms to be visited on a daily basis shall be provided with stairways except where a permanent access ladder is  the  only  feasible  means  of  access.  All  interior  and  exterior  platforms,  gratings,  checker  plate,  stairways  and handrails shall be galvanised.
label: text

chunks.text:
Platforms shall be constructed using galvanised open steel flooring in a normal condition and a suitable grade of GRP or stainless grating in areas of high salinity, in accordance to the internationally recognized standards and shall cater for the relevant loadings for maintenance. Frequently accessed platform shall not be less than 1 m wide and those platforms shall be extended up to the equipment, valves and instrumentation which they serve.
All edges of floors, platforms and walkways shall be provided with curbs or kicking strips.
Particular  attention  shall  be  paid  to  internal  and  external  access  in  order  to  facilitate  inspection,  cleaning  and maintenance. For GT enclosure inside, OEM standard is acceptable.
label: text

chunks.text: The Contractor shall build, after Notice to Proceed, Site office facilities for the Owner, Owner's Engineers and Owner's Representative, as described in SCHEDULE Q.
label: text

chunks.text:
To minimise spares holding and enhance maintenance and operation, plant items performing similar functions e.g. valves, switchgear shall, as far as practicable, be standardised and obtained from a minimum number of suppliers. Similarly, the design of major plant items shall be consistent to maximise interchangeability of components.
For Gas turbine package, vendors of instruments and control system will be selected from Supplier's standard list of reputable vendors to realize high safe, reliable and optimal unit operation.
Type/model of the instruments will be selected as per Supplier's design practice.
label: text

chunks.text:
Plant  maintenance  philosophies  and  the  selection  of  equipment  shall  reflect  the  need  for  a  Plant  with  a  high availability.
The Contractor shall ensure that their detailed design complies with the Availability, Reliability and Maintainability requirements during the course of design implementation.
label: text

chunks.text:
Materials  selected  by  the  Contractor  shall  be  proven  to  be  suitable  to  all  relevant  process  and  environmental conditions prevailing at the Site, and sufficient for the complete Plant life cycle.
Components of the Plant which are subject to abrasion or potential high rates of wear including heat transfer surfaces shall  be  selected  from  proven  grades  of  high  corrosion/erosion  resistant  materials  (copper  alloys,  nickel  alloys, stainless steels and titanium).
GRP water supply pipes shall be manufactured in accordance with AWWA C 950. The pipe shall have a minimum stiffness of 2500 N/m2 in accordance with AWWA C 950 and shall include an internal and external corrosion barrier.
Stainless-steel piping shall be passivated in accordance with ASTM A380 after shop and site fabrication has been completed as required. Socket welded is acceptable for 2" and below including stainless steel materials.
Where  materials  are  subject  to  an  elevated  risk  of  corrosion  (e.g.  due  to  stagnant  water,  high  temperatures, aggressive conditions or  presence of crevices) additional protection shall be applied e.g. by  coating  or  cathodic protection.
label: text

chunks.text:
Storage facilities for all operational chemicals shall be provided. At least  7 days (shall be considered for 30 days keeping in view consumption, long lead delivery and  availability) storage shall be provided for chemical for the operation of the Power Facility. The tank shall be equipped with level measurement for remote monitoring.
Storage facilities for hazardous chemicals shall be subject to review and comment by Owner at the design stage of the Project.
The chemicals supplied for this Plant shall be of food grade /non-carcinogenic if required. All chemicals used in the project shall be in line with the EIA study recommendations.
All chemical handling equipment shall be bundled such that any chemical spillage is contained. Each storage tank shall be equipped with a bund having a volume of at least 110% of the capacity of the tank. If hydrochloric acid is used, the acid bulk storage tank shall be equipped with adequate fume extraction facilities.
For chemical spill management, secondary containment shall be considered for truck unloading so to avoid spillage.
Chemical storage area shall be provided with fire detection and sprinkler type protection system as per NFPA 101 and 400.
label: text

chunks.text:
Areas where a potential flammable atmosphere may exist shall be classified to the relevant sections of the Institute of Petroleum (IP) and IEC codes, or other internationally recognised standard. Suitably certified equipment shall be used in  the  designated  hazardous  areas  adopting  the  installation  practices  in  line  with  applicable  IEC  or  other internationally recognized codes. To the maximum extent practical, equipment requiring operator attention and/or electrical equipment shall not be installed in hazardous areas.
The Contractor is required to demonstrate in the Plant Design that adequate segregation of electrical equipment from hazardous areas has been made, and that no hazardous area extends beyond the Site boundary fencing.
The Contractor shall appoint an independent specialist to undertake a HAZOP study to demonstrate the safety and integrity of the Plant design. Owner shall be invited to attend all HAZOP meetings. The results of the HAZOP shall be made available to Owner and relevant Competent Authority prior to construction.
HAZOP studies shall be carried out for entire plant including power plant and all subsystems at the appropriate time during the design and the construction phase to ensure timely implementation of HAZOP study results, if any, without affecting the project schedule.
The Contractor shall appoint an IECEx or other internationally recognized standard certified/authorized 3rd party for review, inspection and certification of all hazardous area equipment and installations at site. The aforesaid 3rd party shall be proposed by the Contractor and shall be approved by the Owner prior to its selection.

Damage to any property belonging to Owner, the Government or others, due to accident or exposure caused by the Contractor's activities during and after construction activities, or during plant operation, shall be restored by the Contractor at their cost. The Contractor shall be held responsible for any damage caused by the Contractor's activities to the adjoining properties.
No excavation shall be started without the presence of the representative of the respective authorities of the existing buried/on  ground/aboveground  services  in  the  concerned  area.  Written  permission  shall  be  required  from  the concerned parties before the start of any excavations. The Contractor shall make arrangements to expose, support and  protect  the  related  existing  services  and  shall  include  in  their  scope,  the  works  involved  in  overcoming  the obstacles caused by the existing services by deeper excavations, necessary temporary supports, complete relocation or any other means which may deem fit and are approved by the respective Owners or the Government.

chunks.text:
Steel  sections  shall  be  new  and  shapes  shall  conform  to  American,  British,  European,  Japanese  Standards,  GB Standards or equivalent international standards subject to approval by the Owner during detailed Engineering stage. All structural steel sections shall be hot rolled with a minimum grade A572 in accordance with ASTM standards and the AISC manual for steel construction. Contractor can use built up section higher than 400mm as per the design requirement subject to the QA/QC of the built up section is approved by the Owner. In this case the utilization ratio for built up members shall not be more than 90% for design Pre-engineered steel structures shall be approved by the Owner/Owner's Engineer. All  pre-engineered  constructions  shall  be  in  accordance  with  the  specification  of  steel works, especially the description of material, etc.
For HRSG following materials shall be applied:
A572 : HRSG main frames.
ASTM A36 : Casing/ducting, diverter, by-pass and exhaust stack, secondary structures (i.e. platforms, stairways, etc.)
All bolts in elevated steelwork connections shall be minimum grade ASTM A325 or A490 high strength bolts to suit the required design. All holding down bolts shall be minimum grade ASTM A307. Finishes etc. shall be selected such, to eliminate galvanic corrosion. Bolt finishes shall conform with the finishes applied to the steelwork elements which they connect. Welded connections will comply with the AWS D1.1 of the American Welding Society.
Non Destructive Inspection shall fulfill the requirements of AWSD1.1 of the American Welding Society.

chunks.text:
All  materials  in  contact  with  seawater  and  brine  if  applicable  shall  be  of  suitable  design  and  shall  have  proven suitability in comparable installations. Corrosion due to inadequate combination of different metals must be avoided.
Where  materials  are  subject  to  an  elevated  risk  of  corrosion  (e.g.  due  to  stagnant  water  high  temperatures, aggressive conditions or  presence of crevices) additional protection shall be applied e.g. by  coating  or  cathodic protection.

chunks.text:
The whole preparation and paint system shall be suitable for the operating environment specified. In general, all paintings have to be shop finish painted.
Though proprietary items may be used in their standard finish, subject to the approval of the Investor care shall be taken in the application of this principle, to ensure that cosmetic, and more importantly safety and operational, colour clashes do not occur. For specified applications, adequate supervision shall be provided for all stages of preparation, application and testing.
The  Contractor  shall  provide  painting  specifications  and  application  methods  that  are  suitable  for  the  exposure conditions  in  accordance  with  the  international  standards  and  painting  manufacturer's  recommendations.  The painting specification shall include the paints to be applied, thinners or any additives that may be required, tools and instruments required to prepare the surfaces, the application of protective coats, quality control, quality assurance and personnel safety.
During detail design, GT OEM should prepare painting specification for relevant supply package which needs to follow painting class and durability requirements as per section 5.3.1 of this document, and submit it for approval to the Owner.
All steelworks shall be protected in accordance with EN ISO 12944 and EN ISO 14713 or equivalent. Galvanising work shall be performed by means of the hot dip galvanizing process, unless otherwise specified and shall comply with the following standards: EN ISO 14713 and ISO 1461.
The coating durability shall be based on a 25 years of Design life (PPA term) painting system for outdoor and also for 25 years of Design life (PPA term)  painting system for Indoor. The ambient environment shall be classified in the C4 for outdoor installations and C3 categories for indoor atmospheric corrosion as a minimum or as per Section 5.3.12 whichever is stringent. Where more corrosive environment will prevail, EPC shall do proper due diligence and provide the solution accordingly subject to Owner's approval.
label: text

chunks.text: All switchyard structures shall be Hot Dipped Galvanized with C4 category for 25 years of Design life(PPA term) or as per Section 5.3.12 whichever is stringent. After all machining, forming and welding has been completed, all steelwork surfaces shall be thoroughly cleaned of rust, scale, welding slag or spatter and other contaminations prior to any painting. The surface of all non-ferrous parts usually painted, shall be cleaned, rubbed down, stopped, filled and given one priming coat of paint in preparation for the under and finishing coats. Any  damage  occurring  to  any  part  of  a  painting  scheme  shall  be  made  good  to  the  same  standard  of  corrosion protection  and  appearance  as  that  originally  employed.  Any  finish  coat  applied  on  site  shall  be  considered  for decorative purposes only. Interior structural steel and equipment and materials with a shop applied finish paint system shall only be touch-up painted at site. The  following  articles  contain  various  lists  of  equipment  and  materials,  identifying  the  painting  work  typically required for each kind of item. These lists should be used to establish the general philosophy for the scope of the painting work and any additions or changes to equipment as the detailed design and procurement are completed should be treated accordingly. Applied coatings shall have a design life to first maintenance of minimum 25 years from PCOD (duration between manufacturing/painting until PCOD need to be added on the top of 25 years). Following codes and standards shall be followed for concrete and metal corrosion protection work.

All steelworks shall be blast cleaned (to SA 2-1/2 or SA 3 as applicable (Swedish Standard if submitted in English language or ISO 8501 whichever is stringent). Paint systems applied to surfaces which may at any time be submerged below water shall not be susceptible to debonding or other degradation through cathodic action.
The components and/or equipment shall be mechanically and /or chemically cleaned during the following stages of the Contract.
- Cleaning in workshop
- Cleaning before painting and/or corrosion protection (application of prime coat)
- Cleaning before erection and during installation.
Cleaning of fabricated component items shall be carried out after fabrication and final heat treatment or welding at manufacturer's works or at site, as appropriate.
For cleaning in workshop and before painting mechanical cleaning as opposed to alternative chemical cleaning is the preferred method for works cleaning except where this is precluded by design or access considerations.
Machined surfaces shall be protected during the cleaning operations.
In the event of the surfaces not being cleaned to the purchaser's satisfaction, such parts of the cleaning procedures or agreed alternatives as are deemed necessary to overcome the deficiencies shall be carried out at the supplier's sole expense.
For reclining small areas, hand cleaning by wire brushing may be permitted. Wire brushes used on austenitic steel bristles.
Austenitic  stainless  steels,  copper  and  aluminium  alloys,  cast  iron,  bimetallic  and  metallic/plastic  items,  and components fabricated by spot welding or riveting shall not be chemically cleaned. All weld areas shall be suitably stress relieved before chemical cleaning.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text: Chemical cleaning shall be done for boiler pressure parts components at site. The detailed procedure for chemical cleaning as well as the system for which chemical cleaning is required shall be submitted by the contractor for Owner's approval.
label: text

chunks.text: Main steam, hot and cold reheat piping and any other piping system as necessary shall be subjected to steam blowing. The procedure and the system for which steam blowing is required will be submitted by the EPC Contractor for Owner ' s approval.
label: text

chunks.text: Mechanical cleaning shall be carried out by abrasive blasting.
label: text

chunks.text:
The Metal surfaces shall be clean and free of mil scale, rust, dirt, grease and any other deleterious matter.
Where metal surfaces are to be painted the surface profiles shall conform to the painting specification requirements. Where this does not apply surfaces shall have a surface texture not coarser than Grade 80 abrasive paper.
label: text

chunks.text:
Abrasives containing silica, silicates or slag residues shall not be used for water/steam side surfaces of plant except for cleaning sand castings, where hydro blasting with sand may be used.
For austenitic materials only, abrasives containing 98% or more of aluminia, Al2 O3, shall be used.
label: text

chunks.text: After cleaning, abrasive and debris shall be thoroughly removed for components.
label: text

chunks.text: The procedure shall comprise pre-treatment acid treatment to achieve cleanliness equivalent to that specified for mechanical cleaning. The procedure to be adopted must meet with the purchaser's approval.
label: text

chunks.text: As soon as all items have been cleaned and within four hours of the subsequent drying, they shall be given suitable anti-corrosion protection. All water and steam side surfaces shall be protected by the application of approved water-soluble corrosion inhibitors, or vapour phase inhibitors that can be subsequently removed by site water washing or steam blowing. The gas side of steam generating plant items shall be protected by the application of temporary protective that do not require to be removed before commissioning, but which are removed during initial firing. However, the designed temporary painting system shall be suitable for long term storage at the site corrosive atmosphere as applicable. The rate of application of volatile corrosion inhibitors shall be at least 10 grams per square metre or 35 grams per cubic metre, whichever is the greater, except for pipes up to 300 mm diameter for which the minimum application rates shall be 5 grams per square metre. Immediately after the protective treatment has been applied all vessels and pipes shall be suitably sealed off by discs or caps or approved alternatives to prevent ingress from the surroundings. Cylindrical plugs shall not be driven into the ends of pipes. These protective covers shall not be removed until immediately before final connection is made to the associated equipment.
label: text

chunks.text:
Painting shall be done only when the surface temperature is above 5°C. Surface temperature must be at least 3°C above dew point to ensure that condensation does not occur on the surface. Reasonable protection against precipitation shall be exercised for the painting of outdoor parts. Precautions shall also be taken against solar radiation to ensure that the specified dry film thickness of priming or finish coats is obtained. Any prime coat exposed to excess humidity, rain, dust etc., before drying, shall be permitted to dry and the damaged area of primer shall be removed and the surface prepared and primed again. Sheltered or unventilated horizontal surfaces on which dew may collect require more protection, and to achieve this an additional top coat of paint shall be applied.
The temperature quoted as 'normal' in the 'Paint System Tables' refers to the average local climatic conditions.
label: text

chunks.text: In  preparing  any  surface  to  be  coated,  all  loose  paint,  dirt,  grease,  rust,  scale,  weld  slag  or  spatter  or  any  other extraneous material shall be removed and defects repaired, so as to obtain a clean, dry, even surface to receive the priming or finishing coat (s) as called for in the painting schedules. Sharp edges should be rounded, especially when tank linings have to be applied. All machined surfaces, including flange faces, shall be suitably covered to prevent damage during surface preparation. All surfaces should be blast cleaned whenever possible. Surface preparation methods Bare  steel  surfaces  should  be  prepared  by  one  of  the  methods  described  below  in  order  of  preference  and  in accordance with Swedish Standard SIS 05 59 00 or Steel Structures Painting Council, SSPC, Vis 1, or DIN 55928, section 4.
label: text

chunks.text: Sa 3 Blast cleaning to bare metal mill scale, rust and foreign matter must be removed completely. Subsequently, the surface is cleaned with vacuum cleaner, clean dry compressed air or a clean brush. It must then have a uniform metallic colour and correspond in appearance to the prints designated Sa 3.

Sa 2 1/2. Very thorough blast cleaning. Mill scale, rust and foreign matter shall be removed to the extent that the only traces remaining are slight imperfections in the form of spots or stripes. Subsequently, the surface is cleaned with a vacuum cleaner, clean dry compressed air or a clean brush. It must then correspond in appearance to the prints designated Sa 2 1/2.
Mechanical cleaning should only be used when procedures (a) and (b) are not practicable.

Steel structures to be blast cleaned have to be free of pitting and other severely corroded places in accordance with B.S. 4232 and SIS 055900.
The abrasives used for blast-cleaning shall be graded flint, grit, shot or silica sand and shall be such that they will produce an average keying profile on the blast-cleaned surface of not more than 40 microns.
An air pressure of 7 bar (g) at the nozzle shall be used.

chunks.text:
After blast-cleaning, all accumulated grit, sand, dust, etc., must be removed leaving the surface clean, dry and free of mill scale, rust grease and other foreign matter.
In the event of rusting after completion of the surface preparation, the surface must be cleaned again in the manner specified.
Oil, grease, soil, cement, salts, acids or other corrosive chemicals shall be cleaned from steel surfaces, by the use of solvents, emulsions or cleaning compounds. The final wiping shall be with clean solvent and clean rags or brushes. There shall be no detrimental residue left on the surface.
Primed areas which suffer damage must be spot blasted on site to a degree of cleanliness P Sa 2 1/2 before touching up.
Protective coating must be applied as quickly as possible after the completion of surface preparation no matter what cleaning method has been used. No blast-cleaned surface shall be allowed to remain uncoated overnight. Wood surfaces shall be sanded clean. All nail holes shall be puttied and sanded before priming. Concrete: If a protective coating is required, concrete shall be allowed to cure before painting.
label: text

chunks.text: All containers shall remain un-opened until required for use. Primers and paints which have livered, gelled or otherwise deteriorated shall not be used. The oldest primer or paint of each kind shall be used first. All  ingredients  in  any  container  shall  be  thoroughly  mixed  before  use  and  shall  be  agitated  frequently  during application to keep the primer in suspension. Primer or paint mixed in the original container shall not be transferred until all settled pigment is incorporated into the body of liquid. Mixing in open containers shall be done in a well-ventilated area. Primer or paint shall be mixed in a manner ensuring the breakdown of all lumps, complete dispersion of pigment and uniform composition. Twocomponent primers shall be mixed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. Thinners  shall  not  be  added  to  primers  or  paints  unless  necessary  for  proper  application  according  to  the manufacturer's instructions. When use of thinners is permitted, it must be added to the primer or paint during mixing.
label: text

chunks.text: The supplier has to check all painting work to be carried out according to the specification of the paint supplier further to all relevant prescriptions and regulations concerning the health and safety of work. The paint supplier has to present a written specification including at least the flash point of the paints, ventilation requirements,  handling  precautions  such  as  inhalation,  eye  and  skin  protection,  and  first  aid  procedure,  storage requirements, spill or leak procedure, fire precaution, waste disposal.
label: text

chunks.text: Quality of the surface to be painted or coated has to be tested acc. to DIN 55928 and DIN 8202. Temporary corrosion protections are to be completely removed prior to applying the definite one, in accordance with DIN 55928. All prime coatings shall be applied by brush or airless spray or a combination of these methods, as approved by the coating manufacturer. All doors, windows, stairways, handrails (if painted), bolts, flanges and equipment supports shall be finish painted by brush. Spray guns should not be used outside in windy weather or near surfaces of a contrasting colour unless the latter is properly protected. All cold-spray painting shall be done using standard equipment in accordance with accepted standards and methods. Care has to be taken not to connect spraying devices for nitro and backelite paints simultaneously to oil based paints. Paint applied to items that are not be painted shall be removed at the supplier's expense, leaving the surface clean, unstained and undamaged.
label: text

chunks.text: To the maximum extent practicable the coats shall be applied as a continuous film of uniform thickness and free of pores. Overspray, skips, runs, sags and drips should be avoided. The different coats shall not be of the same colour.
label: text

Particular attention must be paid to full film thickness at edges.

The colour coding for identification of pipelines should comply with standard practice.
The type and number of protective coats for any item requiring painting are to be in accordance with DIN 55928 and are to be at least of a quality as shown in the attached tables 'Paint Systems'
Alternative  to  the  'paint  system'  specified,  are  to  be  presented  on  the  schedule  Departure  from  Specification,  as indicated elsewhere.
Generally, all parts shall receive the specified prime coat (s) at the supplier's works to ensure that no corrosion occurs during transport to the site and storage at the site.
Parts which cannot be damaged during transport shall receive the full number of coats.
label: text

chunks.text:
Galvanizing works shall conform in all respect to ASTM or B.S. 729, B.S. 3083 and
B.S.C.P. 2008 and to DIN 50976 whatever requires the higher quality and shall be performed by the hot dip process, unless otherwise specified.
It is essential that details of steel members and assemblies which are to be hot-dip galvanized should be designed in accordance with B.S 4479 or ASTM.
Vent-holes and drain-holes should be provided to avoid high internal pressures and air-locks during immersion, which may cause explosions, and to ensure that molten zinc is not retained in pockets during withdrawal.
Careful cleaning of welds is necessary before welded assemblies are dipped. The welds and the surrounding metal should be cleaned separately, preferably be blast-cleaning, because the usual preliminary pickling cannot be relied on to remove the welding slag.
All defects of the steel surface including cracks, surface laminations, laps and folds shall be removed in accordance with B.S. 4360. All drilling, cutting, welding, forming and final fabrication of unit members and assemblies shall be completed, where feasible, before the structures are galvanized. The surface of the steelwork to be galvanized shall be free from paint, oil, grease and similar contaminants in accordance with DIN 55928, part 4 and DIN 50976. The weight of zinc coating per unit area has to be noted in the manufacturing documents in accordance with DIN 50976.
The minimum average coating weight shall be as specified in Table 1 of B.S. 729 or Table 2, DIN 50976, whatever requires higher quality.
Structural steel items shall be initially grit-blasted to B.S. 4232, second quality, (Sa 21/2) or by pickling in a bath and the minimum average coating weight on steel sections 5 mm thick and over shall be 900 g/m2.
For Hot dipped galvanization work ASTM 123 can be followed if it complies with C4 corrosion protection for Very High durability for the outdoor ambient condition.
On removal from the galvanizing bath, the resultant coating shall be smooth, continuous, free from gross surface imperfections such as bare spots, lumps, blisters and inclusions of flux, ash or dross.
Galvanized contact surfaces to be joined by high-tensile friction-grip bolts shall be roughened before assembly so that the required slip factor (defined in B.S. 3294, part 1 and B.S. 4604, part 1) is achieved. Care shall be taken to ensure that the roughening is confined to the area of the mating faces.
label: text

chunks.text: Bolts, nuts and washers, including general grade high-tensile friction grip bolts (referred to in B.S. 3139, and B.S.4395 part 1) shall be hot dip galvanized and subsequently centrifuged (according to B.S. 729). Nuts shall be tapped up to
label: text

chunks.text:
0.4 mm oversize after galvanizing and the threads oiled to permit the nuts to be finger-turned on the bolt for the full depth of the nut. No lubricant, applied to the projecting threads of galvanized high-tensile friction-grip bolt after the bolt has been inserted through the steelwork, must be allowed to come into contact with the mating faces of the steelwork. A local remelting of the galvanized parts to achieve the nuts to be finger turned on the bolt is possible in accordance with DIN 50976.
Protected slings must be used for offloading and erection. Galvanized work which are to be stored at the works or on site shall be stacked so as to provide adequate ventilation to all surfaces to avoid wet storage staining (white rust).
Small areas of the galvanized coating damaged in any way shall be restored in accordance with DIN 55928, part A and DIN 50976 by:
- Cleaning the area of any weld slag rust and other impurities and by thorough wire brushing to give a metallic clean surface.
- application of suitable number of coats of zinc-rich paint containing more than 90 % w/w of zinc in dried film. The dry film thickness shall exceed at least 50 % the thickness of the desired galvanization. In case of application of a low melting point zinc alloy repair rod, the rods shall be in accordance with DIN1707, the thickness of the alloy shall be at least as of the desired galvanization.
The restored area shall not exceed 1 % of the galvanized surface.
Surface restoration of parts in contact with drinking water is not allowed and the quality of the galvanization is to be in accordance with DIN 2444.
After fixing, bolt heads, washers and nuts shall receive two coats of zinc- rich paint. Connections between galvanized surfaces and copper, copper alloy or aluminum surfaces shall be protected by suitable preferably hydrophobe tape wrappings to the Owner's approval.

chunks.text:
Corrosion protection may also be achieved by spraying of suitable metals as zinc and/or aluminum on the surfaces of structures. For special cases tin, copper, lead can be used as well. Methods of surface preparation have to conform to B.S. 2569 or to DIN 8567. A proper treatment of the surface followed by an immediate spraying is to apply to ensure adhesion of the sprayed metal. The surface has to be clean, free of impurities, rust, mill scale and rough enough to have binding properties to ensure good enticulation with the sprayed layer. Suitable roughness can be achieved by blast cleaning according to BS 4232 or DIN 8567. Welds are to be cleaned and prepared with special care. All surfaces to be treated have to be dry and accessible.
Application  of  coatings,  requirements  for  thickness,  adhesion,  composition  of  coating  metals,  and  subsequent treatment have to conform to BS 2569 DIN 8565 and 8567 or as per OEM manufacturing specification.
Testing of the spray coated layer are to be carried out in accordance with DIN 8565.
The EPC Contractor has to specify the type, composition and thickness of the sprayed metal and of the sealing coating according to DIN 8565 including the corresponding warranties and tests if sprayed metal coating will be applied.
label: text

chunks.text:
All precautions connected with this type of application of corrosion protection have to be in accordance with German regulation DVS 2307, page 1.2.
Sprayed, unfused coating of metals and metallic compounds applied by combustion gas flame, plasma arc, detonation and similar processes, and the preparation of components, spraying techniques, sealing, finishing and inspection shall be according to B.S. 4761.
The hot galvanized surface has to be cleaned before the application of the coats to remove corrosion products, dirt, dust, grease.
The cleaning can be achieved by
- brush off
- washing with 1 - 1.5 % ammonia water with up to 0.1 % detergent added and followed by wet grinding using e.g. scotch brite to turn the foam to grey colour,
- steam blasting,

chunks.text:
All  outdoor  onshore  steel work  shall  be  painted  (except  for  Switchyard,  which  requires  HDG)  with  C4 corrosion protection for very high durability up to the PPA term from IAT. Cladding shall be galvanized and painted. Indoor steelwork shall be painted as per corrosion protection class mentioned above. Surfaces to be  painted  include  exposed  surfaces  for  the  internal  parts  of  all  building  structures  and  the  exposed surfaces of all indoor equipment, piping, valves, and hangers, unless excluded hereinafter. The following lists include the major surfaces of indoor materials (Unless noted otherwise) and equipment to be painted. Surfaces of materials and minor equipment not listed but requiring painting for protection shall also be painted.
- Breeching not insulated and lagged
- Concrete masonry units (interior and exterior)
- Concrete bare wall, floors, sidewalks, curbs, and paving including in chemical storage and water treatment areas
- Miscellaneous supports for tray, bus duct, conduit, lighting, electric unit heaters, etc
- Field erected tanks (interior and exterior)
- Reservoirs
- Air receivers
- Shop fabricated tanks (if not insulated)
- Turbine generator
- Interior structural steel
- Galvanized Metal wall panels and flashings
label: text

chunks.text:
The colours of the primer, intermediate and finishing coats of a paint system shall be easily distinguishable from each  other  and  the  materials  used  shall  be  suitable  for  the  method  of  application  employed  and preferably be supplied by one manufacturer who shall ensure that all coatings are compatible.
Using the Contractor's proposal as a basis, the final colours and identification systems for the equipment, piping etc. shall be in accordance with accepted practice and with the agreement of the Owner and off taker.
Where materials are subject to an elevated risk of corrosion (e.g. due to stagnant water or presence of crevices) additional protection shall be applied e.g. by coating or cathodic protection.
label: text

chunks.text:
Where dissimilar metals are in contact or close proximity and corrosion may occur through electrolytic action or differences in electrical potential, protection shall be afforded by electroplating, suitable gaskets, cathodic protection or other means.
Chromium plated parts shall not be used in any damp or corrosive atmosphere.
All surfaces shall be adequately protected in transit, and any damage shall be renovated immediately on off-loading and on completion of erection.
After cleaning and inspection but before the plant leaves the Contractor's works, the machined surfaces of steel  and  ironwork  shall  be  covered  and  protected  with  a  preserving  fluid  according  to  the  related applicable standards otherwise to the Owner's approval.
All external steel screw fixings shall be supplied in the hot dipped spun galvanized condition, stainless steel, or sherardized to comply with BS 4921, Class 1 or Class 2 or equivalent with passivation treatment. The EPC Contractor shall provide with his bid the civil design criteria he intends to follow, in which details regarding his proposed methods of corrosion protection for reinforced concrete and steel structures are given and procedures described.
All splash zones and concrete surface in contact with aggressive atmosphere shall be painted with epoxy coating.
label: text

chunks.text:
All plant shall run without undue vibration and with the least practicable amount of noise.
Noise levels from the Plant shall not exceed the limits identified in section 4.1.9.5 of the OTS Part A.
label: text

chunks.text:
Insulation  of  the  Plant  shall  generally  be  in  accordance  with  the  Contractor's  standard  procedure. Notwithstanding this, the provisions described below shall apply to the Contractor's design.
All exposed portions of the Plant which are subject to a temperature exceeding 60°C and are likely to come into direct contact with operational and maintenance and other personnel shall be provided with approved thermal insulation so that the temperature on the outside of the insulation does not exceed 60°C when the ambient temperature is 35°C.
All heat insulation materials shall be chemically inert and shall remain so in the event of being saturated with water. The Contractor shall ensure that insulation materials shall be prevented from any possible formation of Hexavalent Chromium contamination for all types of turbines, generators and other balance of  plant  equipment/pipeline. All materials shall be asbestos free.  Thermal insulation  of pipe work and equipment  shall  comply  with  the  relevant  recommendations  of  BS  5970  and  BS  5422.  All  insulation material shall be in accordance with BS 3958 or equal Standard as applicable with regard to definition, physical characteristics and tests. OEM's standard codes shall be allowed.
All insulation adjacent to hot surfaces shall be capable of withstanding the maximum surface temperature obtainable  in  service  without  deterioration  or  breakdown  of  the  material.  The  maximum  permissible temperature, which the insulation will withstand in continuous service, shall be stated.
Thermostatic steam traps shall be insulated in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.
The type, thickness and heat loss of insulation, reinforcing and protection shall be subject to approval and shall be stated.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
The design code for the metallic piping shall be ASME B31.1 Power piping standard. Boiler piping shall be in accordance with ASME Section I - Boiler Code.
The EPC Contractor shall provide a piping specification for each piping system which shall describe the following:
- Service description
- Pipework material
- Design pressure and temperature
- Operating pressure and temperature
- Pipe wall thicknesses including corrosion allowance
- Materials
- Pipe connection arrangements
- Flange ratings and material groups
- Principal valve types and materials
- Hydrostatic test pressure
The corrosion allowance to be considered for piping shall be as follows:
- Carbon steel: 1.5 mm
- Alloy steel:  1 mm (0 mm can be allowed as long as design life criteria can be met)
- Stainless steel: 0 mm
- Plastic: 0 mm
The piping  thicknesses  shall  be  sufficient  to  withstand  the  design  pressure  at  the  design  temperature during the plant's life cycle.
The minimum thicknesses to be used in the process piping shall be the following:
- Carbon steel piping
- o DN ≤ 6' Schedule STD
- o DN  8' Schedule 20
- Alloy steel piping
- o DN ≤ 2' Schedule 80
- o DN  2½' Schedule STD
- Stainless steel piping Schedule 10S
Piping design of the main fluid systems shall be developed assuming velocity of fluids determined by the EPC Contractor taking into account pressure drop of the fluid in the lines, possible erosion, water hammer effects, noise emission and any other possible effects.
Piping shall be designed within the following flow velocities, unless otherwise agreed with the Owner.
Superheated steam, Maximum Velocity = < 65 m/s. Saturated steam, Maximum Velocity = < 45 m/s. Bypass Line Upstream & Downstream of Bypass Valve, Maximum Velocity = < 100 m/s. Feedwater, Maximum Velocity = Suction < 2.5 m/s Discharge < 4 m/s (Normal Operation) Discharge < 6 m/s (transient operating condition, such as bypass, start- up/shutdown)
Condensate Water (normal operation), Maximum Velocity = Suction < 2 m/s Discharge < 4 m/s. Circulating water, Maximum Velocity = 2 to 3 m/s. General service water, Maximum Velocity = Suction < 2 m/s Discharge < 3.6 m/s. Natural gas, Maximum Velocity = < 30 m/s. Compressed air and other gases, Maximum Velocity = 10 to 25 m/s
Piping systems larger than DN50 shall be stress analysed as required and the scope of analysis shall meet the requirements of ASME B31.1.

chunks.text:
In Gas turbine package, the piping, piping support, piping hangers, valves, fittings, welding of pipe works and etc. of the proposed generator and its auxiliaries will be in accordance with JIS(Japanese Industrial Standards) or manufacturer's standard. The stress analysis is not necessary and will not be conducted for the piping of the generator and its auxiliaries.
All pipe systems shall be arranged, installed, supported and provided with all necessary means of venting, draining  and  expansion  subject  to  the  approval  of  the  Owner  in  accordance  with  the  Contract  before erection commences. The space between pipes shall be sufficient to allow easy repair and/or replacement of insulation or repaint.
The pipework layout shall be designed so that items of equipment and sections of pipework can be removed from  the  pipelines  without  major  disturbance  to  the  adjacent  pipework,  additionally  piping  shall  be arranged so that full access is provided for the operation and maintenance of equipment, and that removal or replacement of equipment can be achieved with the minimum dismantling of piping.  Particular care shall be taken to ensure that pipework thrusts are not transmitted to machinery or associated apparatus.
Dead legs shall be avoided but where this is not possible provision shall be made for flushing the pipework. Changes in pipe bore sizes shall be by the use of proprietary fittings or fabricated sections to avoid sudden changes.
All  nuts,  bolts,  washers,  flanges,  gaskets,  flanged  tied  adaptors,  drain  valves,  special  connection  pieces, supporting hangers, brackets or clips and temporary supports for the pipework, together with all terminal point connection materials shall be supplied and installed.
All  flanged  joints  shall  be  fitted  with  suitable  insertion  ring  gaskets  which  shall  be  carefully  adjusted concentric to the bore of the pipe so that no undue strain is placed on any of the bolts or flanges of the pipe when bolting up.
The Contractor shall be responsible to issue a bolting torque procedure in accordance with the applicable Standards and on the case of equipment's, fulfilling also the recommendations of the suppliers.
When the conditions of the system exceed P≥40 bar or T≥425ºC, two drainage and vent valves shall be included. Additionally, drains in steam lines will be provided with double isolation valve if design pressure >22barg, whatever the temperature.
All the saturated steam pipes shall have a 1% slope when cold and 0.5% slope when hot for draining.
All drains or vents shall be routed to a collection point.
All steam pipe work shall be carefully designed to ensure that it is fully drainable. Drain and vent valves shall be supplied as necessary.
For steam lines, drain design shall consider the guidelines included in ASME TDP-1 Standard providing recommended practices for the prevention of water damage to steam turbines used in Electric Power Generation.
label: text

chunks.text: The steam pipe work shall be carefully designed with regard to anchor points and expansion provisions to ensure  that  any  thrust  transmitted  to  the  turbine  inlet  flanges  is  kept  to  a  minimum.    Adequate  pipe supports and anchors shall be supplied for all piping.
label: text

chunks.text:
The piping specification provided by Contractor will define the selected material as well as the applicable standards and identification code for the different system services.
The materials used for the manufacture of the metal piping must be in accordance with the ASME or ASTM standards.
The material of all  the  elements  (pumps,  valves,  strainers,  etc.)  shall  be  suitable  for  connecting  to  the corresponding piping system to which they belong.
As a general rule pipe and valve sizes 1/4', 1 -1/4', 3 -1/2', 5', 7' and 22' will not be used.
Steel flanges shall be in accordance with ASME B16.5 for DN≤ 24', and ASME B16.47 Series A or AWWA C207 for DN> 24'.
Bolts, nuts, washers for flange joints shall be hot dip galvanized as applicable, except for bolts/nuts to be used in high temperature (bichromated).
The gaskets of flange joints will be suitable for each fluid and design requirements.
Pipes and fittings shall be joined by welding in accordance with the following criteria:
DN> 2': Butt weld (BW)
Hydraulic pipework shall be of stainless steel, tubing high pressure grade ASTM A213-TP316L.
label: text

chunks.text:
The design, fabrication and testing of the valves shall be in accordance with the  applicable Codes and Standards (ASME B16.34, API 6D, etc.) The class of the valves shall be compatible with the design service requirements.
The EPC Contractor shall provide a valve specification (data book or valve class) for the valves which shall describe the following:
- Valve characteristics
- Design and operation conditions
- Construction data
- Materials
- Actuator
- Other requirements
The  Valve  List  shall  include  the  detailed  identification  (KKS,  P&ID,  line,  system,  fluid, type,  ND, rating/schedule, ends, etc.), design data, insulation and heat tracing data, painting data (system and colour), critical valve, manufacturer, and origin of the valve.
Valves, valve drives and accessories, which are of a similar make, size and type, shall be standardized as much as possible in order to facilitate interchangeability and maintenance and limit the stock of spare parts.
All valve bodies shall be of the same nominal size as the adjacent piping, unless otherwise required. The internal diameter of valve ends adjacent to the pipework shall be the same as the internal diameter of the connecting pipe (full bore type).
Valves  shall  be  designed  for  long  life  tightness  and  smooth  non-sticking  operation  at  all  operating conditions. They shall be wear resistant as possible, reliable and approved in practice.
Valves shall be installed maintainable from the outside (field repairable).
After disassembly of actuator (regardless of manual or motor actuator), valve position must be readily identifiable.
For all globe and check valves, the direction of flow shall be clearly stamped on the body of the valve.
For butterfly valves, preferred direction of flow shall be stamped on the body of the valve.
Gate valves shall not be used in flow regulation and throttling service.
In vacuum service and wherever otherwise necessary to prevent the entry of air, valves shall be provided with packings appropriate for vacuum service (without external sealing water).
Each equipment item will be provided with isolation valves.
Instrument isolation valves shall be ball or globe valves.
Welded valves of size 21/2' and above shall be provided with butt welding ends prepared as per ASME B16.25 and welded valves 2' or below shall have socket welded ends as per ASME B16.11.
Control valve sizing shall be made in accordance with ANSI/ISA S75.01 standard and the control valve Contractor's sizing computer program. The Contractor shall be responsible for the proper sizing, selection, and application of all control valves, control valve components including trim or plug design, actuators, valve materials, valve accessories, and other such factors directly under the control of the Contractor.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
Proper control valve selection shall ensure that the required energy can be dissipated without exceeding the maximum vibration levels in the piping system and without exceeding the wear properties of the trim material.  Contractor shall select control valve trim design that facilitates maximum reduction of control valve induced vibration and trim wear.
The opening percentages (referred to 100% full stroke) shall be between:
- a) Minimum flow >10%
- b) Normal Flow 30-60% for linear curves. 30-75% for iso-percentages.
- c) Maximum flow <75% for linear curves. <85% for iso-percentages
When the valve is also used for isolation purposes, class V (ANSI/FCI 70-2) in general and Class VI for "Tight shut off" (TSO) application shall be provided.
Except for turbine control valves, each critical and/or high pressure control valve station shall be provided with bypass valves and motorized valves on feedwater and steam lines.
All regularly operated isolation valves and control valves shall be accessible from a permanent floor or access platform.
Safety and relief valves design shall be in accordance with the applicable standards: API RP 520 Parts I and II, API 521 and ISO 4126. Valves shall be grouped together and an access platform provided.
For Gas turbine package, GT OEM standardized equipment, and the control valves with accessories are not general service ones but dedicated ones. Hence, the control valves with accessories will follow GT OEM's standard.
In Gas turbine package, the valves are designed according to GT OEM standard for following systems.
- -Generator Cooling Water System
- -Generator Seal Oil System
- -Generator H2 & CO2 Gas System
- -Generator H2 & CO2 Gas Supply System

chunks.text:
Welders employed on any work under the EPC Contract, either at works or on site, shall be proved to be competent to carry out the type and standard of welding required prior to commencing work. All welders shall  be  qualified  in  accordance  with  the  governing  design  code  or,  where  no  appropriate  standard  is thereby  indicated,  with  Section  IX,  "Welding  and  Brazing  Qualifications  of  the  American  Society  of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code" or approved equivalent.
In Gas turbine package, the piping, piping support, piping hangers, valves, fittings, welding of pipe works and etc. of the proposed generator and its auxiliaries will be in accordance with JIS(Japanese Industrial Standards) or manufacturer's standard, provided that reference standards are equivalent to International standard such as ISO for welding procedure qualification and NDT requirement.
In the case of pressure parts and pressure part attachment welds, each approved welder shall have a unique identification number which shall be indicated on all welds made by him and on all permanent test records applicable to those welds including radiographs.
All welders engaged on either shop or site welding shall be under the supervision of a competent welding engineer who shall demonstrate, to the Owner's approval according to the related applicable standards, a complete system for the control and treatment of consumables, deployment of welders, use of approved procedures, heat treatment, non-destructive testing, including spectrographic material checks on weld and parent metals, repairs and general quality control. Also, the welding Engineer shall monitor all the qualified welders at site or manufacturing shop for their performance, repair rate, re-training and re-qualification in consent with Owner.
label: text

chunks.text:
Sample welds shall be carried out on specimens of similar shape, thickness and chemical analysis to the material to be welded, and in a position which shall represent as far as possible the worst conditions under which actual welding shall take place, as laid down by the approved Standard/Code. The welders shall be considered approved to weld after the positive result of the radiographs of the sample welds.
The method of preparation of the test pieces and the standards to be used in examination of them shall be according to the agreed Standard or Codes, or as may be agreed with the Owner. All expenses of every kind in connection with welder's tests shall be borne by the Contractor.
label: text

chunks.text:
All welding procedures including those proposed in repair situations shall be qualified as required by the governing design code or, where no appropriate standard is thereby indicated, by Section IX of the ASME Code or approved equivalent and all qualified procedures shall be submitted to the Owner for approval prior to the commencement of any welding. This applies in full for boiler, water steam cycle and all BOP piping, where the required welding procedures shall be submitted as "For Information". For rest of the plant equipment, the requirement shall be dealt on case-to-case basis.
Gas turbine interconnecting piping will be shop welded according to ASME B31.1 and all relating nondestructive testing will be performed according ASME B31.1. Test documentation related to these welds shall be submitted to Owner.
label: text

chunks.text:
Where necessary, the work shall be heated prior to welding in an approved manner, and the temperature maintained  throughout  the  operation.  The  metal  temperature  shall  be  checked  by  means  of  suitable thermocouples or temperature indicating crayons.
For  9  Cr  material  welds,  the  use  of  thermocouples  is  mandatory  and  the  preheating  process  must  be recorded in all the welds. The use of torches for the Preheating of material grade 2 1/4 Cr and 9Cr is it not allowed.
label: text

chunks.text:
Regardless  of  the  requirements  of  the  specific  code  or  specifications  applicable  to  the  design  and/or construction of the plant and associated pipework, it is a mandatory requirement of this specification that all welds shall be subject to appropriate post weld treatment with the following exceptions:
- Austenitic stainless steels
- Plain carbon steels containing less than 0.25 per cent carbon at thicknesses up to and including 30 mm
- Low  alloy  steels  containing  ½  per  cent  molybdenum  and  1¼  per  cent  chromium,  ½  per  cent molybdenum up to and including thicknesses of 12.5 mm provided that:
- o A hardness traverse across the weld zone gives no single result greater than 240 HV10
- o No fillet weld leg is greater than 8 mm
- o A minimum preheat of 200°C is used for welding
Plain carbon steels shall contain no more than 0.25% carbon.
All post weld heat treatments of materials and components for use at temperatures in excess of 400°C shall be so designed as to guarantee maximum creep properties in the parent materials and weldments.
The soaking times at the selected heat treatment temperatures shall be:
- Low alloy steels not containing vanadium, 5 minutes per mm of thickness with a minimum time of 120 minutes
- Low  alloy  steels  containing  vanadium  and  high  (11  to  15  per  cent)  chromium  steels  containing vanadium, 180 minutes regardless of thickness
In the event that any post weld heat treatment is carried out at a temperature in excess of the original tempering temperature of the parent materials, a re-assessment of the design strength limit stresses for the materials will be required. This may, in the absence of acceptable mechanical test data for the specific condition, require re-determination of the relevant mechanical properties of the materials.
The requirements for post weld heat treatment do not affect or replace in any way the requirements for maintenance of welding preheats or post welding heating for the purposes of diffusing hydrogen from the weldment.
The PWHT (post weld heat treatment holding temperatures), time and heating and cooling rates must fulfil the requirements of the applicable Part of the ASME Code depending of the type of component. Before the start of any PWHT the charts must be signed by the Owner or his Representative

The extent of weld inspection, the final weld quality, and the method of examination shall be as stated in this  OTS  or  the  agreed  Standards  or  Codes.  The  Contractor  shall  maintain,  both  at  works  and  on  site, adequately indexed records of all welding, weld inspection and repairs, which shall be available to the Owner, together with facilities for viewing of X-ray photographs.
The  views  taken  by  X-ray  shall  be  to  a  procedure  and  resolution  agreed  with  the  Owner  and  shall incorporate the appropriate image quality indicator. In case that the Inspection and Manufacturing Code allows  the  use  of  two  diferent  NDT  methodologies  the  Owner  reserves  the  right  to  choose  the  most appropriate one in his understanding.
However, for the Butt welds of thickness of 60 mm and above shall be tested either by X-Ray or by Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing (PAUT) methos instead of Gamma rays due to its limitation. If PAUT method is selected, demonstartion block as same as welding & material being tested is necessary in additional to code required standard calibration blocks.
After the appliance of the PWHT on the Gr92, Gr91, Gr22 and Gr11 an hardness test must be performed as follows:
- 100 % on Base Metals, Weld and Heat Affected Zones( 3 identations in each area)
The maximum and minimum acceptable values for each material must be agreed with the Owner before the start of the works,
On the 9Cr materials, the NDT Inspections must be performed after 48h after the conclusion of the PWHT
Adequate safe storage facilities and appropriate safety regulations shall be provided for gamma-ray units, if used.

chunks.text:
Where repairs on major items of plant are found to be necessary by welding, dimensioned sketches of the excavated areas shall be prepared and the proposed repair procedure submitted to the Owner before any repair is commenced. Under no circumstances shall the repair be commenced until the agreement of the Owner has been obtained. The areas shall be subjected to a suitable non-destructive test and on completion of the weld will again be non- destructively tested. In the event that the repair requires all or any part of the item to be stress-relieved, the non-destructive tests shall be repeated on any part deemed to have been affected by the stress relief. The welds repairs are allowed just on the cases that is accepted able by the Manufacturing Code. Supplier shall document all the major and minor welding repairs areas carried out on all the weldable castings applicable for turbine casings, valves, equipment's if any, and these documents including the post repair weld stress relieving chart and NDT records shall be a part of the manufacturing quality dossier. The major welding repair shall be carried out only with Owner approval.
In the case of weld cracking, the Owner may require a full investigation to be made of the cause of the cracking prior to any approval of repair procedures. The cost of all such investigations and reports is to be wholly borne by the Contractor.
Weld repair of cast iron parts is not permitted under any circumstances.

All rotating parts of the machinery shall be statically and dynamically balanced as per the relevant design and testing code unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Owner.
In  Gas  turbine  package, generator rotor is balanced by  the most effective method being considered its characteristic. Since generator rotor runs through several critical speeds up to the rated speed, generator rotor is an elastic rotor not a rigid rotor. In such case, the high speed balancing (i.e. dynamic balance) is most effective. Therefore, statically balance is not applicable.

General  arrangement  drawings  will  be  provided  clearly identifying the outline of all major plant equipment, their weights and associated floor loading capacity and lay down location.

Plant requiring regular routine maintenance that does not have direct or mobile crane access shall be provided with monorail and hoists for items that may not be reasonably manipulated by a single average person. Monorail or forklift access shall be provided for moving heavy equipment and for equipment that requires regular dismantling for maintenance and repair. The Steam Turbine building shall have overhead cranes with main and auxiliary hooks sized to enable removal of the heaviest item for maintenance. Special devices, slings, runway beams, trolleys and other lifting tackle necessary for the maintenance of the plant shall be provided by the Contractor.
The marking and test specification of Safe Working Load values on lifting equipment shall be in SI units.
Mobile  plant  such  as  fork-lift  trucks,  cranes,  sewage  tankers  etc.  required  for  the  operation  and maintenance of the Plant shall be provided by the Owner to a recommended list to be provided by the Contractor.
