Level measuring devices may be of the direct measurement, differential pressure or electrical/electronic type as appropriate to the application.
Reflex-glass or magnetic level gauges will be used. Gauge glasses used in conjunction with level instruments will,  as  a  minimum, cover a range in excess of that required for alarms and trips. Level gauges will be selected so that the normal vessel level is approximately at gauge centre, where practical.
Level indication for corrosive service will use devices other than reflex-glass gauges. Level gauges for high pressure service will have suitable personnel protection.
Each measuring instrument shall be capable of being removed without the vessel or other instruments being taken out of service.
Differential pressure transmitting devices shall preferably be used on all services other than slurry.
Displacement type instruments and switches shall be mounted in external cages with flanged connections, rating same as the vessel. This type of instrument shall not be used for applications involving viscous, corrosive or flashing liquids.
Direct measurement of level by means of internally mounted floats, etc, shall only be used when the switch point is either well defined in advance or is adjustable in service, and the vessel can be emptied and/or depressurised for the removal of the switch without effect to the normal operation of the Plant, or where choking of extended connections is likely to occur.
Float switches shall be glandless with magnetic coupling.
In Gas turbine package, guided wave radar type and displacement type level transmitters will also be used as per Supplier's standard design.
label: text

chunks.text:
Low pressure gauges may employ manometer or barometer devices to indicate small gauge, differential pressures or vacuums.
Sensing element materials shall be selected to resist corrosion by the process medium.
When gauges or transmitters are to be used for duties where the process medium temperature exceeds 70°C, siphon loops shall be utilised. (Siphon loops will not be utilized in gas turbines, gas turbine generators and their associated auxiliaries. Instead, impulse piping for pressure gauge or transmitters is considered in the GT package.)
Gauges measuring low ranges that can be exceeded by a higher containment pressure shall be fitted with over-range protection. Gauges shall be fitted with vent/test valves. Blow out devices shall be provided for high-pressure applications.
Pressure switches shall be such that under normal process operating conditions, the contact in the switch shall be closed unless otherwise approved by the Owner in accordance with the Contract. Switches shall have adjustable set points and adjustable hysteresis, as required. (In Gas turbine package, hysteresis of pressure switches will depend on manufacturer's standard specification.)
label: text

chunks.text:
The method of temperature measurement to be employed shall be selected for the particular application bearing in mind requirements for accuracy and reliability.
Sensing elements for air, inert gas and radiant temperature measurements shall be complete with suitable protective sheath. For steam, water and hazardous applications, Thermowells shall be utilised.
label: text

chunks.text:
For Turbine/Generator set OEM standard and general industrial practice are acceptable.
Resistance temperature detectors (RTD's) shall be to IEC 60 751 Grade II, resistance of 100 Ω at 0°C, using 3-wire connections and applications up to 600°C. On differential temperature measurements RTD's to IEC 60751 Grade I will be used. RTD's shall be used only where they can be readily replaced without loss of Plant capability.
Where thermocouples are employed then cold junction compensation shall be provided.
Where an external junction box is provided it shall be located in a position so as not to be in excess of 50°C or a lower temperature commensurate with the insulation material of the compensating leads.
In the case of direct immersion metal couples of the mineral insulated type, the couple up to the associated junction box shall be capable of easy replacement. A flexing coil having a minimum diameter of 250 mm shall be provided in the couple between the junction box and the carrier.
Where thermocouple assemblies are supplied, a disconnection head shall be arranged clear of the pocket and  associated  lagging  and  shall  be  sufficiently  long  as  to  prevent  excessive  temperature  of  the  head assembly.
Local temperature indicators shall be supplied with a thermowell and shall preferably be of the bimetallic type and of the multi-angle variety.
No temperature measuring system shall use mercury as its sensing medium.
In  general,  temperature  instruments  will  have  scales  with  temperature  units  in  degrees  Celsius.  Dial thermometers will have 100 mm or larger dials and white faces with black scale markings and will be everyangle type and bimetal actuated. Dial thermometers will generally be visible 3 m from an operator's normal stance at floor level, platform, or stairs (viewing area) and will be resistant to plant atmospheres.
Temperature elements and dial thermometers will be protected by thermowells except when measuring gas or air temperatures at atmospheric pressure and for Steam Turbine/Generator set OEM standard and general industrial  practice  are  acceptable.  Temperature  test  points  will  have  thermowells  and  caps  or plugs.
RTDs will be either 100 ohm platinum or 10 ohm copper, ungrounded, three-wire circuits (R100/R0 = 1.385). The element will be spring loaded, mounted in a thermowell, and connected to a cast iron head assembly.

Position  measuring  devices  employing  magnetic,  proximity,  electrical  (e.g.  potentiometers  and  limit switches) or optical principles may be utilised as appropriate to the application.
Mounting locations shall, wherever possible, be remote from sources of heating or leakage of process, gases or liquids. Where vibration-free locations are not possible, the mounting arrangement shall incorporate flexibility in the coupling between the device and the point of measurement and the transducer mountings.
For position instruments in high temperature applications such as steam valves, etc, the calibration of position  transducers  and  the  setting  of  limit  switches  shall  be  unaffected  by  the  hot/cold  operating temperatures of start-up and shutdown.
label: text

chunks.text:
Analytical instruments monitoring chemical or physical properties of process fluids and substances may be installed either directly in the process line or vessel or at a distance and connected by means of sampling systems.
Analytical  instruments  shall  be  selected  to  operate  continuously,  infrequently  or  on  a  continuously interrupted cycle as most suited to the measurement and the intended application.
Sensors shall be of ruggedized construction and shall not require frequent maintenance or recalibration. Where sensors require the use of calibration solutions or gases then a minimum of one year's supply at normal  usage  shall  be  supplied.  Where  sensors  require  replacement  or  removal  for  recalibration  or rejuvenation at regular intervals, then an adequate number of spare sensors shall be supplied for one year's normal usage.
Self-cleaning pH and conductivity probes are preferred.
label: text

chunks.text:
Vibration monitors will be provided on all major high-speed rotating equipment greater than 500 kW, such as steam turbines and boiler feed pumps.
As a minimum, the following functions shall be provided:
- a) Bearing  pedestal  vibration  measured  by  seismic  mass  type  velocity  transducers  or piezoelectric accelerometer, if required by the Owner.
- b) Axial displacement of thrust collars of Steam Turbine monitored by means of a non-contact proximity probe. If it is not feasible to measure axial displacement of the Steam Turbine, other means of high-speed protection in the event of axial displacement occurring shall be provided.
- c) A phase marker facility and associated non-contact proximity probe.
- d) Relative shaft vibrations shall be measured by two non-contact proximity probes fitted into each journal housing 90° apart.
- e) High vibration alarm and trip facilities.
- f) Display vibration levels on DCS in CCR.
For Gas turbine package, the vibration monitoring system (vibration probes in x-y direction and monitoring rack)  of  GT  relative  shaft  vibration,  GEN  relative  shaft  vibration,  GT  absolute  vibration,  GEN  absolute vibration and pinion shaft vibration sensors (in x-y direction, 4-20 mA directory connected to GT control
system) of GT Enhanced Cooling Air Compressor are provided. Vibration monitoring system will not be provided for any other rotating equipment in the Gas turbine package.
GT absolute vibration measurements will be used not for trip and alarm functions but for monitoring only. Axial position and shaft eccentricity measurements will not be provided for gas turbine and gas turbine generator as per GT OEM standard design.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
A fully integrated, DCS shall be provided to monitor, control, display, alarm and record selected physical and electrical parameters associated with all plant areas.
The Plant (each Unit) shall be operated, monitored and controlled from a Control Room (CR).
- The minimum requirements of the Plant's DCS shall be, but not limited to:
- Allow for automatic control of all the systems of the Plant from the CR,
- Ability to collect signals and alarms from all the necessary systems.
- Critical  signals  shall  have  a  minimum  level  of  redundancy  to  guarantee  reliability  and availability of the Plant in any circumstance.
- Provision of a remote monitoring system and software with supervisory role and access to historic values.
- This shall include 2 web based monitoring for Offtake connection along with any license required.
- Remote access shall be allowed for maintenance and backup purpose.
The system shall be designed to have a functionally and geographically distributed architecture utilising a number of independent outstations. The equipment located in the DCS cubicles shall include all necessary control processors, input/output (I/O) cards, power supplies, data highway interfaces and termination facilities.
The microprocessor-based distributed control system shall comprise of multifunctional modules operating over a network. The operators have access to all significant process information and all controls Analogue and Digital signal will have separate cables. Analogue cables are twisted pair and screen protected.
Outstations shall be capable of autonomous operation and perform data acquisition, calculation, digital (open loop) and analogue (closed-loop) control functions.
Operator's workstations shall allow monitoring, control and adjustment of Plant operation conditions via highresolution 'windows' style graphics displays. All VDUs, keyboards, printers and peripheral devices and their associated control desks shall be supplied.
One 72' large screen graphics wall monitor for the plant shall be provided in the CCR which will primarily be used for:
- I. Display of important data and graphics from the DCS, video, etc.;
- II. To provide real time clear luminous information to operators and visitors;
- III. The whole screen of the large screen graphics wall should behave as a single logical screen and the control of the same shall be from a dedicated graphical control unit having a keyboard and mouse. However, as an option it should be possible to control the Graphics Wall from a PC on LAN having Windows NT/2000 OS;
The complete system shall be interfaced on 10/100 MBPS LAN as a minimum. Provision for additional VDU shall be provided for future additions. The man machine interface shall be to the review and approval of the Owner in accordance with the Contract. The display screens shall be developed in conjunction with the Owner and shall be to the review and approval of the Owner in accordance with the Contract.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
Communications between the outstations located in different plant areas and the Operator's and Engineer's workstations located in the CCR shall be performed over a redundant high-speed serial data highway. The
data highway shall be designed to perform at the speed necessary to ensure that all variables are updated and control commands are issued without loss of system performance. The data highway shall include all control equipment, error detection and correction facilities and cabling.
The redundant data highway will have different routing.
The DCS shall be designed to ensure maximum availability by the inclusion of built-in redundancy for both hardware and software. This shall include duplicated control processors, data highway and power supplies with automatic changeover to the standby unit upon detection of a fault or failure of the operating unit. Where appropriate, I/O cards shall also be duplicated. The failure of any single element shall not affect the operation of any item of operating plant. In particular, the duplicated control processors shall be capable of  fail  over  without  change  to  Plant  status,  sequence  status  or  control  actions,  at  any  stage  of  Plant operation.
Comprehensive  system  diagnostic facilities shall be incorporated to assist in  maintenance  and troubleshooting. These shall include memory, control processors, I/O cards, data highway, storage devices, as a minimum.
The DCS shall have a master clock of GPS satellite controlled clock for time synchronisation with package computer systems. To allow the DCS equipment to be synchronised irrespective of the time shifting in summer.
The Contractor  shall  ensure  that  DCS  system  is  provided  with  sufficient  storage  capability  to  perform manual and automatic back-ups.
label: text

chunks.text:
The response times for the Operator's workstations under normal conditions shall be as follows:
The DCS, as finally configured and installed, shall exhibit response times which do not adversely impact the operation of plant equipment nor impede the operator's response to events. To this end the maximum response times defined within this specification shall not be exceeded.
- a) Control  response  time  is  defined  as  the  elapsed  time  between  the  moment  a  signal  change  is originated at the input card of a processing unit until a controller action takes place in another processing  station,  assuming  the  worst  communication  situation  possible,  including  maximum data highway traffic level, longest cable length and largest access time to the data highway. This time shall not exceed the following values:
- i. Slow Loops 1000 millisecond (such as temperatures and large tank levels)
- ii. Fast Loops 500 millisecond (such as most flows and some pressures)
- iii. Discrete/Logic Control 500 millisecond (motor control/interlocks)
- b) Monitoring function response time is defined as the time between initiation of an action or event and the time at which the operator is advised of the event through a LCD display or a printer output. These times include the elements of the control response times, including consideration of worst case communications, as well as the additional delays associated with operator station equipment such  as  LCD  buffers,  display  drivers,  and  memory  access.  These  times  shall  not  exceed  the following values:
- i. Operator  Commands  to  Equipment  1000  millisecond  (exclusive  of  external equipment reaction times)
- ii. Alarms/Annunciation  1000  millisecond  (including  pre-processing  for  alarm suppression)
- c) The time between selection and display of a VDU, fully updated, from the database shall not exceed 2 seconds with a typical workstation loading of 4 graphic displays, 2 trends and 1 alarm display in 'windows' on the VDU.
- d) The time between the occurrence and change of a signal at the origin and the change of state, value or alarm showing on the VDU shall not exceed 2 seconds.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text: The DCS shall be supplied with all hardware, system and applications software (VDU displays, alarms, etc) fully developed, tested, debugged and installed for all analogue and digital I/Os. An overall 10 percent spare capacity shall be provided to all necessary hardware including I/O units and associated wiring, supplied and tested.
label: text

chunks.text:
The latest  version  of  the  manufacture's  system  software  shall  be  provided  fully  developed,  tested  and installed.
The application software and associated displays, reports, databases, etc. shall be pre-formatted when installed at Site. The creation or modification of displays, reports, databases or control strategies shall be possible  with  the  system  online  by  the  Owner's  engineering  personnel  without  affecting  the  Plant operation. Modifications to the software shall be done in straightforward and logical steps using, wherever possible, graphic displays. It shall not be necessary to have specialist knowledge of the underlying software in order to carry out modifications.
All necessary software licences shall be included. This shall lead to unrestricted use of all specified software packages by the Owner. Access to software and application programmes at various levels shall be possible by operating or engineering personnel using passwords. This shall protect the software from unauthorised access.
label: text

chunks.text:
The operator interface software shall enable the Operator to carry out the necessary actions in a safe and efficient manner. In particular the following features shall be included, as a minimum, but not be limited to:
- a. Software shall be structured in such a way so as to provide a hierarchy of control from automatic sequential Plant start-up through to manual control of an individual item.
- b. During  manual  intervention  by  the  Operator  (sequence  initiation  and  individual  device control under normal and failure conditions), all software derived, hardwired permissive and overrides shall be visible to the Operator.
- c. Where process measurements have been duplicated into the DCS for improved reliability, the signals shall be averaged for control purposes and quality monitoring shall be employed to  automatically switch to the good signal in the event of an interruption. The Operator should have, for the purposes of maintenance, the on screen facility to select either signal or the average, as the measured variable for control.
A philosophy shall be developed to define the action of the sequence logic in the event of a step failure, Operator intervention or the initiation of a sequence with not all Plant conditions satisfied. It  shall  be possible to bypass a required plant condition but this section shall be alarmed and logged and only valid for one attempt for that step. This philosophy of operation shall be to the Owner's approval in accordance with the Contract.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text: The DCS shall be capable of presenting to the Operator, pre-defined reports. The information on the reports may be either in tabular form or in a pre-formatted report form and may be automatic at specific times or on request. Reports shall include periodic logs, daily logs and group logs, balance of energy and efficiency log. In addition, reports shall be produced to meet the requirements of the Environment Agency, and all report formats shall be to the approval of the Owner in accordance with the Contract.
label: text

chunks.text:
All plant and system generated alarms shall be prioritised, logged and displayed by the DCS. There shall be a  dedicated  alarm  display  which  shall  show  all  the  Plant  alarms  or  groups  of  alarms. The  Operator's workstations shall have a visual and audible warning which will raise the attention of the Operator upon the receipt of any alarm. Alarms shall also be printed on the alarm/event printer for DCS, ST and GT.
The Operator shall have the facility to select different alarm displays, summary of alarms, historical alarms on global or point based, unacknowledged alarms, alarms by priority, alarms by pre-defined system groups.
There shall be a facility to suppress an alarm or groups of alarms as a result of a particular alarm or other Plant condition in order to minimise the number of alarms under transient conditions.
All alarms generated from analogue I/O shall be configured with a dead band of approximately one percent (1%).  This  shall  be  an  adjustable  value,  which  forms  part  of  the  configuration  software.  All  alarms generated from digital I/O shall have the facility to be supported with an adjustable time based dead band, which will defer the reset by the allocated time. This value of time shall form part of the configuration software.
Plant level Alarm System shall be engineered /designed to minimise number of alarms in the plant level to meet the latest revision of ANSI standards (Number of alarms for Operator) - ISA-18.2 or IEC 62682.
Alarm management shall be based on Alarm EEMUA 191 guidelines.
label: text

chunks.text:
The DCS shall include a mass storage memory device to provide storage of operating data for the plant. Data storage shall be non-volatile. Hard disks and optical disk drives are the preferred media for mass storage of data.
A magnetic tape drive, magnetic cartridges, optical laser disk type device shall be provided for permanent long term storage of data. The system shall automatically dump accumulated data to tape or cartridge when the storage media nears capacity, or at user defined intervals, whichever occurs first. The system shall generate an alarm if the drive is not in the ready condition to receive data. Sufficient time shall be provided to allow operator intervention before loss of data.
It  shall be possible to retrieve data from the hard disk or permanent storage media from any operator station to display time based trends of stored data. The hard disk mass storage media shall have a capacity of 2 Gigabyte or of a larger storage capacity as required by the system design.
In addition to process data, the system shall record manipulations to the database to include, but not be limited to:
- a. Adding/removing points from scan
- b. Adding/removing points from alarm
- c. Changing alarm limits
- d. Algorithm tuning changes
- e. Force/clear of digital point status
- f. Processing unit/operator station configuration change
- g. Force of analog signal value
Each operator station shall be capable of retrieving and trending stored data. Operator-adjustable time frames of 10 minutes (with 1 second resolution) to 24 hours shall be provided as a minimum.
As a minimum, the system shall be capable of archiving data from all system points.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
The DCS shall incorporate long term data logging facilities for all analogue, digital,  serial  data,  alarms, condition  monitoring  and  other  internally  generated  points  including  the  overall  extension  capacity specified. All signals shall either be scanned periodically or reported by exception, and updated values or digital status changes shall be stored. Data shall be stored for up to 3 months on a suitable storage medium. An alarm shall be given to the Operator when the storage medium approaches its maximum capacity. All data shall be automatically archived and retained for future reference in either optical or magnetic medium.
The operator shall have the facility to present real time data, recall data held in the data logger memory or from  archives  over  a  specified  period  of  time.  The  requested  information  may  be  presented  on  the Operator's  workstations  either  in  tabular  form  or  as  selected  variables  on  a  trend  display. It  shall  be
possible to compare on the same display, multiple trends of real-time data or historical data from the data logger or archives.
The format and content of the reports for data retrieval from the logging facility shall be subject to approval in accordance with the Contract.
label: text

chunks.text:
A sequence of events (SOE) recording system shall be supplied to allow analysis of the causes of trips or Plant disturbances. The SOE recorder may be either integrated within the DCS (preferred method) or a stand-alone item of equipment. The SOE recorder shall scan all designated binary inputs continuously with a resolution of 1 millisecond.
The  status  of  each  point  shall  be  time  tagged  and  stored  in  a  database  together  with  other  relevant information  for  a  specific  time  period.  Data  will  be  continuously  deleted  from  the  database  after  the specified time period has elapsed. Facilities shall be provided for data to be archived for future reference.
On the occurrence of a nominated event (e.g. Steam Turbine, generator or pumps trip) or manual initiation from the DCS, all data for the time period before the event shall be retained and continue to be recorded for a period after the event.
The SOE recorder shall automatically reset after the elapsed time period and continue to monitor the Plant in the normal way.
SOE reports shall be generated and printed using the stored data and shall be used for post trip review and analysis. The report shall be presented in a clear and logical format.
label: text

chunks.text: All  operator control command functions (both modulating and discrete) shall include a tag-out feature which permits the control  function  to  be  placed  into  a  secured  mode  (e.g.  stopped,  off,  minimum  and output)  with  normal  operator  commands  inhibited.  Software  logic  shall  inhibit  any  device  from  being placed in the tag-out condition until operator action has placed the field device in the safe and secured mode (e.g. motor stopped and valve closed). Any function placed in the tag-out mode shall be identified as such on all displays of the function or controlled equipment. Operator action shall be required to set or remove the device from the tag-out state. Means shall be provided for logging and printing tagged-out mode points and functions. This tag-out function should be a standard feature of the DCS not requiring additional memory or engineering to implement.
label: text

chunks.text:
An  emergency  shutdown  system  shall  be  provided  to  automatically  shut  down  discrete  equipment,  a system, or the Plant, in a safe and controlled manner, in the event of abnormal operating conditions which could cause permanent damage to the plant endangering human safety or exceed operating limits to the detriment of Plant life.
The Contractor shall be responsible for the co-ordination and provision of an integrated tripping system, which  will  monitor,  initiate  and  interface  with  other  systems  which,  will  initiate  the  protection requirements of the Plant.
The  Contractor  shall  develop  in  conjunction  with  all  his  sub-suppliers  a  Plant  inter  trips  philosophy document/drawing, which will be used to control and implement the protection requirements of the Plant.
Emergency push button and programmed logic shutdown system shall be provided for the safety shutdown of the plant. The Emergency Push Button in the main control room and at locally shall be hardwired to control  system  (directly  to  the  output  card)  for  the  plant  critical  process  /equipment.  Meanwhile programmed logic trip system could also be applicable as per manufacturer standard control system.
The system offered shall have a successful record of proven usage in the same or similar duty. Each field input shall be separately protected against possible faults or induced voltage pickup and line monitoring shall be provided. A simple arrangement for each I/O to indicate the presence or absence of I/O shall be provided, and thus allow problems to be quickly identified.
The design of the protection system shall be failsafe that is to fail to the condition, which would normally protect the Plant.
label: text

chunks.text:
All critical inputs which, if present will cause loss of Plant performance, shall be engineered and included, but not be limited to, the following:
- Devices leading to Steam Turbine shutdown.
- Facilities  shall  be  provided  to  allow  routine  testing  of  trip  systems  without  causing  Plant shutdown, by inhibiting the trip systems, while tests are being carried out. The inhibits should be designed in such a way as to provide restricted use and application of such inhibits shall be alarmed to the Operator.
The  emergency  shutdown  system  providing  automatic  trips  shall  be  sufficiently  reliable  or  contain sufficient redundancy to produce the required level of security.
It shall be possible to initiate from the workstations in the CCR, the shutdown of complete Plant. These features shall be provided by hardwiring from the control area, direct to the emergency shutdown systems.
The emergency shutdown system shall be operational at all times, irrespective of the equipment/package control mode.
Remote and local start-up trip override and trip reset facilities shall be provided to assist in commissioning and the auto sequence control of the Plant by the DCS. The shutdown system either in part or as a whole shall be capable of event analysis either by discrete data logging or transfer of information to the DCS.
Where 2 out of 3 trip logic has been incorporated, then 1 out of 3 discrepancy alarms will be generated for the attention of the operator, via the DCS. All trip initiations from the emergency shutdown systems will be alarmed to the DCS for event logging.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text: As optional, (in case of awarding this scope should be treated as optional), the Contractor shall offer an online performance monitoring package commercially available in the market for monitoring net output of the plant exported to the grid with correction applied as required under the Power Purchase Agreement for  site  ambient  conditions  and  the  net  plant  heat  rate  without  applying  any  corrections  as  well  as monitoring output and heat rate applying the corrections agreed in the Contract and applicable PTCs. The package shall provide instantaneous and historical trends of corrected output, auxiliary loads, and heat rate and efficiency  of  each  generator  and  shall  have  diagnostic  features  for  investigating  the  causes  of  any performance degradation, benchmarking against performance as of new conditions, and finding solution for that. The package shall use the historical data from the DCS for long term trending.
label: text

chunks.text:
Integrated services digital  network (ISDN) type PABX, approved for connection to the public switched telephone network (PSTN) and situated within the Plant Administration Building shall be provided.
The installed capacity shall be 16-exchange lines, 16-tie lines and 50-extension lines. A personal computer (PC) based telecommunication console shall be provided together with a VDU, keyboard and headset.
The Contractor shall provide necessary equipment for VHF/UHF/microwave wireless connection between the nearest public telephone exchange and install tower on the site for connecting of the PABX with the public telephone network system (this connection could also be provided by means of optical fibre). The wireless/OF equipment shall be fully compatible with the KSA Telephone Exchange system. The Contractor shall be responsible for taking approval from KSA Telephone Exchange for such connection and the PABX and making payment of all fees and charges for installation of the system.
All other internal telephone connections within the Plant boundary, including cabling to and within the administration, control and turbine area, etc, shall be the responsibility of the Contractor.
label: text

chunks.text:
The following basic facilities shall be included in the PABX design:
- i. Extension to extension calls shall be made by direct dialling.
- ii. Extension to exchange lines for outgoing calls shall be made by dialling a single access digit.
- iii. Operator access from extension by dialling a single digit is required.
- iv. Trunk barring on outgoing calls shall be provided as required on selected extensions.
- v. Provision  for  limited  barring  on  outgoing  calls  from  selected  extensions  shall  be provided.
- vi. Incoming calls from the public exchange shall normally be routed to the operator. However, the exchange shall be suitable for direct dialling-in. The ringing period for such calls shall be limited to 30 seconds after which the calls shall be diverted to the operator.
- vii. Operators recall from an extension engaged with an incoming or outgoing call shall effected by operation of a recall button followed by dialling the operator access digit.
- viii. Call transfer between extensions on incoming and outgoing exchange calls shall be provided.
- ix. Operator  intrusion  into  an  established  call-in  order  to  offer  an  exchange  call  or message shall be provided. An intrusion tone shall be introduced.
- x. Night service facilities shall be provided by extension of exchange lines to selected extensions.
- xi. PABX alarms shall be displayed on the telecommunication console.
- xii. It  is  desirable  that  a  limited  number  of  extensions  (not  exceeding  6  in  the  first instance) shall have a priority facility to intrude into extension to extension calls. An intrusion tone shall be introduced.
- xiii. Telephone handsets shall be provided with the facility for 'hands free' operation, and these shall be suitable for desk and wall mounting.
- xiv. Industrial type wall mounted telephone handsets shall be provided. These handsets shall  be  of  rugged  design  for  use  within  a  Plant  and  equipped  with  a  large  visual indicator  suitable  for  mounting  separate  from  the  handset,  for  use  in  noisy environments.
- xv. Acoustic hoods shall be provided.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text: The direct ring telephones on the leased lines shall enable the CCR to call the National Grid Control Centre. When the telephone handset in either the CCR or the Grid Control Centre is lifted the telephone in the other location shall ring.
label: text

chunks.text:
The system shall have the following functions, as a minimum, but not limited to:
- a. Automatic calling upon lifting handset at 'calling' end.
- b. Operation by the PABX battery supplies.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
The power plant will be provided with an emergency warning system in conformity with the international standard and shall include necessary siren and emergency warning lights. This system will be activated in the control room of the power plant in case of emergency and will warn by a sound transmitted to all the power plant components through the above paging system together with sparkling alarm lamps in the noisy areas.
The emergency warning system will be supplied with an UPS, battery and standby power supply in case of interruption of the main power supply.
label: text

chunks.text:
The following electrical power supplies should be made available for the C&I equipment:
- A. 480 V or 400 V ac (3 phases + neutral).
- B. 277 V or 230 V ac (1 phase + neutral + protective earth).
- C. 227 V or 230 V ac (1 phase uninterruptible power supply).
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
In general, the power supplies available in electrical installations can be subjected to voltage and frequency variations, harmonic distortions, interruptions, and transient voltage peaks. Equipment shall be designed and proved by test, to the following unless otherwise specified.
Short  time  duration  peak  voltages  can  occur  on  both  ac  and  dc  supplies,  typically  due  to  switching operations, and are unpredictable in magnitude. For example, on AC systems, the peak may be up to 5 times the rated rms voltage, and on dc systems, the peak to rated ratio may be even higher. Sensitive equipment shall therefore be protected against such transients at its supply terminals.
Equipment shall ride through interruptions up to 100 milliseconds duration. (GT control system can ride through interruptions up to 40 milliseconds duration, since redundant power supply is provided)
label: text

chunks.text: Connections to the external power sources shall normally be made via switches and fuses or via miniature circuit breakers.
label: text

chunks.text:
All circuits intended to be electrically isolated from external circuits shall be designed to withstand the following voltage levels:
All circuits requiring isolation (including contacts of switches, relays or contactors) shall have an insulation resistance across the isolating barrier of not less than 20 mega ohms when measured at 500 V dc.
A circuit intended for connection to 110 V ac or 125 V dc and above shall withstand 2 kV 50 Hz rms between itself and all other points for one minute.
label: text

chunks.text:
All control and instrumentation equipment shall comply with the requirements specified in IEC 61000-4 series of standards for electromagnetic interference and immunity.
Equipment proposed shall not generate electrical or electromagnetic interference at a level detrimental to the performance of the equipment itself, other equipment or to the hazard or discomfort of personnel.
Equipment proposed shall not be susceptible to the effects of radio frequency interference which could emanate typically from a 1watt ERP mobile radio telephone operating at VHF or UHF at a distance of 1 metre from the equipment.
label: text

chunks.text:
All non-current carrying metallic parts of plant, equipment, components, enclosures, protective screens, etc, shall be provided with earthing facilities for personnel safety reasons and for obtaining the maximum possible rejection of electrical interference.
Earthing should be generally designed and installed in accordance with IEC, IEEE 80 unless otherwise approved.
Protective screens around insulated cables shall be insulated from field instruments, connected through any field junction boxes, and be continuous up to the earthing point in the destination cubicle or panel.
Cable armouring shall not be used as a protective screen. Earthing of cable armour shall be arranged for electrical safety purposes and not for noise reduction. Cable armouring shall be insulated from any cable protective screening.
Where the Contractor's design requires a separate and dedicated earthing arrangement for example, a 'clean' earth for electronic equipment then the Contractor shall provide such earthing facilities as required. All instrument clean earth bars shall be clearly labelled as such.
Earth bars inside cabinets of GT control system will not have any label. Cables connected to the earth bars will have a wire marker label such as PE (Protective Earth), FE (Functional Earth).
Where the system design requires a single connection from the C&I equipment to the main Plant earth bus, then a removable link shall be provided to connect the equipment earth to the main Plant earth bus for testing purposes. This removable link shall be clearly labelled with a warning indication.
Where a cubicle, frame or enclosure is earthed via the above facilities then it should be insulated from structural steel works or any other plant earth.
label: text

chunks.text:
In  addition  to  the  manufacturer's  production  tests,  the  Contractor  shall  carry  out  routine  tests  on completed equipment.  The Owner reserves the right to witness such tests.
Routine tests on each piece of equipment shall include at least the following:
- a) Visual inspection.
- b) Performance test.
- c) Control loop testing
- d) Voltage withstands test and insulation test.
Where a number of items of equipment are intended to operate together, the complete assembly shall be tested to demonstrate that the interconnected items are compatible.  Design consideration should be given to the testing requirements of the Plant as defined in the OTS.
The Site acceptance tests shall include, but not be limited, to the following:
- e) All outstations are tested without connection to workstations in the CCR.
- f) Data communications to workstations are established for each outstation.
- g) Commissioning tests including, in-situ instrument calibration check to DCS control loops, DCS device drivers, protection and interlock logic, sequences, station master load control, alarms, and all other equipment supplied (s), firmware(s), equipment(s), firewall(s), switch(s), etc. installed within the network.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
Each item of equipment shall be durably and legibly labelled as required by the Owner, indicating the purpose, plant identification number and where necessary any operating position functions.
The  material  of  all  labels  and  the  dimensions,  legend  and  method  of  printing  shall  be  to  approval  in accordance with the Contract. Surfaces of labels for cubicles and control equipment shall have a matt or satin finish to avoid dazzle. Colours shall be permanent and free from fading. Danger labels shall have red lettering on a white background.
Labels shall be provided on front and rear access doors of all cubicles. Labels shall also be provided inside cubicles to assist the identification of apparatus and terminals.
All  actuated valves shall be provided with labels, which shall include the valve and actuator reference number.
label: text

chunks.text:
Fuses shall be of the high breaking capacity cartridge type of approved manufacture and shall comply with IEC 60269.
Fuses, link carriers and  bases shall be of approved manufacture and shall be of good quality moulded insulating material. Control circuit fuse carriers and bases shall be black and for links they shall be white.
The arrangement of the fuses and the design shall be such that fuses, when operating, will not cause an arc to form between phases or to earth. Fuses and links shall be grouped and spaced according to their function
in order to facilitate identification. Fuse carriers shall be capable of taking any size of fuse, up to the marked full rating of the carriers.
All incoming circuits in which the voltage exceeds 110 volts shall be fed through insulated fuses and/or links, the supplies being connected to the bottom terminal, which shall be shrouded. The contacts of the fixed portion of the fuses and links shall be shrouded so that accidental contact with live metal cannot be made when the moving portion is withdrawn.
Isolating links shall be provided on each panel to facilitate isolation of the dc circuit (where used) to permit testing or other work on individual equipment on the panel without danger to other circuits, and such links shall be provided with labels, indicating their function and polarity.
Distribution  of  220VDC  power  and  power  feeds  to  power  units  (24VDC  output)  inside  cabinets  of  GT control system can be isolated by circuit protector.

chunks.text:
Manual operations may be used to prepare the plant when cold, but, having completed these, only a single operation shall be required to start major sections of plant. At appropriate points (e.g. synchronisation, etc.) the sequences shall pause and ask the operator for permission to proceed.
The plant shall be equipped with an Automatic Generation Control (AGC) system through which the each generation unit can be remotely controlled from the Load Despatch Centre (LDC). In principle, the AGC system will enable the output of each generating unit on the system to be controlled directly from the LDC (either automatically or manually) to match the system demand. The AGC logic shall be designed to prevent the  application  of  inappropriate  or  undeliverable  remote  demands  and  to  ensure  that  remote  control signals are consistent with the technical and commercial provisions of the Offtaker.
label: text

chunks.text:
The Gas receiving and treatment shall be in accordance with the OTS.
EPC shall design & supply the metering facilities at the existing Gas Connection Facility, and hand over the same to the Owner. After handing over, the Gas Delivery Point at the downstream of the Seller's Metering Facility will be the operational interface point between the Seller and the Owner during the operational period.
The gas system is a potential single failure point so special attention must be given to meeting the criteria of  OTS.  Every  effort  shall  be  made  to  maximise  reliability  and  safety.  Common  reduction/compressor stations (if applicable) shall meet the requirements of OTS under all circumstances. Main and Back-Up Metering Equipment for gas shall be provided by the Contractor. Instruments for Gas metering shall have an accuracy of 0.5% or better and as per Client approved Standards and Specifications.
An on-line calorimeter and spectrometer shall be provided and shall also be interfaced to both the DCMS and flow computers.
label: text

chunks.text:
Governors and AVRs shall meet the requirements of OTS. They shall be proprietary items and interfaced to the DCS so the supervisory functions are available via the DCS MMI. A separate MMI may be supplied for intimate plant level control for commissioning/fault finding/repair/special monitoring purposes if these are not available through the DCS. If over-speed protection is fully two (2) out of three (3), fully fail-safe and  self-checking,  the  same  transducers  may  be  used  for  speed  control  and  over-speed  protection. Otherwise, separate equipment is required.
It shall be possible to start the gas turbine by a single operation in the CCR and steam turbine and its control system shall be suitable for all modes and conditions of operation.
The governors shall be capable of withstanding full load rejection without tripping, operation in island mode, at fixed power, and for the gas turbines, frequency support (droop) mode and in accordance with the requirements of OTS.
The HRSG stacks and bypass stacks shall be equipped to online monitoring system and record NOx, SO2, CO and O2 emissions. At any time either one or the stack -either HRSG stack or bypass stack will be in service while Gas Turbine in operation.
label: text

chunks.text:
Control will be by the DCS automation outstations, with additional protection. Less critical protection, such as maintenance of desuperheater spray water, can be vested in the DCS outstation, however it shall not be possible to override this protection in normal operation (e.g. by not permitting manual operation of a valve under certain circumstances).
The Burner Management System (BMS) in case supplementary firing is provided, shall be proven, be fully failsafe and meet the requirements of OTS. The International Standard used for BMS and boiler controls shall  be  stated.  The  BMS  shall  be  separate  from  all  other  outstations  (in  accordance  with  NFPA  8502, Section 4-3.2.3.1.)
Turbine  and  superheater  water  ingress  protection  shall  meet  or  exceed  ANSI/ASMI  standard  TDP-1 Recommended Practices for the Prevention of Water Damage to Steam Turbines used for Electric Power Generation.
The steam and feedwater systems shall be fully automatic in normal operation and automatic sequences shall be provided for all start-up and shut-down operations (eg. BMS sequences, floating together steam systems etc.). The sequences shall pause for operator permissive where required, but emergency actions (such as dump condenser, bypasses etc.) shall operate immediately.
label: text

chunks.text:
The HV and MV electrical systems shall be monitored and controlled by the DCS. For operator actions, the interlocks provided by the electrical system shall be exactly duplicated in the DCS so the operator knows of any missing permissive.
The DCS shall also monitor the DC and UPS systems.
Generator parameters such as vibration, temperature, coolant flows etc. shall be monitored but protection is provided by the generator protection system. Transformers shall be similarly monitored.
An active generator capability diagram shall be provided.
The fault monitoring system shall be interfaced with the DCS with a view to collection of post-incident data for archiving purposes (see earlier).
Time stamping shall be coordinated with the DCS. It is not intended that relay settings can be changed thorough the DCS.
Currents of all MV motors shall be monitored and running hours shall be recorded. Currents and running hours of other motors shall be monitored and recorded where necessary.
The DCS shall be interfaced to Generator and Transformer AVRs to provide manual raise/lower facilities (see earlier).
Automatic synchronisation can be initiated by the DCS (generally after release by an operator).
All metering shall be connected to the settlement system and also totalised by the DCS.
label: text

The main requirements are stated elsewhere in this OTS Part B.
The fire detection system shall cover the entire new Plant and gas detection shall cover all necessary areas within the new Plant. An interface with the DCS shall be provided for information and protection of the operators. The system shall interface with the other fire detection systems, if any, to inform the control room operators of fire elsewhere on the site. The master panel shall be mounted in the control room with repeat indication in the Gate House. Repeat panels shall also be provided at the entrance of other buildings where information is required for protection and/or safety.

The system will include and an OPC server for access from external networks to the Control System, with consideration of cyber security. OPC server shall include all parameters and signals provided from DCS/ SCADA system.
The plant control systems are critical for plant safety and operation. If degraded or sabotaged they put people, environment and assets at risk. The requirements for security are therefore high.
To  ensure  availability,  confidentiality  and  integrity,  at  least  the  following  points  shall  be  taken into account:
- Be designed with security measures, segregation and availability to reflect the plant requirements;
- Have  measures  to  protect  itself  from  unauthorized  access  from  external  systems including the corporate office data network;
- Have measures that enable secure remote operation according to process requirements;
- Have measures for disaster recovery;
- Operate safely also if communication to external systems fails; and
- Be  documented  and  maintained  in  a  manner  that  reflects  the  requirements  of  the connected systems.
The measures  shall be based on international standards such as ISO 27001, IEC  62443  and NERC 1300.
For more detail refer to Schedule C Network Security to this OTS.
All  external  communication  and  data  links  shall  have  all  necessary  protections  in  order  to  achieve  a maximum level of cyber security. The system shall be designed with security measures, segregation and availability to reflect plant requirements and have measures for disaster recovery. The measures shall be based on international standards like ISO 27001, IEC 62443
and ISA S99.
A CCTV system shall be supplied to cover the entire Plant including stacks, GT&ST turbines, control room entrance, etc.
Anti-virus & Malware Protection: The Contractor shall provide the most recent versions of anti-virus and malware  protection  software  at  the  end  of  warranty  period  or  Defect  Liability  Period  (DLP).  It  is recommended that antivirus software should be in line with ACWA Power ICS guidelines.

Such requirements are to be implemented by the Contractor in the phases described below in this section. Each phase can be completed consecutively or concurrently.

chunks.text:
The  Contractor  shall  propose  and  submit  to  the  Owner  for  approval  the  network  architecture  for  the binding of 4 quadrant subnetwork(s) comprising of SCADA/DCS, metering, historian, LDC, remove support connectivity in Quadrant 4, iPAS, PI or Plant performance monitoring system, Offtaker and business users connectivity in Quadrant 3, O&M IT network in Quadrant 2 and Project Company IT network in Quadrant 1.
Prior to submission, the Contractor will have discussed with the Owner, all of the necessary equipment (e.g. firewalls, AV, Endpoint protections, P2P connections etc.) that are needed in order to ensure the overall Plant architecture is cyber security compliant.
label: text

chunks.text:
The Contractor shall implement a data diode device between Quadrant 4 and Quadrant 3. The data diode device shall enforce unidirectional data transfer from the source to the destination.
The  Contractor  shall  use  the  OPDS-100  data  diode  device  (including  the  relevant  support  service(s)) produced by OWL Technologies (as set out below) and shall coordinate with the Owner who shall provide further details in this respect.
label: text

chunks.text:
The Contractor shall propose a disaster recovery plan for the complete network for approval by the Owner.
In addition, the Contractor shall ensure unitary testing along with end-to-end testing is in place before handover to the O&M Contractor.
The Contractor shall furnish the Owner with the relevant testing schedules and logs on a regular basis.
label: text

chunks.text:
The Contractor shall implement a continuous monitoring and protection service for the monitoring of the Plant network.
The Contractor shall use FireEye, Inc. services and hardware to implement the monitoring and protection service and shall coordinate with the Owner who shall provide further details in this respect.
label: text

chunks.text:
The Contractor shall arrange for a third-party audit of the cyber security measures to ensure compliance with the specifications set out in each of phases 1-4 above (subject to that, Each Phase must pass such audit before handover to the O&M Contractor).
The Contractor shall use THALES Holding Maroc SAS to perform the audit and shall coordinate with the Owner who shall provide further details in this respect.
Any non-conformances identified by the auditor shall be notified to the Contractor. The Contractor shall have 30 days (unless the parties agree otherwise) to implement such comments and make the necessary changes to the cyber security measures at the Plant. The audit process shall be repeated in respect of the relevant Phase(s) until the auditor declares a satisfactory result is achieved. All costs related to additional audits shall be borne by the Contractor.
label: text

chunks.text:
The cyber security measures implemented at the Plant shall at all times comply with:
- i. local laws, ordinances, regulatory requirements, codes and standards of Saudi Arabia (if any);
- ii. Schedule C; ACWA -Requirements -001 ICS Network Security -v2.0 policy document & Document Technologies Unification.
- iii. Essential Cybersecurity Controls -ECC-1: 2018 requirements developed by Kingdom of Saudi Arabian Cybersecurity Authorities for KSA Project or any specific requirement of Country where the Project is located.
- iv. provisions of the Project agreements (including the Power Purchase Agreement); and
- v. Requirements set out in phases 1-4 above.
Any inconsistency or conflict between the provisions shall be resolved with priority being given as follows: (i), (iii), (ii) and (iv).

The common Plant system shall be DCS-based, with incorporated display hierarchy and display selection concept as follows:
•, 1 = Power Block Overview level,. • Functional area, 1 = Area level control,. • Mechanical units, 1 = Group/Unit level control.. • Components, 1 = Item level control
Item level control may be by means of pop-ups.
Operator communication and monitoring shall be carried out via monitors providing the window(s) to the process.
The display layout of an operator station shall be as follows:
- A frame with header and footer is always visible. It contains selection fields for displays and additional information as well as collective displays, which shall also indicate faults in displays not currently visible,
- Basis diagrams occupy the rest of the screen. They provide information on the process in the form of plant diagrams, curves, characteristics, etc.
- Windows  are  selected  in  addition  to  the  basic  diagrams.  Normally  the  window  is  allocated  to  a particular object, e.g. pumps, and provides detailed additional information in graphic or alphanumeric representation.
- The control room operator shall be presented with displays for information and control functions, which are especially designated for monitoring, intervention and clarification at the process, plant or control  system  level.  The  displays  shall  present  process  sequences  and  statuses  in  a  functionally related manner. This shall be achieved by means of three types of displays with different information content, such as:
- o Plant displays which show the physical items in the plant such as pumps, fans, valves, etc. and their  state  by  the  means  of  the  symbol,  colour,  blinking,  (in  acc.  to  DIN  2481)  to  facilitate operator intervention,
- o Representations of physical and technical relationships in form of curves, characteristics, bar graphs,  digital  displays,  to  provide  a  view  the  process.  They  provide  the  operator  with historical, current and forecast states of process.
- o Control system displays showing function diagrams for instrumentation and control as well as device configuration diagrams.
- o Step-bystep indication of sequences' progress and permissive awaited.
The above shall be available whether a DCMS vendor's outstation or packaged plant vendor's PLC provides control.
These different types shall mutually supplement each other and can be called up by the plant personnel in accordance with their access authority. Mixed displays shall be possible.

chunks.text:
The DCMS shall incorporate an alarm system with the main tasks of providing a comprehensive and clearly arranged representation of faults in the power plant, facilitating quick localisation of the plant sections affected by faults.
There shall be a Common Alarm Display facilitating blinking marks in diagrams, menus and the overview single lines permanently displayed. Signal disturbances from the complete plant, regardless of the current display and operator control situation, shall b e indicated at the operator's workstation.
It shall be possible to identify every measurement in alarm whether displayed in a table or on a mimic, and the  state  of  its  acknowledgement.  (e.g.  by  blinking  or  different  colours.).  Sequence  time-outs  shall  be treated  as  alarms.  The  event  sequence  display  additionally  shall  list  events,  which  do  not  need  to  be acknowledged, if this cannot be accommodated by the 'sorting' process.
For alarms at the operator stations limited consequential alarm suppression shall be provided but not on printed alarm logs (see below). The extent of suppression shall be agreed in engineering phase. In addition to display on the screen, audible signalling of faults shall also be possible.
The Alarm Sequence Display / Event Sequence Display shall be facilitated by listings in tabular form of currently pending, non-acknowledged alarms / faults in chronological order and in plain text. Even if ASD has not been selected, the alarms shall be stored in the background and new incoming alarms shall be indicated in the overview line. It shall be possible to designate one monitor exclusively for ASD operation, however, additionally it shall be possible call up the ASD immediately on any other monitor.
The event sequence display additionally shall list the event alarms, which do not need to be acknowledged. The Contractor shall supply a separate alarm list with initiation points and all corresponding operator actions.
The alarm sequence display shall be stated according to:
- Alarm class; and
- Functional area.
All the non-acknowledged alarms are written into new pages whereas all alarms acknowledged, but still pending, shall be shifted to the old pages and marked with blinking display. Additionally, it shall be possible to print out all alarms (alarm log).
In addition to display on the screen audible signalling of faults shall also be possible.
Alarm management shall be based on Alarm EEMUA 191 guidelines.

chunks.text:
A log shall be the filtered output of data from the short- and long-term archives supplemented by titles and explanations.
The following logs shall be available:
- OM-configurable logs (to be freely programmable);
- Status logs;
- Sequence logs;
- ES-configurable logs.
Logs of this nature shall be available as status logs, sequence logs and incident review logs.
Online logs are 'open' sequence logs, which are continuously routed to a printer starting at the time of their activation and shall show:
- Trends (with history)
- Characteristic curves (X-Y plots).
- All alarm/event logs
The print of the above shall be visible as soon as it is printed.
All signal changes occurring within recent hours shall be archived in the short-term process data archive located in the processing units, where a replica of the process signals shall be maintained.

The firefighting systems and equipment shall be designed in accordance with the NFPA recommendations and with any additional requirements of local authorities and shall comply with the local regulations in respect of supplier, installer and system approval.
The local regulation and standards shall have the highest priority in case any conflict with the international standards i.e. NFPA etc.
The firefighting system shall also cover the fire protection system and the fire and gas detection system and shall be one unified system of the same make and type for the entire plants. Approval shall be received also from authorized insurance company.
For fire protection and detection purposes the overall Plant site shall be divided into separate fire zones and the alarms and control requirements for each zone shall be actioned through a local control and alarm panel, including alarm signal to the central alarm panel of the fire brigade. All penetrations between two different fire zones shall be sealed with fireproof sealing material of listed type. Warning, Safety, Exit, No Smoking Signs shall be provided. The labels shall be weatherproof and UV resistance.
An automatic fire detection and alarm system shall be provided, with detection devices and with manual control switches selected to suit particular risks, and with a control system designed to provide operating and fire brigade staff with sufficient information to identify and respond to any fire detected.
The firefighting water system shall be designed as continuously pressurized ring system to serve outdoor hydrants at strategic locations and to supply water to indoor hydrants, hose reels, sprinkler and spray water systems and shall be equipped with sectionalizing valves so that a failure in any part of the system can be isolated while allowing the remainder of the system to function properly.
Generally, it shall be considered that the following firefighting installations shall be foreseen:
- Oil tanks, lube oil tanks of turbines, Gas generators, other related facilities: Foam/water spray systems;
- Oil filled transformers: Automatic fixed spray water systems;
- cable  tunnels,  cable  floors:  Automatic  sprinkler  systems;  Cable  room  shall  be  provided  with  fire detection and suppression system as per NFPA 850, Cl:7.8.2.1, The Cable spreading rooms and Cable tunnels should be protected with automatic sprinkler, water spray, water mist or automatic gaseous extinguishing system
- Ventilation systems: Portable extinguisher
- Switchgear facilities, electronic and control rooms and buildings: carbon dioxide extinguishing systems and/or mobile extinguishers; and
- Other buildings and open air facilities: Outdoor/indoor hydrants, hose cabinets.

chunks.text:
The firefighting water source shall be pre-treated water from the services/firefighting water tanks. Two (2) 100% firefighting water pumps shall be foreseen, one (1) equipped with electric motor drive and the other  with  diesel  engine  drive.  Redundant  jockey  pumps  (2  x  100%)  shall  be  considered  to  maintain pressure in ring main. The firefighting water pumps shall be installed in a separate building and the Diesel Pump and Diesel tank shall be installed in separated rooms at the building at the water storage tank area.
A  central  fire  brigade  station  shall  be  built  for  the  Plant  which  shall  house  the  mobile  fire  equipment (vehicles) and a command room, the main alarm panel, offices, staff rooms, a fully equipped medical station with a first aid room, workshops, stores, etc. and refilling units for portable fire extinguishers and breathing apparatus, as well as any other equipment required for firefighting and rescue.
For fire protection and detection purposes the overall Plant site shall be divided into separate fire zones and the alarms and control requirements for each zone shall be activated through a local control and alarm panel, including alarm signal to the existing central alarm panel and mimic board at the fire brigade station. A fire and gas alarm panel shall be provided in the central control room of the Plant.
An automatic fire and gas detection and alarm system shall be provided, with detection devices selected to suit particular risks, and with a control system designed to provide operating and fire brigade staff with sufficient information to identify and respond correctly to any fire detected.
The contractor shall provide temporary firefighting and alarm services during construction according to own assessment and requirements.

A public address system (loudspeaker system) shall be provided to cover entire plant for the broadcast of announcements throughout the power station. Loudspeakers shall be connected on a zonal basis with the call station and zone selection facilities located in the CCR. The complete PA system shall conform to the latest state-of-the-art. The system shall be complete including central amplifier station, master call station, remote call stations, loudspeakers, interfaces, cables, etc.
The loudspeaker lines shall be organized in different zones.
Different tone signals shall be provided for at least the following purposes:
- Call announcement;
- Operational alarm;
- Fire alarm; and
- All-clear signal (for resetting of alarm).
The sound output level of the PA system shall be designed to achieve a sound pressure level 10 dB higher than the ambient noise in the area to ensure speech intelligibility.
The PA system shall incorporate a self-surveillance facility for monitoring the status of the PA equipment including loudspeakers. Appropriate alarms shall be raised automatically to alert the operator when a fault is detected in the system.
The  Contractor  shall  be  responsible  for  ensuring  that  the  loudspeakers  supplied  are  suitable  for  the environmental conditions and that the loudspeakers are positioned and oriented to give the required sound coverage.
Power amplifiers shall be sized to provide sufficient power to drive all the loudspeakers under normal operating conditions plus 20 percent overload margin.
The public address system shall be interconnected with the PABX system for access from each extension.

Gas Turbine Generator and Steam Turbine Generator (STG) shall generate power at a terminal voltage of 15.75  ~  22  kV  or  any  other  voltage  level  according  to  OEM  standard  of  the  generator,  at  the  power frequency of 60 Hz. The generator shall be provided with all associated auxiliaries such as cooling system, and  all  other  associated  instrumentation  and  auxiliaries  of  proven  type  with  suitable  redundancy  in equipment.
The generators shall comply with the requirements of the relevant parts of IEC 60034 and shall be rated to match the turbine output over the full range of ambient temperature under all operating conditions. Each generator shall be subject to factory tests as required by those Standards. The generator shall be of an existing design which has a proven record of reliability for similar applications. Prototype designs are not acceptable.
Due to reasons of transmission operation needs the generator sub -transient reactance (saturated) shall be minimum 12%.
Turbine generators and related cooling systems shall be designed to class F and operated to maintain internal heating within insulation class B limits according to IEC 60034-1 throughout the entire operational range and throughout the ranges of ambient temperature.
Generator design consideration shall be in accordance to OTS. Generator performance requirement, voltage variation  and  frequency  variation  shall  be  in  accordance  with  the  Grid  Code.  Stable  Generator  Unit operation shall be possible at any power factor within the capability limits of the generator performance chart. Each generating unit must be capable of meeting any Network Connection Conditions for the 380 kV Grid and compliance to the Saudi Arabian Grid Code latest version.
The generator shall be either air or hydrogen cooled. For generators with a hydrogen cooling system, it is required that there shall be local hydrogen production and that provision shall be made for any hydrogen

chunks.text:
leakage into the cooling water system in service to be detected, alarmed and the rate of leakage measured. Similarly,  all  appropriate  generator  protection  systems  and  related  instrumentation  including  partial discharge detection and fire protection systems shall be provided and comply with the relevant NFPA standards.
In case of closed air cooling system, the generator air coolers shall be sized so, that maximum rated generator output can be maintained with 15% of the tubes blocked and with 15% of the tubes blocked and one cooler section out of service (cleaning) with temperature rise according class F. The cooler and isolating valves shall be arranged to permit isolation and cleaning of individual sections whilst the generator is on load.
In case of closed hydrogen cooling system, the hydrogen shall be circulated by fans mounted on the generator shaft in a closed circuit system incorporating H2 to water coolers. The generator hydrogen cooler etc. shall be sized so, that maximum rated generator output can be maintained with 15% of the tubes blocked and with 15% of the tubes blocked and one cooler section out of service (cleaning) with temperature rise according class F. The cooler and isolating valves shall be arranged to permit isolation and cleaning of individual sections whilst the generator is on load.
Continuously acting rotor winding earth fault monitoring, Generator online partial discharge monitoring system and flux probe for each generator.

Generator shaft voltage monitoring and Flux probe monitoring shall also to be provided.
Generator associated component i.e. Collector Ring, Shaft Grounding, Exciter Fan , Brush Holders shall be of proven design and similar design machines are being operated for at least since 10 years (a confirmatory letter for the same to be provided by OEM).

Continuously acting rotor winding earth fault monitoring, Generator online partial discharge monitoring system and flux probe for each generator with a common portable type online monitor (not continuous monitoring) as optional shall be provided with each GT and ST Generator.
Generators shall be provided with Online Partial discharge monitoring device with facility to monitor at remote DCS. Generator shaft voltage monitoring and Flux probe monitoring shall also to be provided.
PDM (Partial Discharge Monitor) in the Gas turbine package

MELCO PDM has a lot of proven track record.
For large capacity turbine generators, antenna type sensor is recommended because the sensor is not installed on to the high voltage winding, and they are not subject to any high electrical stresses.

- (2) IEC 60034-27-2 is the standard for on-line PD measurement on generator stator winding insulation.

The requirements of the Grid code shall apply.
The STG shall have sufficient capacity such that it does not limit the capability of the steam turbine over the range of ambient conditions.
The EPC is requested to design the components (turbine, generator, generator transformer) so, that the following conditions will be met within the complete range of defined range of maximum and minimum design-temperatures_ PT (Transformer power (MVA) at nominal power-factor and tap changer in middle position  '0'  )  ≥  PSG  (Generator  output  power  (MVA)  at  nominal  power  factor  as  input  power  to  the generator transformer) ≥ PST (Turbine power (MVA) at nominal power factor and consideration of the generator efficiency)
A graph shall be submitted with the bid showing in one diagram the power outputs PT, PSG, PST and PWT (Turbine  (active)  power  (MW)  as  input  power  to  generator)  versus  minimum  to  maximum  designed ambient air temperature (+4°C to +50°C).

Capacity curves, V%/f% curves, capability diagram and also permissible single phase and unbalanced 3phase loading plotted against time shall be submitted with the Bid. All diagrams shall be valid for operation under ambient air conditions from +4°C to +50°C.
The bearings shall be of the metal sleeve and self-alignment type and designed so as to be readily accessible and replaceable without the removal of the rotor. (For Gas turbine generators, tilting pad bearings are applied for better rotor shaft vibration characteristics.)
Air Cooled or Hydrogen cooled generators shall be provided. However, hydrogen cooled generators with stator winding direct-cooling clean-water cooling system will also be accepted, if of manufacturer standard design.
If hydrogen cooling equipment is applicable, the cooling system shall comply with the requirements of IEC 60034-3 for hydrogen cooling equipment. The cooling classification shall be stator/rotor IC7 (8) H1W7 and if applicable for stator-winding IC9W7W7.
The  generator  coolers  etc.  shall  be  sized  so,  that  rated  generator  output  at  class  B  operation  can  be maintained with 5% of the tubes blocked
Additionally, the numbers of coolers (preferably 4 coolers) are to be chosen so, that with one cooler section out of service (cleaning), a maximum generator output can be maintained. The requirements of IEC 600343,  Para 4.21 are to be fulfilled; (The hydrogen gas coolers of the proposed generators comply with the requirements in IEC 60034-3:2020, Para 4.22.)
The cooler and isolating valves shall be arranged to permit isolation and cleaning of individual sections, preferably whilst the generator is on load. (For Gas turbine package, the hydrogen gas cooler cannot be cleaned during generator operating condition considering safety concern.
A  complete  set  of  brushless  or  static  excitation  system  including  power  system  stabilizer  (PSS)  and excitation limiting devices.
A numeric type automatic voltage controller (AVR) with power factor and reactive power control
The excitation system shall be capable of producing a steady state short circuit current to ensure that the main and back-up protection are sensing and clearing the fault on the generator terminals.
A block diagram of the complete excitation system shall be provided with the Tender, together with the time-constants of the transfer functions for the control and stabilizing circuits.
Provision shall be made for testing the excitation equipment without the operation of the main generator.
Rotating exciters (RE) shall be of the enclosed, ventilated type, IP 54. They shall be directly driven by the generator. Ventilating air for rotating AC exciters shall be closed circuit cooling, incorporating an air-towater heat exchanger, and shaft mounted fans.

chunks.text:
For  Static  excitation  (SE)  the  thyristor  converter  shall  incorporate  a  number  of  three-phase  full-wave bridges and shall be arranged so that a minimum of 20% spare capacity is incorporated. The converter should be of modular construction, so that a minimum of one bridge may be removed for maintenance, whilst maintaining unrestricted operation of the main generator. This shall apply also for the field flashing facilities.  The  SE  system  shall  be  equipped  with  forced  cooling  in  2  x  100%  design  with  automatic switchover and monitoring from the CCR. The cooling medium for slip rings and commutators shall be separated from the exciter- and generator cooling circuits. This cooling circuit shall be provided with filters (easily maintainable) against carbon dust from the brush-gear.
In Gas turbine package, thyristor rectifier cooling fans are provided for each thyristor element in GT OEM standard system.
The redundancy is N+1 and that is as same as thyristor rectifier. Even if the fans are out of service in the one parallel of thyristor rectifier, excitation cubicle maintain generator normal operation.
The fan is applied DC fan which has features of long life and easy of maintenance and etc. Cooling fans power source are supplied by Distribution Panel.
A minimum excitation limitation device shall be incorporated, to prevent the AVR reducing the generator excitation below a value, which might endanger power system stability limits. The characteristic of the varlimiter shall be adjustable (also remotely) and facilities shall be provided so, that the var-limiter operating characteristic can be adjusted to any setting within the specified range.
For each generator a state of the art generator on-line condition monitoring system shall be implemented to show the momentary condition of the rotating machine respectively as well as long term trends. The generator on-line condition monitoring (partial discharge monitoring) system shall consist of sub-systems for specific monitoring tasks and shall comprise at least the following main functions:
Electrical real-time partial discharge (PD) monitoring system in accordance with IEC 60270 for permanent installation on-site;
Vibration monitoring system shall be provided as detailed below covering the vibration and displacements measured at each main  bearing  housing  (angle  of  90  degrees  between  the  two  probes)  and  by  direct measurement off the shaft adjacent to each main bearing plus axial position of the shaft also. Measurement and indication of shaft eccentricity shall also be provided. All measured values shall be readable in the control room.
