chunks.text:
The  excitation  system  for  the  generators  may  be  brushless  system  or  static  excitation  system.  Two automatic independent digital AVR shall be provided along with a manual channel. The regulator will be equipped with the required limiters for limiting the stator current, load angle / under excitation limiter, power factor, v/f, VAR etc., as per modern engineering practices. Power system stabilizer shall be provided as required by local regulations. The excitation system design and equipment shall conform to the Grid code / or any Government Authorisations Regulation requirements and IEC / IEEE standards requirements or as per agreed with Client.
The  excitation  system  and  equipment  shall  be  complete  with  fast  response  continuously  acting  dual channel  automatic  voltage  regulators,  (Dual  AVR  modules  with  automatic  and  manual  mode),  power system  stabiliser,  limiters  and  stabilisers,  field  suppression  equipment  and  all  necessary  control, monitoring and protection equipment. The static excitation systems shall include redundancy for thyristor bridges and cooling fans. Brushless excitation systems shall include redundant AVR.
Must have provision of complete control and monitoring of excitation system (AVRs) in remote control room through DCS. (For ST OEM, control and monitoring of the excitation system of STG will be sent to DCS from STG control system via OPC server. However, complete control and monitoring requirement of this document should be fully complied.
The generator excitation systems of high response static type complying with the requirements of relevant IEC 60034 or IEEE standards and Grid Code shall be provided. Automatic excitation control system of a proven design shall be provided to control the generator voltage without hunting/instability over the entire operating range of the generator.
The excitation equipment shall operate reliably and shall not impose restrictions on the availability of the generators due to excitation equipment faults or malfunctions according to excitation architecture and relevant redundancy.
Each static excitation system shall utilise a three phase fully controlled thyristor bridge rectifier energised from the machine terminals or medium voltage busbar through a suitable transformer. The transformer shall  comply  with  the  requirements  of  IEC  60076-11  (dry  type  transformer)  as  applicable.  Excitation transformer is connected to MVSWGR (medium voltage busbar) considering black out start.
Each excitation systems rated output voltage and current shall be at least 110 percent of the corresponding generator field (rotor) voltage and current for generator rated output overexcited.
label: text

chunks.text:
In order to provide adequate safety margins, the diode and thyristor devices in the power rectifiers shall have current (IFAV) and voltage (VRRM) ratings, which are at least 1,6 times the rated values and 1,1 times the rated current, unless otherwise approved by the Owner in accordance with the Contract. The Contractor will need to demonstrate its design is in line with industry standards. It shall be possible to detect failure of a diode / thyristor.
Excitation Transformer shall be located indoor i.e. Turbine House building and shall have the Thermal Insulation class F but the Temperature rise class shall be Class B. Following shall be considered in Excitation Transformer:
- Temperature detectors in LV coils of each phase
- Temperature detector in the middle core shank
- Tapping links on the HV side which can be disconnected under de-energized condition.
- For outdoor installation a metal enclosure is provided with IP23 class protection. (For Gas turbine package, oil immersed type excitation transformer will be considered and located outdoor.)
In case of GTG / STG OEM offer Dry Type Excitation and SFC Transformer for the Generator Excitation System, following consideration are recommended for design consideration:
- a) Excitation  Transformer  manufacturer  to  provide  detail  design  of  electrostatic  screen  and  its termination with ground. Electrostatic screen ends shall be labelled with bold tag with instruction to terminate it with ground. OEM documents and drawings shall be available with guideline of electrostatic screen connection with ground.
- b) EPC  to  ensure  completion  of  all  transformer  commissioning  works  and  confirm  electrostatic screens are properly connected with ground
The excitation systems and equipment shall be complete with fast response continuously acting (AVR) automatic voltage regulators one in operation, one in standby and one manual regulator (MVR) in standby,  power  system  stabiliser,  limiters  and  stabilisers,  quadrature  droop  compensation  and  cross  circuit compounding, field suppression equipment and all control, monitoring and protection equipment to enable operation from the Central Control Room. The excitation system shall be provided with a fast-acting MVAr limiter so as to prevent the generator output falling below its safe limit. Protection features as part of the system shall include over-voltage, overcurrent, VT fuse failure, diode failure, and AVR power supply failure.

A  field  shorting  or  discharge  switch  feature  shall  also  be  included  in  the  system  as  protection  against overstressing the generator insulation in the event of a fault.
Manual excitation control facilities shall be provided as a backup to the automatic control and shall have an adequate range to allow for control of excitation for testing purposes. A true null balance shall be provided to allow for smooth excitation transfer between manual and automatic control.
The system shall be one of high-initial response as defined in IEEE Standard 421.1. The continuous current capability of the excitation system at maximum ambient conditions shall be adequate for the operation of the generator at full load and rated power factor at 95% -105% terminal voltage, with the generator field at maximum temperature.
The  excitation  system  shall  be  capable  of  supplying  its  ceiling  voltage  and  the  growing  field  current associated with the sudden application of ceiling voltage to the generator field for at least 5 seconds. The ceiling current shall be at least 2 times the rated field current. The transient thermal capabilities of the excitation system for periods of more than 10 seconds and up to 120 sec shall be higher than the short-time thermal capabilities required in Section 7.2 of ANSI Standard C50.13 or IEEE C50.13 section 4.2.1&2 for the generator field winding.
The excitation system shall meet the requirements of the interconnection system but in any case, the AVR shall be capable of maintaining the steady-state terminal voltage of the generator within +/- 0.2 % of the set point according IEEE 421.1 or 0,5% over the entire operating range of the synchronous machine.
Over  excitation  limit  value  setting  shall  be  adjusted  automatically  according  to  rotor  temperature (proportional to rotor cooling air outlet temperature).
An adjustable device shall be incorporated to limit the per unit ratio of generator voltage/frequency (over flux) to such a value that the maximum ratio shall not exceed 1.1 per unit.
Under excitation, over excitation, stator current and overfluxing limits shall also be incorporated to prevent excitation falling or rising above the values necessary to ensure steady state stability and rotor and stator thermal  limitations  are  not  exceeded.  The  regulator  equipment  shall  be  free  from  voltage  drift  and temperature errors and insensitive to frequency variations between -6% and + 10% of nominal.
The excitation equipment shall operate reliably and shall not impose restrictions on the availability of the generators due to excitation equipment faults or malfunctions according to excitation architecture and relevant redundancy.
The static excitation system shall consist of:
- Excitation transformer;
- Solid state Thyristor based rectifiers;
- Field DC circuit breaker; and
- Excitation controls, Limiters and Protections.

Thyristor rectifier cubicle (including redundancy to satisfy reliability requirement under this document)

The excitation system shall be provided with a field ground detection system that monitors the soundness of the field insulation. The detection shall be continuously acting during operation.

Generator circuit breaker needs to provide ease of testing during O&M phase for Electrical testing with ease of doing and removal of main enclosure / major fitment.
On the conductor, aluminium flexible laminations, with the same total cross sectional area of the conductor shall be welded between the two sections of the conductor, to avoid sliding or bolted contacts.
The generator line-end bushing cubicle, which encloses the line-end bushings and allows the connection between generator and bus duct, shall be metal-clad isolated phase type, the cubicle shall be made of aluminium. The terminal block for connection of secondary windings of CT´s mounted on bushings shall be arranged in this cubicle. The star point cubicle shall be made up of a sturdy structure of aluminium fitted with all accessories necessary for connection to generator neutral grounding cubicle. The star-point cubicle shall  enclose  the  generator  star-point  bushings  and  the  relevant  current  transformers.  For  Steam Turbine/Generator set, OEM standard and general industrial practice are acceptable.
Temperature Limits rise for Conductor and enclosure of Isolated Phase Bus duct shall be as per ANSI/IEEE C37.23. The temperature of the conductor shall not exceed 90°C and for the enclosure the temperature shall be limited to 70°C.
The Generator circuit breaker and the bus duct shall be rated for the continuous operation of the maximum apparent power at minimum generator voltage.
The generator shall be provided with a (GCB) generator circuit breaker. The GCB shall comply with IEEE Standard C37.013. The generator shall be synchronized with the power system across the generator circuit breaker and the generator circuit breaker shall be suitable for this purpose in all respects.
The generator circuit breaker shall be sufficiently rated to break the maximum fault current under any fault condition without damage to itself or any other item of plant. The generator circuit breaker shall be of the SF6 type and arranged for assembly in conjunction with the busducts. The breaker shall be equipped with a  series-disconnector  on  the  transformer  side  and  with  earthing  switches  on  both  sides.  The  earthing switches shall have motor operated actuators. The breaker and disconnector shall normally be controlled remotely.
All the breaker unit functions shall be operable from the local control panel at the breaker unit.
Generator Bus Duct and Generator Circuit Breaker shall be subject to a type test, certified by a third party.

chunks.text:
Automatic  and  manual  synchronising  facilities  backed  up  with  check  synchronising  circuits  shall  be provided for the generator circuits. Synchronising equipment shall operate satisfactorily in conjunction with the automatic excitation control and turbine speed governing equipment.
Synchronizing of the generator by means of the generator circuit-breaker shall be carried out automatically from the generator control desk located in the CCR and automatically and manually (with synch. check) from the same location. (For Gas turbine package, manual synchronization device is not provided in CCR.) Synchronizing of the 380 kV feeder circuit breaker at grid substation(by the client). Under exceptional circumstances, at the sole discretion of the Client, the plant shall be permitted to open the Client's 380 kV Power  Unit  Cable  Circuit  Breaker(s)  or  due  to  transfer  trip  in  case  of  cable  protection  /  380kV  grid switching station bus bar protection operate. The Generator shall be able to open Client's 380 kV Power Unit Cable Circuit Breaker(s) only in an Emergency.
Each generator shall be provided with synchronizing relays which by means of a selector switch at the generator control desk shall provide the following facilities for the associated generator circuit-breaker:
Automatic:  Where  control  of  speed  and  excitation  is  carried  out  automatically  and  a  suitable  relay  is arranged to automatically close the circuit-breaker when speed, voltage and phase relationship are within permissible limits.
On the turbine control desk at CCR indication shall be given that synchronizing control is available at DCS. The DCS will include the necessary equipment for initiating an automatic synchronizing procedure.
The scheme shall be arranged so that the circuit breaker will either close directly once synchronism is achieved or closing can be delayed pending further operator action. A 'ready for synchronizing' indication shall be given.
Synch-check: Where speed and excitation are controlled manually and closing of the circuit breaker is also under manual control by means of the control switch on the generator control desk. In this mode, the synchronizing relay provides a check feature to ensure that closure of the circuit breaker is inhibited if speed, voltage or phase relationships are outside the permissible limits.
Manual: Closing of the circuit-breaker is under manual control the operator using the instruments to ensure that conditions are correct. The same shall be interlocked with Synch- check.
Selection of the method of synchronizing shall be by means of a key operated selector switch having the following positions AUTO/OFF/SYNCH-CHECK (lockable in all three positions).
Selection of the 'MANUAL' mode shall be made by putting the above selector switch in the 'SYNCH -CHECK' position.

chunks.text:
A set of synchronizing instruments comprising incoming and running voltmeters and frequency meters, a synchronous scope shall be provided on each generator control desk at Central Control Room.
Each  generator  unit  shall  be  provided  with  an  automatic  synchronizing  relay  and  a  separate  check synchronizing relay and this could be through generator control system facility.
Synchronization scheme for Plant Intermediate substation(s) feeder bay(s) and Client 380 kV feeder bay(s) subject to approval of Client respective Transmission department.
The  generator  shall  normally  be  synchronized  with  the  grid  by  the  generator  circuit  breaker  (GCB). Provision has to be provided that, It may also be resynchronized with the grid by the 380 kV circuit breaker of Plant Intermediate substation(s) / Client 380 kV remote substation. As the distance between Offtaker's 380 kV breaker and the plant is long then the VT circuits cannot be extended directly to the plant. Therefore, the synchronising relay will need to be installed in the 380 kV Client's site and synch ronizing with 380 KV networked through to the plant controller.
The generator shall have an automatic dual channel synchronizer. Synchronization shall be carried out by auto-synchronization mode and as well as by Manual synchronization mode.  A synchronization checking device shall be provided to control and supervise the Auto / Manual synchronization operation.

chunks.text:
The entire generator shall be mounted on a single fabricated frame supporting, the stator frame and the pedestal  bearings.  The  stator  frame  shall  allow  the  radial  expansion  of  the  core  and  absorb  the  core vibration without undue transmission of noise to the outside. The frame shall provide enough strength against the torque caused by the electric load and short circuit currents. In case of faulty synchronization, the stresses in the materials shall not exceed 2/3 of the elastic limit. The stator frame shall allow adequate air circulation for cooling of the rotor and stator.
The stator magnetic circuit shall be built with high permeability; low-loss grain-oriented stampings stacked on the frame key bars and pressed to form a single continuous core, with spacers as required for allowing an effective circulation of cooling air.
As an alternative, it can be non-grain oriented stator core laminations.
The stator windings shall consist of single-turn copper bars with the conductors transposed in the slot portion by the Roebel method and joined at their extremes. Thermosetting insulation shall be used, with spring type fillers and ripple springs to ensure that the bars will remain tight into the slots. The slot portion shall be covered with a semi conducting varnish and the end-turn portion shall be provided with graded semi  conducting  varnish  over  the  main  insulation.  The  end-turns  shall  be  adequately  supported  and secured  against  the  dynamic  forces  arising  from  solid  short  circuit  currents  between  the  generator terminals.
The  rotor  body  shall  be  a  one-piece  forging  machined  to  receive  the  copper  field  windings.  The  field winding shall have an ample cross section for a high ceiling current.
All components of the rotor insulation system shall be to class 'F' standards or better. Rotor earth fault protection  shall  be  provided.  A  continuous  monitoring  electronic  system  for  brushless  electronic protection equipment is preferred for brushless excitation system.
label: text

chunks.text:
The retaining rings shall be shrunk on the rotor to support the rotor field end turns. They shall be made from  18Cr-18Mn  stainless  steel  alloy.  The  rotor  shall  be  provided  with  radial  fans  at  both  ends  for ventilation of the rotor and the stator. The rotor shall be dynamically balanced at the manufacturer's shop, and it shall be mounted on tilting-pad type bearings. The bearing pads shall be insulated to prevent the flow of shaft currents. The number of bearings shall provide for ease in removing and inserting the generator rotor and exciter.
Shaft voltage measurement facility shall be provided by suitable means. One end of the rotor shaft shall be earthed by means of a strap brush which shall be easily re-measurable for the purpose of insulation checks. Where the bearing insulation is not easily accessible test terminals shall be brought to convenient point outside the bearing

chunks.text: The generator shall be provided with all required accessories for an efficient and continuous operation within its whole range of operation, including hydrogen gas to water heat exchangers inside the generator, bearing oil cooling system using oil to water coolers, lubrication oil supply, RTDs for thermal protection relays,  indication,  etc.  A  closed  circuit  water  cooling  system  shall  be  provided  for  the  cooling  of  the generator hydrogen gas coolers and bearing oil. Current transformers at the neutral and at the terminals shall be provided as needed for all the protection, metering and indication functions.

Generator neutral grounding equipment shall be provided for the generator. The grounding system shall consist of a single-phase, encapsulated dry-type distribution transformer with secondary loading resistor located in an outdoor compartment near the generator neutral terminal. The resistor and the distribution transformer shall provide high-resistance grounding to the generator to limit the magnitude of any ground fault current to approximately 10 A. The connection from the generator neutral to the grounding equipment cubicle shall be as short as practically possible if the grounding equipment cubicle is not connected directly to the generator enclosure.
The generator neutral connection shall be fully insulated from surrounding metallic enclosure and the connection  between  generator  neutral  terminals  to  earthing  transformer  shall  be  fully  insulated  and primary terminal of earthing transformer shall also be fully insulated.

chunks.text:
The transformers shall comply with the Saudi Arabian Grid Code especially with Section 2.5.5 of Chapter 2: Connection Code (refer to Section 4.1.11 of Part II of OTS Part A (Technical Specifications) of the RFP) and all NGSA related standards.
Oil-immersed  power  transformers  shall  comply  with  the  requirements  of  IEC 60076  and  series  of standards including IEC 60076-7 and shall be of the outdoor type. The selection of insulating oil shall take into consideration the most up to date protection against sulphur corrosion (according to IEC 62535) and without metal passivator (according to IEC 60666). The transformer oil must be pure virgin of naphthene base petroleum product, without any antioxidant (uninhibited) in accordance with latest edition of IEC 60296. Thermally upgraded paper to be considered for GSU/UAT transformers.
The  generator  step-up  transformers  and  the  isolated  phase  busducts  shall  be  designed  to  be  able  to transmit the maximum output of the corresponding unit at all possible ambient temperatures. Contractor shall provide with its proposal a diagram showing the capacities of the turbine, generator and generator transformers versus all possible ambient temperatures.
The transformer shall be designed to operate without exceeding the temperature limits of IEC 60076-2 under the continuous maximum output conditions of the Power Plant and during all other operational sequences. All transformers shall be of the core type, Cu/Cu winding and shall comply with the latest edition of IEC 60076.
Cooling classification shall be ONAN/ONAF or ONAN/ONAF/OFAF or ONAN/ ONAF / ODAF, except for plant auxiliary distribution transformers as that may be of the ONAN cooling for oil type or AF cooling for
label: text

chunks.text:
dry type, subject to provisions specified below. For oil immersed transformers, the radiators/coolers may be mounted separately from the tank or mounted on the transformer tank.
All transformers shall be equipped with tap changers that have local manual control as a minimum. The tap range, impedance and losses shall be selected to enable full output under normal conditions which allow for the highest and lowest system voltage operation and shall not be restricted over the specified ambient range.
The motor drive, plus all auxiliary equipment for operation of the tap changer, shall be incorporated in a rigid control cabinet, protection class IP56 and shall be mounted onto the transformer tank in a convenient floor height. The driving gear shall be of the belt-type or equivalent dry-type gear. Oil filled driving gears are not acceptable.
The  generator  unit  main  transformers  and  the  unit  auxiliary  transformers  shall  be  provided  with diaphragm  type  of  conservator  and  online  transformer  condition  monitoring  and  diagnostic  system including dissolved gas analysis (DGA). Online Dissolved Gas (Multi-gas) and Moisture Analyzer along with all required accessories shall be provided with each Unit Step transformer for measurement & analysis of dissolved gases and moisture in the oil. Interpretations shall be as per IEC 60599. These all DGA signals shall be wired to DCS for remote monitoring as well.
Each  Generator  Unit  Step  up  main  transformer  shall  also  be  equipped  with  in  line  partial  discharge monitoring system, whose functioning is based on the simultaneous use of three unconventional methods of PD detection: high frequency (HF), and acoustic emission (AE), vendor proposal can be acceptable during detail  engineering  stage  subject  to  in  compliance  with  IEC  standard.  PD  system  shall  be  integrated according to the IEC 61850 standard with SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) system to registering voltage, active power, and oil temperature of the monitored unit.
For the oil type transformers, the permissible temperature rises will be according to the IEC-regulations (IEC 60076-2). The top oil temperature rise is 40 K, the average winding temperature rise is 45 K for cooling method ONAF. The winding hot spot will be also selected in accordance with the IEC loading guide (IEC 60076-7). Considering the temperature rises mentioned before the winding hot spot will be 58 K at design ambient temperature of 55°C (outdoor without the shade) + 5°C. The winding and the oil temperature rise shall match this requirement as required by the OTS Part A. For the liquid filled transformers shall be provided  with  embed  temperature  sensors  in  the  critical  points  of  the  winding  to  ensure  hot  spot temperature measurements during the factory tests. For dry type transformers position in line with IEC 60076 for temperature measurement shall apply.

The step-up Transformers and the isolated phase bus ducts shall be designed to be able to transmit the maximum  output  of  the  corresponding  unit  at  all  possible  ambient  temperatures.  the  unit  auxiliary Transformers should also be designed for the ambient conditions on site and a sufficient spare capacity of at least 10%.
All oil cooled transformers shall be complete with the following:

damage and oil spillage (In excitation and SFC transformer of Gas turbine package, tap changers are not considered)

Power  transformers  shall  be  provided  and  installed  outdoors  in  the  main  substation  building.  These transformers shall be designed in accordance with IEC 60076.
Approved facilities shall be provided for inspection, testing and maintenance access to the gas and oilactuated relays and conservators associated with the transformers.

chunks.text:
Each Generator shall be connected to a generator step-up transformer to connect it up to the 380 kV GIS or AIS substation bay. The Two winding type generator transformers suitably rated to match the output of the prime movers over the entire ambient temperature range of the site and in every mode of operation, shall be provided. They shall also have ONAF/ONAN rating.
The generator step-up transformers shall be of ONAN/ONAF or ONAN/ONAF/OFAF or ONAN/ONAF/ODAF type of cooling. The ONAN rating shall be at least 60% of the generator MVA output rating over the whole range of site temperatures up to the maximum site ambient temperatures. However, ODWF type cooling with 4 x 33% oil/water coolers will be accepted. The generator step-up transformers shall be procured from  one  of  the  manufacturers  as  identified  in  the  Agreed  Approved  Vendor  List.  If  alternative manufacturers are proposed, then those will be subject to Owner approval.
The transformers shall be designed so that the 380 kV connections can be made by means of cable sealing end fittings with protecting funnels, motor operated isolators switches and earthing switches and with surge arrestors (all SF6 gas insulated).
The transformers shall be located in an outdoor compound adjacent to the generators each having firewalls, fire water spray system, oil collecting pit and a common oil separator. The transformer shall have an onload tap changer. The tapping range shall be selected to meet the voltage and reactive power control and operating requirements of the transmission system. The transformer LV terminals shall be connected by phase isolated bus bars to the generator. Generator step-up transformers shall have ONAN/ONAF/OFAF cooling.
The single phase fault contribution from each of the generator transformers to the 380 kV system shall be minimised by designing the transformers with the ratio X0/X1 not less than 0.95. The X0/X1 ratio of 0.95 shall be the absolute minimum and no tolerance below this figure shall be allowed. Such a design should ensure that there are no voltage regulation problems.
Each generator transformer shall be capable of continuously delivering the rated MVA of the generator over the Site ambient temperature range.
Neutral Point of each Generator step-up transformer (at 380 kV side) shall be solidly grounded as per detailed design engineering with compliance to requirement of the Grid Code. The star points are to be fitted with motor operated single-pole earthing switches and lightning arresters in parallel with the earth co nnections or grounded with 40 Ω impedance to limit the short circuit current.
label: text

chunks.text:
Generator transformers shall be fitted with On Load Tap Changer with AVR. The numbers of taps and tapping range shall be in accordance to meet the voltage variations at 380 kV (Grid Voltage). The OLTC shall have provision for manual local control, both mechanically and electrically, as well as manual control from a remote control room. Moreover, for automatic voltage control by means of a suitable voltage regulator.
The generator transformer shall be fitted with on-line gas monitoring equipment. For the oil type transformers, the permissible temperature rises will be according to the IEC-regulations (IEC 60076-2). The top oil temperature rise is 40 K, the average winding temperature rise is 45 K for cooling method ONAF. The winding hot spot will be also selected in accordance with the IEC loading guide (IEC 60076-7). Considering the temperature rises mentioned before the winding hot spot will be 58 K at a design ambient temperature of 55°C (outdoor without the shade) + 5°C. The winding and the oil temperature rise shall match this requirement as required by the OTS Part A
Technical Specification of Generator Step up Transformer shall be as under:
Bushings, surge arresters and cable sealing ends utilized for outdoor connections shall have a minimum creepage distance of 31mm/kV based on maximum phase to phase voltage (SCD) The creepage distance value is to be finalized as per the severity of the Site pollution characterization qualitatively defined in IEC 60815-1. The most stringent requirement between these two shall apply.  The Transformer shall have onload tap changer with a tapping range of ± 12 % in steps, each step not greater than 1.25 % of nominal Voltage. However, this may be revised according to country Grid Code for voltage variation by respective Offtaker / Competent Authority requirements,
Each generator step-up transformer OLTC (On Load Tap Changer) shall be equipped with an automatic voltage regulator (AVR). The AVR shall be active only if the generator circuit breaker is in off position
Transformer shall be designed to deliver maximum power at the worst voltage and power factor conditions and maximum design temperature.
Transformers with forced cooling shall be capable of remaining in operation at full load for 15 minutes after the failure of the fans, without the rise of temperature above the calculated hotspot temperature.
All transformers equipped with radiator units shall be equipped with one unit more as required.
The transformer neutral (star) points on the high voltage windings are to be solidly earthed  with the possibility of isolating them when necessary.  Therefore the star points are to be fitted with motor operated single-pole earthing switches and lighting arresters in parallel with the earth connections.
The low voltage side is to  be  equipped  with  connection  flanges  and  a  connection  frame  to  connect  an isolated phase generator main connection.

generator circuit breaker. UATs shall be designed for Plant's maximum auxiliary power demand (in 3x50% configuration). The UAT will step down the voltage to the MV voltage for unit and station Auxiliary loads. The UAT shall be a 2 or 3 winding oil filled transformer with LV windings which will get connected to the MV bus to serve unit and station loads. The transformers shall be adequately rated with suitable design margins to provide the auxiliary power supply systems and to be provided with off-load tap-changers as well  as  with  winding  temperature  indication  and  alarm  devices  and  gas  and  oil  actuated  relays.  The transformers shall comply with the requirements of IEC 60076 for temperature rise.
The Contractor shall suitably size these transformers taking into account power requirements of the Plant.

The  numbers  and  ratings  of  the  various  auxiliary  transformers  required  around  the  Plant  are  to  be determined by the Contractor based on load estimates for each service or building.
The LV auxiliary transformers shall be of two winding, outdoor oil filled type with ONAN cooling or cast resin dry type with AF cooling suitable for indoor location. Transformers with ratings less than 1 MVA may preferably be dry type.
Dry  type  transformers  shall  comply  with  the  requirements  of  IEC  60076-11and  and  be  mounted  in protected enclosures installed indoor with minimum mechanical protection IP23. Heat dissipation must comply with requirements of IEC 60076-11 (Para 4.2.3). Design of enclosure to guarantee to confirm and design to ensure that adequate supply air (clean, cool and dry) shall be provided to dissipate total heat as per design calculation of transformer.
Climate, environment and fire class shall be E2, C2 and F1 as per IEC 60076. Insulation class shall be F or H.
The no load voltage ratio of the auxiliary transformers shall be stated in the Contractor's proposal.
MV/LV Auxiliary power transformers shall be provided with off-load tap changer with minimum ± 2x 2.5 % steps or as per Grid Compliance study results. Generally, the transformers will be fed in MV via cables whereas the LV side will be connected to the MCCs through busbars.
The current transformers in all transformers, shall be wired to short-circuiting, screw type terminal blocks mounted in the transformer control panel.

chunks.text:
Dry type transformers shall be of cast-resin type designed for class F insulation and shall be operated with class B temperature rise. Temperature supervision for each winding shall be provided.
Cast resin power transformers shall be located in transformer housings with a degree of protection of min. IP23 and shall be located indoors in air-conditioned rooms.
The  numbers  and  ratings  of  the  various  auxiliary  transformers  required  around  the  Plant  are  to  be determined by the Contractor based on load estimates for each service or building.
The LV auxiliary transformers shall be of two winding, outdoor oil filled type with ONAN cooling or cast resin dry type with AF cooling suitable for indoor location or AN cooling suitable for outdoor installation. Transformers with ratings less than 1 MVA may preferably be dry type.
Dry type transformers shall comply with the requirements of IEC 60076-11 and be mounted in protected enclosures installed indoor with minimum mechanical protection IP23 or outdoor with protection IP54. Heat dissipation  must comply with  requirements of IEC  60076-11 (Para 4.2.3).  Design of enclosure to guarantee to confirm and design to ensure that adequate supply air (clean, cool and dry) shall be provided to dissipate total heat as per design calculation of transformer.
Climate, environment and fire class shall be E2, C2 and F1 as per IEC 60076. Insulation class shall be F or H.
The no load voltage ratio of the auxiliary transformers shall be stated in the Contractor's proposal.

chunks.text:
Design temperature of electrical equipment installed indoor in non-air conditioned rooms shall be based on 50°C and Design temperature of electrical equipment installed indoor in air conditioned rooms with HVAC n-1 redundancy shall be based on +5°C to 40°C and the relative humidity 10% to 100%.
MV switchgear bus of each GT shall each fed from UATs of the respective GTGs. And each section shall be connected to the MV switchgear of next GT with High-speed automatic transfer switch in order to achieve the full fed redundancy of each section to avoid a single point of failure concept.
The EPC has to provide type test certificates according IEC62271-200 for all switchgear in his scope of supply. Type test certificates shall also prove that the switchgear supplied is internal arc classified IAC = AFLR (arc duration 1 sec) according to IEC 62271 Part 200.
The  switchgear  shall  be  of  metal-clad  air  insulated  compartmented  type  tested  design  for  indoor installation and shall comply with IEC 62271-200, IEC 62271-1.
The  MV  switchgear  shall  withstand  a  short-circuit  current  of  minimum  10%  higher  than  required  by calculations for a duration of 3 seconds.
As basis for short-circuit calculation IEC60909-0 is suitable.
The cubicles are to be provided with single copper busbar system and draw-out type circuit breaker.
All electrical system switchboards shall be labelled for Hazard Risk category (HRC) as per results of ARC Flash assessment study using NFPA 70 E
The  MV  and  LV  electrical  system  will  be  fitted  with  the  necessary  electrical  and  mechanical  safety interlocking devices. Electrical interlocking will be in place to ensure that all closing and tripping functions (incl. in between, upstream, downstream systems) take place in a particular sequence (including busbar earthing switches). The interlocking scheme will be presented to the Owner for approval. The switchgear apparatus concerned by the interlocks will be equipped during the manufacturing with the appropriate keys and locking devices (type Castle Key or equivalent)
Arc flash study shall be conducted in accordance with the relevant categories are defined as per NFPA 70E (Test shall not be repeated if Certificate shall be provided by OEM). MV Switchgear comply with IEC 62271200 and LV switchgears shall comply with IEC 61641 for the internal arc flash resistance and testing. A label with the arc flash level and the PPE required to operate the equipment shall be provided in all MV cabinets/circuits. The label shall be of weather/UV resistant and posted in front of the equipment.)
The current transformers in all transformers, shall be wired to short-circuiting, screw type terminal blocks mounted in the transformer control panel.

Panels to be considered with inspection windows so to facilitate IR Inspection

HSBT systems to be added for Unit and common MV SWGRs

All  incoming  and  outgoing  feeders  including  motor  feeders  with  vacuum  circuit  breakers  with  motordriven stored energy mechanism. The circuit breaker shall have a defined test position. In this position, the main inserts of the breaker shall be isolated from the busbar and the cables and the shutters shall be closed.
The bare copper conductors of the busbars shall be provided with temperature indicators.
Any internal fault shall be cleared quickly by detectors sensitive to light (internal arc), pressure, heat or by the differential bus bar protection system. LV switchgears are not required differential bus bar protection and arc detection.
For earthing and short-circuiting the busbars, fault making earthing switches are to be provided on each section. The earthing switch shall be interlocked with the circuit breakers of all feeders connected to the relevant switchgear section.
The  individual  cubicles  are  to  be  bulkheaded  from  one  another  by  double  sheet  metal  partitions  or approved equivalent system. The busbar compartments must be bulkheaded from panel to panel by arc barriers. Within the cubicles, the compartments for circuit breakers, busbars, instrument transformers and cable connections as well as the relay recesses must be bulkheaded from one another.
Sufficient pressure relief must be provided in the case of fault arcs. For each bulkheaded compartment a separate pressure relief must be provided. Care must be taken that in the event of arcing no hot gases escape to the front of the cubicle (operational side)
A high-speed transfer system from one incoming feeder to the other incoming feeder shall be provided for MV-switchgears which are required for power auxiliary supply of the plant which when failure could cause an outage of a total Plant Unit and/or the total Plant
High-speed transfer systems shall be provided between the power sources with the required interlocking to avoid overloading of the related unit auxiliary transformer. Each of the systems shall be provided with facilities for selection of the changeover sequence/priorities.
The high-speed transfer system shall be started as follows:
- -manually (local or remote through the DCS)
- -automatic by protection relays
Each high-speed transfer system shall comprise following:
Logical analyser for all required control, interlocking and monitoring functions, Phase comparison device for continuously monitoring the phase angle, frequency and voltage, Test facilities for testing the complete transfer  system  up  to  the  closing  and  trip  coil  of  the  circuit  breakers  whilst  the  system  is  ready  for operation.
All main switchboards, MCC, relay panels, control equipment etc. shall be provided with duplicate power supplies for control and alarm purposes.

Each of the bus section will be fed power supply from respective sections of the 13.8 kV Block switchgear through a 13.8 kV /380 or 400 V. The bus coupler air circuit Breaker (ACB) will be interlocked with the incoming ACBs of the two sections.
380 or 400 V normal cum emergency auxiliary bus shall supply normal auxiliaries and essential auxiliaries of the Plant. This bus shall also receive power supply from the emergency supply bus. The essential bus provides power supply to chargers of the battery system, 380 or 400 V/220 or 230 V UPS systems, AC lube oil pumps, lighting system, etc.
The 380 or 400 V switchgear system main incomers, interconnectors and bus-section circuits shall exclude check-synchronising  facilities  but  shall  be  electrically  interlocked  to  prevent  the  paralleling  of  two incoming supplies to a switchboard.
Each switchboard shall have the degrees of protection IP40 specified for the enclosures and partition. The switch room floor shall not form part of the enclosures.
Circuit  breakers  supplied  shall  be  identical  to  those  used  for  the  type  tests  for  which  certificates  are submitted.
MV  switchgear  and  all  main  LV  switchgear  shall  be  of  withdrawable  type.  Fault  levels  and  thermal withstand  time  of  these  switchboards  shall  be  in  accordance  with  the  technical  requirements  of  the appropriate standards.
The Contractor shall perform a short-circuit calculation, in accordance with standards IEC 60909 and IEC 60865, in order to define the fault levels at all the different points of the Plant electrical network.
A two position (Local/Remote i.e. Switchgear/CCR) selector switch shall be provided at the switchgear for all  switchgear  incomer,  bus-section,  feeder  and  interconnector  circuits  respectively  for  switchgear emergency control and isolated testing/CCR remote control.
The Plant shall be provided with earthing and lightning protection system, illumination system. The Plant illumination system shall include emergency lighting system.
The Plant cabling system and cable support system shall follow Good Practice, local regulations. A fault monitoring  and  disturbance  recorder  system  shall  be  provided  to  cover  the  entire  electrical  system including incoming / outgoing feeders and Bus tie / coupling breakers.

Where operation of a switching device can give rise to surge voltages, which would be detrimental to the insulation of the equipment controlled, surge suppressers shall be installed in the switchgear to control these voltages to a safe level. Details of the maximum surge voltages which can arise shall be provided by the Contractor and shall state the criteria on which the provision of surge suppressers is based.
Feeder protection shall be by a digital multifunction relay. The MV switchgear shall be designed for remote control via the DCMS.
Low voltage devices and protection equipment shall be mounted in the door or on a mounting plate inside the low voltage compartment of the switchgear panel.
Switchgear design with two level arrangements of circuit breakers shall be available.
The  earthing  switch  shall  be  interlocked  (Electrically  and  mechanical  with  castle  key  or  suitable arrangements).
Interlocks  shall  be  provided  to  prevent  the  door  opening  (including  the  back  panel),  when  the  circuit breaker / contactor is in service position. With the door closed, the indication of position and the status should be Indicated.
Status of the earth switch and Switchgear shall be available on SCADA to ensure safe remote operation.
Medium Voltage Circuit Breakers will have a trip circuit supervision. This shall be provided to continuously supervise the integrity of the circuit breaker tripping circuits and give an alarm in the event of the following fault conditions:
- Loss of dc tripping supplies, e.g. MCB tripped;
- The alarm shall be time-delayed preventing it operating during momentary dips in the DC supply.
MV switchgear shall be provided with circuit labels on the front and rear of the panels. All enclosures and apparatus  shall  be  clearly  labelled,  on  both  the  front  and  back,  indicating  and  at  a  minimum  the  full equipment identification number for the device being controlled as per equipment coding system of project. The labels shall be corrosion resistant material, fade resistant and securely fastened.

chunks.text:
Low voltage switchgear shall comprise IEC 61439  and  IEC 60947 series type tested switchgear and control gear assemblies, factory assembled with all the internal mechanical connections and components fitted.
The design shall be according to IEC 61439 -1 form 4a for incoming feeders, form 3b for outgoing feeders and shall have a short circuit rating of 50 kA for 1 second or according to requirements of short circuit level defined through plant short circuit studies (whichever is higher). Busbars shall be air insulated.
Incoming circuits and tie feeder circuits shall be equipped with withdrawable air circuit breakers. The LVincomers and feeders will be protected by the internal protection of the MCB's, MCCB's and circuit breakers. Outgoing feeders shall use MCCBs and be installed on modular drawers assembled to form a combined power distribution board and motor control centre.
Motors  will  be  protected  by  comprehensive  digital  protection  relays  or  MCCBs  with  special  motor protection functions, subject to design requirements.
Incomers and bus-sectionalisers shall be equipped for remote control via the Facility DCMS. Other feeders shall be suitable for remote control operation as required.
LV distribution boards not controlled via the DCMS shall be equipped with indication lamps on the front door to assist personnel in the safe operation of the equipment and plant.
Switchgear design with two level arrangements of circuit breakers is available.
Motor control centre is available to be erected back-to-back.
There are no local control cabinets for all motors operated by motor control station (MV/LV) or process operation station in the central control room.

chunks.text:
Medium Voltage & Low Voltage Variable Speed Drives shall be provided wherever the process demands variable speed.
VFDs shall comply with IEC 61800-2, IEC 60146-1-3 and other relevant parts.
The converter shall comply with IEC 61800-3 with respect to EMC.
The converter equipment shall generally comply with IEC 60146 series of standards where appropriate.
Harmonic distortion shall not exceed specified limits as per IEC 61000/IEEE standard 519. All VSDs shall be  located  indoor  in  the  Electrical  buildings.  For  Medium  voltage  VSD  18-24  pulse  type  shall  be  used, whereas for Low voltage VSD active front end type shall be preferable.
All VFD's shall be suitable for control and indication through a serial link to the DCS process control system.
VFD  for  GT  auxiliaries  will  have  hardwired  connection  to  GT  control  system  without  serial  link.  The converter unit shall be stand alone for medium voltage drives. They should be self-contained in a sheet steel enclosure with IP31 degree of protection, with inlet and outlet filters where necessary, and shall be located  indoors.  The  cubicle  and  equipment  therein  shall  comply  with  the  appropriate  clauses  of  this Specification.
VFD design shall be reviewed and get confirmation from OEM that how installed design is protected against high voltage peak stresses (dv/dt) associated with High frequency pulse width modulation (PWM). It is also one of the factors which deteriorate cable insulation.
VFD shall be housed inside MCC for low voltage drives.

chunks.text:
The main connections between the generator, the GCB and generator transformer, as appropriate, together with the associated tee-offs to the unit transformers shall be made using isolated phase busduct (IPB). Busducts shall be complete with short circuit testing facilities and shall be pressurized with their own clean and dry air which may be supplied via a dedicated instrument air line from the instrument air receiver tank.
The busducts shall be of the self-supporting rigid type and shall be suitably rated up to the upper ambient temperature limit specified in this OTS and shaded (via sunshade or enclosure) against the direct rays of the  sun.  The  conductors  shall  be  of  high  conductivity  aluminium  and  all  joints  shall  generally  be  fully welded. Some joints of the conductors may be fitted with flexible / expansion conductors and connectors to prevent stress from affecting the conductors and the thermal insulation of equipment. The busducts shall
label: text

chunks.text:
have continuous and short-circuit ratings appropriate to the connected equipment for all site ambient temperatures in the design range.
As required, aluminium terminal enclosures shall be provided for the connected equipment and these shall incorporate expansion compensators, which electrically insulate the busbar enclosure from the equipment and provide a flexible connection to allow for thermal expansion and vibration.
As appropriate, conductors shall be connected via flexible joints. In the event of a unit auxiliary transformer failure requiring prolonged outage, it shall be possible to disconnect the UAT from the main busduct run to allow generator unit operation to continue.
The busduct shall be complete with sealed and fully insulated wall plates, fixings, supports and steelwork. Enclosures  shall  be  pressurised  from  the  instrument  air  system  to  prevent  the  ingress  of  dust  and dampness. Earth bars and flexible earthing connectors shall be provided between individual phases and equipment as appropriate.
Temperature Limits rise for Conductor and enclosure of Isolated Phase Bus duct shall be as per ANSI/IEEE C37.23.
Generator circuit breakers shall be provided for all gas turbine generator units. Generator circuit breakers shall  be  designed  manufactured  and  type  tested  for  generator  switching  duty  in  accordance  with  the requirements of IEEE/ANSI C37.013. The inherent design of these circuit breakers shall be such that they produce over voltages (less than 2.2 per unit) on switching conditions including inductive and capacitive switching to IEC62271-110.
Depending  on  the  Contractors'  proposed  arrangement,  the  circuit  breaker  shall  be  located  within  the isolated phase busduct between the generator and generator transformer and the installation shall include an earthing switch on the generator side and voltage transformers.
Generator circuit breaker needs to provide ease of testing during O&M phase for Electrical testing with ease of doing and removal of main enclosure / major fitments.
label: text

chunks.text:
System earthing shall be as follows:
- Generator transformer HV winding
:with 40 Ω impedance
- Generator neutral
:High impedance (resistance loaded VT)
- MV systems
:Low impedance (current limiting to 600A)
- LV systems
:Direct
The LV network shall be either of TN-S (separate PE and N conductors) or of the TN-C-S type with combined PE&N conductor (TN-C) from transformer to the main distribution, but separate PE and N conductors in the distribution and all connected consumers (TN-S).
DC and UPS system earthing shall be supplied as appropriate to the proposed equipment.
All non-current carrying metallic parts of plant, equipment, components, enclosures, protective screens, etc, shall be provided with earthing facilities for personnel safety reasons and for obtaining the maximum possible rejection of electrical interference.
Earthing should be generally designed and installed in accordance with IEC, IEEE  80 unless otherwise approved.
Protective screens around insulated cables shall be insulated from field instruments, connected through any field junction boxes, and be continuous up to the earthing point in the destination cubicle or panel.
Cable armouring shall not be used as a protective screen. Earthing of cable armour shall be arranged for electrical safety purposes and not for noise reduction. Cable armouring shall be insulated from any cable protective screening.
Where the Contractor's design requires a separate and dedicated earthing arrangement for example, a 'clean' earth for electronic equipment then the Contractor shall provide such earthing facilities as required. All instrument clean earth bars shall be clearly labelled as such.

Where a cubicle, frame or enclosure is earthed via the above facilities then it should be insulated from structural steel works or any other plant earth.

chunks.text:
Redundant (2 x 100%) direct Current (DC) and redundant (2 x 100%) with Nickle Cadmium batteries rated for  standby  period  of  at  least  1  hour  at  100  %  continuous  load  of  its  associated  distribution  board (2x100%). (For Gas turbine package, vented lead acid type with 1 hour is considered as OEM standard). UPS and DC to share the common battery bank is acceptable to provide complete static and dynamic load.
Each charger shall be rated to supply 100% of the normally running DC system load and the required float charge of the connected batteries. The Contractor shall also provide five (5) additional battery cells per DC/UPS system as part of its spare parts provision. (Except Gas turbine package).
DC systems shall be provided for instrumentation purposes and to power motor drives of switchgear and other consumers, as required for the safe shut down of the Plant.
UPS inverter systems supplied from LV AC or DC systems shall be provided for loads which cannot tolerate an interruption in supplies. These supplies or the loads shall be fully redundant.
Switchgear for DC and essential AC supplies may be of the fixed pattern.
The DC and UPS system for GTG will comply with GTG OEM's standard. If the OEM standards are based on approved international standards and codes than they shall apply.
DC/UPS system should feed to 2 x 100 % distribution board.
Chargers should be available with auto restart facility at restoration of main AC power supply.
Control DC power supply for plant critical circuits like protection relays, Control DC supplies of critical switchboards shall be provided with redundant dc sources fed from 02 different DC Banks.
Online boost charging provisions to be added for charger along with dropper circuit, required blocking diodes to be added to prevent circulating currents between the banks.

chunks.text:
All motors shall be designed and manufactured in accordance with IEC 60034 and other related standards. Motors in hazardous areas shall be suitably certified.
All motors with rated power of 200 kW and above must be designed as HV motors, connected to the MV switchgear and shall be fed via a circuit breaker.
The  rating  of  each  motor  shall  be  adequate  to  meet  the  requirements  of  its  associated  load  which  is designed for the whole lifetime of the plant, without infringing upon the service factor. The service factor is defined as the ratio of the installed motor output to the required power at the shaft of the driven machine at  its  expected maximum power demand including specified 10% excess capacity pump. Service factor employed shall be 1.1.
Electric  motors shall be designed for class F insulation. During operation at rated power of the driven machine,  the  motor  insulation  must  only  be  stressed  in  accordance  with  the  requirements  of  class  B insulation.
Anti-condensation  heating  shall  be  switched  into  operation  when  the  motor  feed  circuit  is  in  the  'off' position.  Heater  supply  power  'on'  indicating  lamp  shall  be  provided.  Condensation  outlets  shall  be provided at the lowest point in the housing.
Motor starting current must not exceed 5.5 times rated current for MV Motor DOL and 7 times for LV Motors DOL of rated current (referred to motor rating at 40°C ambient temperature)
The voltage drop at direct-on-line (DOL) starting must not exceed 10% at the motor terminals for MV and 15% at the motor terminal for LV.
Air cooling for the motors is the preferred method; where water-cooling is applied, conditioned, treated water is to be used. Cooler construction shall be per cooling water used. Material for cooler, cooler tubes, etc shall be as per water used. The running quality must be within the classification of "Class III, Zone A" according to the ISO 20816 or equivalent, i.e. the vibration velocity must be not greater than 1.8 mm/s (rms) Design and construction of the motors shall comply with IEC 60034-1 and 60034-5.
label: text

chunks.text:
- -High voltage motors must be fitted with measuring points for the determination of slot and bearing temperatures
- -The winding temperature has to be detected with RTD's at high temperature and alarm to be produced, at extra high temperature the motor to be tripped (In Gas turbine package, RTD is not applied to the LV motor (<100 kW) of the generator's auxiliary systems as per Supplier's standard design.)
- -For motors ≥ 1000 kW winding and bearing temperature readings shall be provided in the DCMS
- -Motors above 1000 kW shall be additionally protected by a high impedance differential protection relay
label: list_item

chunks.text: Motors of the same type must be fully interchangeable and shall comply as far as applicable with IEC standard motor dimensions. AC motors shall be of the squirrel cage induction type provided with either deep slots or double squirrel cages. Motors shall have Class F insulation but the temperature rise shall not exceed Class B However, for some fractional horsepower motors, such as airconditioning motors, it may be Class E or, as per manufacturer's standard. DC  motors  and  starters  shall  be  designed  for  high  reliability  with  direct-on-line  starting  using  a permanently connected series resistance in the armature. Emergency  stop  buttons  of  the  stay-put  key-reset  red  button  mushroom  head  type  shall  be  provided adjacent to all MV motors and all lubricating oil pumps (except for gas turbine package). These buttons shall directly trip the motors, prevent a start until reset and alarm their operation to the Central Control Room. The buttons shall all use a common reset key. For motors rated above 55kW, anti-condensation heating shall be switched into operation when the motor feed circuit is in the 'off' position. Heater supply power 'on' indicating lamp shall be provided. Condensation outlets shall be provided at the lowest point in the housing. All motors shall normally be of the totally enclosed fan-cooled type or water-cooled type, of protection class IP55  according  to  IEC  recommendations  60034  and  60529.  Where  motors  are  installed  outdoors  a weatherproof  design  IP55W  shall  be  chosen  according  to  IEC  recommendation  60034  and  60529. Motorised valves and submersible pump motors shall be to protection class IP65. LV-motors with ratings of 55kW and above shall be equipped with anti-condensing heater. All motors shall be designed as 3-phase squirrel-cage motors suitable for direct online starting The  motors  must  be  capable  of  being  switched  on  to  a  large  and  stable  network  and  with  phases  in opposition. LV-motors with ratings of  55kW and above shall be protected against overcurrent conditions by  PTCthermistors. Motor rating  to  be  at  least  110%  of  the  maximum  required  electric  power  consumption  of  the  driven machine. Continuous delivery of rated power at voltages of 90 - 110% of the rated voltage at rated frequency within the limits of thermal class F Rated  power  output  at  ambient  temperatures  existing  at  the  particular  site  of  installation  and  under continuous running conditions.
label: text

chunks.text:
For motors rated above 11 kW, anti-condensation heating shall be switched into operation when the motor feed circuit is in the 'off' position. Heater supply power 'on' indicating lamp shall be provided. Condensation outlets shall be provided at the lowest point in the housing.
The service voltages of the motors will be:
- 13.8 or 11 or 6.6 kV, 3-phase AC, 60 Hz, for motors above 200 kW (On Line Starting).
- 480/277, or 400/230 V , 3-phase AC, 60 Hz, for motors up to 300 kW (VFD Starting).
- 480/277, or 400/230 V 3-phase AC, 60 Hz, for motors 200 kW and below (On Line Starting) .
- Calculations of  the voltage  drop at start-up shall be made for the  maximum capacity motor to decide if the motor can be directly fed from a 400 V switchboard or through a starting device.
- Motors above 1,000 kW shall be additionally protected by a high impedance differential protection relay.
The  rating  of  each  motor  shall  be  adequate  to  meet  the  requirements  of  its  associated  load,  without infringing upon the service factor as per relevant IEC or NEMA and/or ANSI standards.
Except for low-speed motors (below 1000 rpm) three-phase AC motors of 500 kW and above shall have power factors not below 0.9 at rated power. Motors of a power lower than 500 kW shall be designed and manufactured in accordance with IEC60034.
Motors shall be capable of operating continuously under rated output conditions at any voltage deviation between 90% and 110% of the nominal voltage however their performances may be altered during such events.  A  transient  overvoltage  of  130%  of  the  nominal  voltage  shall  also  be  sustainable.  Further,  the motors shall be capable of delivering the maximum torque as required by the driven machine when running at 70% nominal voltage for a period of 10 seconds without damaging, overheating or slipping.
All motor driven auxiliaries shall be designed for 20 percent over speed for two minutes.
The pull-out torque for continuously loaded motors shall be at least 160% of the rated motor torque and for intermittently loaded motors 200% of the rated motor torque.
In case of Motor design and construction as per IEC standards with Voltage and frequency characteristics of motors are as per IEC 60034-1, Motor will start with allowable voltage fluctuation range, max 10 % drop as per IEC 60034-1.
Fixed speed AC motors shall be designed for direct on-line starting.

With voltage and frequency within permissible variation band, all motors shall be capable of two starts from cold in quick succession with a third start five (5) minutes thereafter all with full load. The motors shall have a hot restart capability of one immediate restart fallowed by two (2) starts at fifteen minute intervals, all fully loaded. Apart from this, the motors shall also be capable of three equally spread starts per hour. At the end of the three (3) starts the temperature of the insulated windings shall not exceed the maximum permitted temperature for class B insulation, and the cage windings shall not suffer damaging temperature rise.
In addition, each 13.8 or 11 or 6,6 kV motor shall be capable of enduring two (2) successive starts with the motor initially at operating temperature and the temperature of the winding at the end of start shall not exceed the Class B limit. Each 400 V motor shall be capable of withstanding two successive starts under the same conditions or once every twenty minutes without damaging temperature rise.
Vertical motors shall have combined thrust and guide bearings. Vertical motors above 37kW and all other motors above 200kW shall have roller type bearings.
All motors utilizing maintenance-free bearings must be clearly and permanently indicated as full. All other bearings  must  be  provided  with  a  lubricator  that  can  be  used  while  the  machine  is  running.  Overlubrication must be avoided by means of a lubricant controlling device.
Motors of the same type must be fully interchangeable and shall comply as far as applicable with IEC standard motor dimensions. AC motors shall be of the squirrel cage induction type provided with either deep slots or double squirrel cages.
All motors shall normally be of the totally enclosed fan-cooled type or water-cooled type, of protection class IP54/IP54w according to IEC recommendations 60034 and 60529. Where motors are installed outdoors a weatherproof design (minimum IP54w / 55) shall be chosen according to IEC recommendation 60034 and 60529. Motorised valves and submersible pump motors shall be to protection class IP65.
Motors shall have Class F insulation but the temperature rise shall not exceed Class B However, for some fractional horsepower motors, such as airconditioning motors, it may be Class E or, as per manufacturer's standard.
DC  motors  and  starters  shall  be  designed  for  high  reliability  with  direct-on-line  starting  using  a permanently connected series resistance in the armature.
Emergency  stop  buttons  of  the  stay-put  key-reset  red  button  mushroom  head  type  shall  be  provided adjacent to all MV motors and all lubricating oil pumps (except for gas turbine package). Synchronization of each Power Unit to the Grid is the responsibility of the EPC and normally shall occur through the Plant generator synchronizing breakers (GCB). The generator circuit breaker (GCB) installed between generator and generator transformer will be used for synchronizing the generator with the Grid through the Generator transformer. The Plant generator circuit breaker units shall have integral isolating facilities downstream of the breaker.
In the 380 kV GIS Substation, the 380 kV generator transformer circuit breakers shall be configured for operation from the Plant and also from GIS Substation control room and the electricity system Control Centre,  with  proper  interlocks  and  control.  The  only  permitted  operation  of  the  380    kV  generator transformer circuit breakers from the Plant shall be to open these in the case of an emergency.
Automatic synchronisation units of the numerical type shall be provided to synchronise the generators via the generator breaker (GCB) or the HV circuit breaker in the 380 kV GIS Substation.
If the circuit breaker of the connected 380 kV GIS or AIS Grid substation is not able to switch the steam turbine generators (ST-generators), all ST-generators shall be equipped with generator circuit breakers. It is  the  responsibility  of  the  bidder  to  clarify  this  technical  detail  with  the  Grid  substation  supplier  and Transmission.
The synchronisation process shall be initiated by the start-up program of the DCS or by manually given operator command after the desired synchronisation point (i.e. HV CB or Generator CB) has been selected.
The synchronisation unit shall automatically check whether the necessary conditions are being met, i.e. matching phase angle, voltage and frequency on both sides of the open breaker.
Manual control facilities in the local synchronisation panel shall also be provided for synchronising the units to allow operators to start or stop the synchronisation process manually. Synchro check relays shall be provided for use in manual synchronisation of the turbo sets. The voltages, frequencies, phase angles, and the status of the synchronising unit shall be indicated on the synchronisation panel.
In general, all necessary frequency, voltage and phase synchronization equipment shall be provided by the EPC allowing the resynchronization of the with the grid as per the latest version of Saudi Arabian Grid Code.

The  scope  of  supply  shall  comprise  all  necessary  control,  protection,  monitoring  and  supervisory equipment,  cabling  and  wiring,  regardless  of  whether  it  is  specifically  mentioned  or  not,  for  safe  and efficient operation of the Plant. The control and monitoring of the electrical system and other associated common systems shall include at least the following:
- Control, monitoring and protection of MV system;
- Control, monitoring and protection of auxiliary power distribution (LV, DC, UPS);
- Energy meter cubicles;
- Alarm cubicles;
- Auxiliary and marshalling cubicles.
MV and LV AC electrical systems (excluding LV sub-distribution systems) shall normally be monitored and controlled from the Central Control Room including for all transformers, switchgear incomers, bus-section, feeders and interconnector circuits via the plant DCS. The voltage of each switchboard, and single-phase current  of  all  main  circuits  (incomers/outgoing,  bus-sections  and  interconnectors)  shall  be  displayed locally at each switchgear, and for motors of 55 kW and above repeated in the Central Control Room via the plant DCS.
Motor circuits shall normally be controlled and monitored from the Central Control Room via the plant DCS system, except for station minor plant needing only local control. For motors of 20 kW and above the phase currents of each motor circuit shall be displayed locally at each switchboard.
Alternative locations of control of switchgear and motors shall be at the switchgear (under Permit to Work for operation or testing) or plant (for operation or maintenance).
LV  sub-distribution  systems  and  the  DC  systems  shall  be  locally  controlled  only,  but  alarms  shall  be transmitted to the Central Control Room via the plant DCS.
The switchgear shall include all related circuit prominent coloured LED type status and alarm lamps. The associated protection relays shall also include LED status/alarm indicators or flags.

The Plant shall be provided with emergency power supplies through diesel generating units to ensure the safe and controlled shutdown of all Units in the event of loss of all electrical supplies without damage to any equipment.
Emergency diesel generators for safe shutdown of the plant including supply of the essential HVAC load, where the essential HVAC load list to be submitted for Owner's approval during detailed design stage. It is suggested to adopt the concept of Two (2) emergency diesel generator (EDG), one for Power Block loads and 2nd one for Common loads (including BOP building HVAC requirements) and for safe shutdown loads of the unit such as Emergency drives, UPS, DC system and Emergency lighting etc. These EDGs will supply backup power to respective Normal cum emergency switchgears of the plant, in case of black-out.
Control Circuit of EDG shall be designed in manner to provide high availability in plant black out conditions. For example, supply of dc control supply for EDG Control circuit shall be provided from two separate DC sources.
Fuel level of Diesel tanks shall be monitored in control room.
The Emergency Diesel Generator Set shall be installed outdoor in the IP 54 Protection Class Canopy / Soundproof Enclosure / Containerized Solution in accordance to the IEC 60529.
Emergency diesel generators shall be designed with a class F insulation and shall be operated with class B temperature rise.
The  EPC  shall  provide  the  sizing  calculation  for  Emergency  and  Black  Start  Generators.  Further requirements are set out in following sections.
Emergency  diesel  generator  including  MV  switchgear,  distribution  cables,  MV/LV  transformers  and emergency power distribution for all units, auxiliary boiler and utilities.
The Plant shall be provided with emergency power supplies through diesel generating units to ensure the safe and controlled shutdown of all Units in the event of loss of all electrical supplies without damage to any equipment.

Black start generator set(s) with N+1 redundancy shall be installed to start one gas turbine. The black start generators shall be fired with Back-up Fuel. Number of black start generators required shall be determined by the EPC considering the load required to start one gas turbine comprising GT starting load, GT associated auxiliary system load and related plant BOP necessary load. The black start system shall be configured to select and start any GT.
The black start generator shall have the same features stated for Emergency Diesel Generator.
The Black start generators shall have the feature to start and synchronise with mains to share load in parallel.
Black start Diesel Generator set shall be able to be tested on any GT of a block, while the other GTs and the ST of the same block are still in operation. During the test the BSDG set shall serve start-up the selected GT which shall be completely isolated from the neighbouring groups and from the Grid. The test is considered successful once the GT, that was started with the BSDG, set is successfully synchronized with the Grid and the BSDG is load is transferred to the normal power supply, without tripping the unit.
The Facility shall be capable of restarting from complete blackout conditions. This could either be achieved by a suitably sized emergency blackout diesel generator or a gas turbine generator and which shall be capable of starting any of the Power Blocks capable of starting the Plant from blackout conditions.
EPC shall install Black Start Facilities and all necessary auxiliaries of sufficient capacity to start any one of the gas turbines, connect to de-energized transformer circuit breakers located in the Offtaker's 380 kV GIS Substation, energize the dead 380 kV bus bars, energize the outgoing transformer feeders and energize the inter bus transformers and reloaded to its maximum capacity under the PPA or PWPA. The Black Start Facilities shall have 100% capacity to start each one of the gas turbines even with the loss of one diesel generator.
The Black Start Facilities should be capable of operation if all other sources of electrical power either within or outside the Plant are not available. The Black Start Facilities shall use liquid fuel and be provided with sufficient fuel storage capacity for 6 hours operation without replenishment of fuel supplies.
The Black Start Facilities shall be capable of being tested whilst the Plant is in operation and without shutting down or interrupting or affecting the operation of other parts of the plant. Provision shall be made available for the functional test of the BS facilities to be conducted to carry out the black start of any GT without shutting down or affecting t he operation of any other parts/system of the plant.'
It is to be provided with feature to start and synchronize with mains to share load in parallel.

EPC shall undertake a detailed study into the operation of the Black Start Facilities and gas turbine and generator control systems design such that a gas turbine can be started, be connected to the Grid and be loaded in the event of a complete system failure. The results of the Study shall be presented to the Offtaker.
The Black Start Facilities shall be commissioned and tested prior to the Scheduled Early Power Commercial Operation Date (as per the PPA).

chunks.text:
The line side connection to the generator shall be designed as a single phase encapsulated IPB. The IPB must be sealed air-tight to the generator bushings to impede ingress of hydrogen into the IPB for the case of hydrogen leakage at generator terminals. A forced ventilation system, installed in each phase of IPB enclosure near to the generator bushings shall prevent a concentration of hydrogen by means of provided outlets towards turbine hall. The connection between IPB conductors and generator terminals shall be realized by flexible copper links with silver-plated contact surfaces. The conductor connection shall be provided as such that a removal of generator bushings is possible without any cutting and re-welding on the IPB enclosure. The generator and the IPB shall be designed in a way that current transformers of ring core type can be installed at line side within the IPB enclosure or at the generator terminals.
The built-up of neutral shall be realized within a special generator neutral box. A forced ventilation system, installed  for  each  of  neutral  bushing  shall  prevent  a  concentration  of  hydrogen  by  means  of  provided outlets  towards  turbine  hall.  The  generator  and  the  IPB  shall  be  designed  that  way  that  current transformers can be installed wi thin the box or as per Contractor's standards. The generator neutral shall
label: text

chunks.text:
be connected via a busduct or a cable with the grounding transformer inside the neutral grounding cabinet. For Turbine/Generator set, OEM standard and general industrial practice are acceptable.
In  Gas  turbine  package,  forced  ventilation  system  is  not  applied  to  the  neutral  cover  of  the  proposed generator. Instead, ventilation holes in the cover is considered to enhance air in-flow through it.
label: text

chunks.text:
The connection of IPB to transformers is designed as single-phase encapsulated solution. The mechanical connection between the IPB enclosure flange and the transformer flange shall be carried out insulated. The flange connection shall be sealed by a gasket. The contact surface of connection between IPB conductor and transformer  terminal  shall  be  provided  by  means  of  silver-plated  flexible  copper  links.  The  conductor connection shall be designed as such that a removal of transformer bushings is possible without any cutting and re-welding on the IPB enclosure.
Surge arresters for each phase of IPB shall be provided near to the generator transformer. The arresters shall be mounted within cabinets which are an integrated part of the IPB enclosure.
label: text

chunks.text:
For testing and maintenance purposes the IPB shall be equipped with a manually operated short-circuit device (SCD). The SCD shall be directly connected at the IPB between the generator and the generator circuit breaker. The SCD must be designed for the full short circuit current for 1 s duration.
For each phase in the IPB a temporary grounding device (TGD) at the transformer side of the generator circuit breaker shall be provided. For this reason, the IPB conductors shall be equipped with a countercontact  for  installation  of  the  TGD.  Access  to  the  conductor  must  be  achieved  by  covers  within  the enclosures which are securely bolted.
