chunks.text:
A control oil system shall be supplied to control and actuate the main steam turbine inlet valves. Such a system may use the same oil and the lubricating oil system and, if so, no separate control oil reservoir, pumps and coolers will be necessary. If a separate system is proposed, however, the control oil system may use  either  mineral  oil  identical  to  the  lubricating  oil  or  synthetic  fire  resistant  fluid  and  shall  have  a dedicated reservoir and dedicated pumps, coolers and filters.
The pressure and temperature of the oil shall be automatically controlled. Failure of the control oil system pressure shall automatically trip the turbine.
label: text

chunks.text: A  jacking  oil  system  shall  be  provided  to  facilitate  turning  of  the  rotor  for  cooling  down  and  during maintenance activities. If required, it is preferable that the jacking oil system should only be required to assist  starting  of  the  barring  motor  and  that  normal  barring  speed  should  be  high  enough to establish hydrodynamic lubrication at the bearings using the main or auxiliary oil pumps.
label: text

chunks.text:
There shall be a motor driven barring gear capable of turning the turbine and generator rotors continuously at a high enough speed to establish full hydrodynamic lubrication.
The barring gear shall be capable of automatic and remote-manual engagement, disengagement, starting and stopping. Interlocks shall be provided to prevent starting and/or engagement if the turbine rotor is turning or if there is insufficient lubricating oil pressure.
An emergency facility shall be provided for turning the turbine rotor by hand with the aid of a hand wheel or, if applicable, jacking oil.
label: text

chunks.text:
The turbine shall be supplied with a fully automatic gland sealing system complete with all condensers, pipework, valves and control equipment. All remotely operated isolation and bypass valves required for remote switching of gland steam sources shall be provided. The system shall ensure that the rotor glands are sealed against air ingress and steam leakage to atmosphere at all turbine loads.
The  system  shall  be  self-sufficient  in  steam  (i.e.  it  will  not  require  constant  make-up)  throughout  the majority of the load range.
The system shall comprise as a minimum:
- Gland steam make-up valve for low load operation
- Gland steam regulating/dump valve
- Gland steam receiver
- Gland steam condenser
- 2 x 100% condenser exhaust fans
Intermediate gland leak-offs shall be returned to an appropriate stage of the turbine.
The outermost gland leak-off shall be connected to the gland steam condenser, which shall be held under a slight depression by the exhaust fan. The discharge of the fan shall be directed to a safe location outside the turbine enclosure.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
The  turbine  and  generator  rotors  shall  be  supported  in  a  conventional  two  or  four  journal  bearing arrangement with a solid coupling and a single thrust bearing. Sleeve-type or tilting-pad type bearings may be used.
The bearings shall provide adequate damping to prevent excessive resonance at critical speeds.
Main journal  bearings  shall  be  of  the  plain  bore  white-metal  type,  with  forced  lubrication.  Alternative designs featuring 'lemon bore' or 'offset halves' may be considered. Bearings for small auxiliary drives such as governor, oil pump, barring gear, may be of the rolling element type.
Journal bearings shall be horizontally split and mounted on spherical pads within spherical housings to facilitate alignment between bearing and journal.
Supply of jacking oil to the journal bearings shall be made.
Each bearing shall have thermocouples to measure the temperature of the bearing metal. Each bearing shall also be supplied with at least two orthogonally mounted vibration monitors of the electronic proximity type to continuously monitor shaft radial vibration. Bearing metal temperature shall be monitored locally and remotely in DCS.
Thrust bearings shall be of the horizontally split, tilting pad type and shall incorporate main thrust and reverse thrust bearings. At least two rotor axial position monitors of the electronic proximity type shall be provided to continuously monitor shaft axial position.
Special attention shall be given to the design of bearings and supports, and to the accurate dynamic balance of the rotating parts of the turbines and generators, to minimise vibrations. The rotors shall be statically and dynamically balanced in the factory so that the maximum effective vibration magnitudes do not exceed the recommended values under steady running conditions at all loads. Means shall be provided so that, if necessary, adjustments to the balance may readily be made. Vibration limits shall comply with vibration criteria as per guideline ISO 20816-2. Both bearing and shaft vibrations shall meet requirements of Zone A. The  acceptance  criteria  for  the  inspections  performed  during  the  component  manufacturing  must  be defined before the start of the works.and must be submitted to the Owner for approval.
label: text

chunks.text:
If necessary, the design of the LP turbine shall include spray cooling to maintain acceptable last stage blade temperatures when operating at part-load conditions.
Automatic sprays shall be provided to prevent high exhaust temperature of LP turbine. When exhaust hood spray valve is opened, water from the condensate pump shall discharge to spray nozzles installed in the turbine exhaust hood chambers. Overheating of the exhaust end shall be avoided even with no load steam and  full  vacuum.  The  exhaust  hood  spray  shall  be  set  to  control  exhaust  hood  temperature  to  90°C maximum. The exhaust hood spray will be deactivated when exhaust hood temperature falls below 60°C.
If power increase does not lead to fulfilment of the criterion (TLe-0 < 100°C ∧ Texit steam < 60°C), the exhaust hood spray will be deactivated when the power level is greater 20% of the rated power.
label: text

chunks.text:
All  protection and control systems shall be 100% redundant including all unit protection systems. The details shall be described in detail engineering stage with Owner's Approval.
At least the following turbine protection devices shall be included in the supply:
- Local hand trip
- Remote emergency push button
- Low bearing oil pressure trip
- Over speed protection system (duplex)
- High back pressure
- High exhaust temperature
- Differential expansion between rotor and casing
label: text
list_item

chunks.text: Arrangements shall be provided for on-load testing of these devices.
label: text

chunks.text: The condensate systems shall supply condensate from condenser to the deaerator. The system shall include condenser, vacuum pumps, condensate extraction pumps, control valves, pipe work, etc.
label: text

chunks.text:
Air cooled condenser(s) will be required to let down steam from the condensing part of the steam turbine and from the LP-steam headers.
The system shall comprise at least the following equipment:
- steam duct from the steam reducing stations to condenser and steam distribution ducting,
- steam duct from turbine exhaust flange to condenser and steam distribution ducting,
- condensate collection headers,
- air moving system,
- fan drives,
- steel support structure, including maintenance platforms, access stairways and escape ladder,
- facilities for prevention of air recirculation,
- noise attenuation features/devices as required,
- all  required  electrical  and  control  equipment  for  safe  operation,  monitoring  and  measuring, earthing and lightning protection,
- air evacuation pumps, if applicable,
- ejector condenser, drain tank and strainers at ejector steam inlets,
- condensate tank and drain,
- drain and vent pumping, piping, valves and traps with supports, and
- semi-automatic ACC outside heat transfer surface cleaning system.
The steam turbine condenser shall be complete in every respect for reliable, efficient and safe operation for a high service lifetime. The design of the air-cooled condenser shall be in accordance with the ambient conditions at Project Site and steam turbine requirements.
The condenser shall be sized to receive:
- Condense all steam for all operating ranges
- Accept the full steam turbine bypass steam when the steam turbine trips.
The  capacity  of  the  steam  turbine  condenser  shall  include  a  reserve  to  cover  possible  steam  turbine overloads.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
The cooling air to each heat exchanging cell shall be forced by individual axial flow fan; each fan, whose blades shall be adjustable when the fan is out of service, shall be driven by a variable speed motor.
All the components of the fan/drive unit shall be designed for continuous outdoor service over the range of air condenser loads, ambient air temperatures and air temperatures adjacent to the tube bundles.
It shall be possible to initiate a cold start of the fans during any ambient air temperature within the specified range.
All drive components shall be rated to take into account any shock loading that may occur from starting a fan which may be rotating in a reverse direction under the influence of prevailing winds or convection currents. As an alternative, a reverse rotation lock may be provided.
Each fan drive shall be individually remotely controlled from the Control Room allowing the operator to optimize the operative configuration on the basis of actual ambient condition.
label: text

chunks.text: It shall be possible to clean the outside heat transfer surfaces by application of well established cleaning procedures. A semi-automatic high-pressure spray-water cleaning system shall be supplied for periodically cleaning the heat exchanger external surfaces during normal operation, keeping them free of deposits and maintaining the heat transfer coefficient of the condenser. It shall be possible for this cleaning system to be used whilst the ACC is in operation.
label: text

chunks.text:
Inert gases shall be evacuated by the air extraction system. The system for air removal from the steam side of  the  condenser may consist of steam ejector system or water ring vacuum pump system for holding operation (2x100% units for any system). For hogging prior to start-up of the ST a water-ring vacuum pump system with one stand-by pump (e.g 4 x 33% or 5 x 25%) for parallel operation shall be applied, in case steam ejectors are provided, 1x100% steam jet air ejector can be used provided that the time required for reaching the vacuum is less than 30 minutes. If water ring pump system is selected, EPC Contractor can propose to be used as common system for holding and hogging.
ST condenser air extraction system discharge flow indicator to provide to know the air ingress quantity.
label: text

chunks.text:
3x50% or 2x100% duty centrifugal pumps, complete with motors, couplings, guards, suction barrel, all necessary steel supporting  structure,  cooling  and  lubrication  systems  with  mechanical  sealing  shall  be provided for each steam turbine. The CEP type (horizontal or vertical) shall be selected also considering condensate storage tank water level (height).
The pump design point shall be selected in order to cope with all the possible operating conditions.
The standby pump is intended as back-up (automatic start in case of failure of the operating pumps). In case of turbine bypass the third condenser extraction pump may need to come into operation.
The pump casing shall be arranged within the suction barrel, which is submerged in the foundations. The suction and discharge pump nozzles shall be located above the floor level and arranged so that the pump can be easily withdrawn after pipe branches have been disconnected.
The pump driving motor shall be air cooled and be flexibly coupled to the pump shaft. All bearings shall be of the removable type to permit easy replacement at site.
Adjustable rigid coupling shall be used instead of split rigid coupling.
Pumps may have either packing or mechanical seals, as determined by the application.
The pumps shall work satisfactorily and free of cavitation under all operating conditions. The available NPSH at the minimum level of the condenser hotwell and with maximum head losses shall be higher than the required NPSH at all loads. The water velocity in the independent pump suction pipework shall not exceed 1 m/s.
The characteristic curve (flow/head) will constantly decrease maintaining a uniform slope from the point of zero flow to the design point. All the identical pumps shall have the same characteristic curve.
Pump  must  be  equipped  with  the  necessary  instruments  (suction  and  discharge  side  manometer, thermometer etc.) For condensate extraction pump, modulating automatic recirculation control valves or combined recirculation/check valves will be used.
The pump impellor shall be made of a suitable grade of stainless steel with high resistance to pitting and erosion., The impellor shall be balanced statically and dynamically and be secured to the pump shaft in a manner, which permits easy maintenance and replacement at site.
Interchangeable stainless steel protecting sleeves shall be provided at the shaft seals and at the lower journal bearing.
The pump casing material shall be cast steel. The suction barrel material shall be carbon steel. A rustproof protective coating shall be applied to the surfaces of the barrel.
Pump characteristic curves and all relevant data for each of the specified operating conditions shall be submitted as well as the arrangement and foundation drawings.
label: text

chunks.text:
All  necessary  auxiliaries  shall  be  supplied  for  the  pumps  as  applicable  (e.g.  Associated  pipework  and valves). For each pump a stop valve shall be provided on the suction and a non-return valve and motor operated valve on the pump discharge.
A strainer with large surface area and low-pressure losses shall be provided in the suction line of each pump.
Venting of the upper parts of each pump shall be realized by suitable connections to the main condenser.
A complete water sealing system shall be provided to seal the stuffing boxes and all parts subjected to vacuum at start-up, during standby operation and/or during normal operation. The sealing water shall be taken from the pump delivery.
A minimum flow recirculating system, common for the two or three pumps and equipped with built in cascade throttling shall be provided.
Sampling and chemical dosing points will be provided on condensate system (downstream of condensate extraction pumps).
label: text

chunks.text: Each feed system shall be furnished  with all necessary equipment required  for manual and automatic control  from  the  Central  Control  Room  during  the  operations  associated  with  Start-up,  synchronising, loading and shut down of the GT/HRSG sets. Each feed system shall be designed as appropriate as to the function  with  either  Power  Block  in  case  multiple  blocks  are  provided.  The  design  shall  also  take  due consideration of all possible operating scenarios of the Plant. All materials in the feed water system shall be ferrous.
label: text

chunks.text: The demineralised water storage tanks shall feed 2 x 100% make-up water supply pumps for initial filling of HRSGs, deaeration facilities, condensers and makeup to the condensate water storage tanks. The Makeup water during plant operation shall then be provided from the condensate water storage tanks by 2x 100% condensate transfer pumps.
label: text

chunks.text:
The  design,  manufacture  and  construction  of  the  deaerators  shall  be  in  accordance  with  recognised pressure vessel codes. The deaerators shall be designed to withstand full vacuum.
The deaerators shall be of the spray-tray type (although a purely spray type will be considered) and shall consist  of  a  deaerator  vessel,  water  storage  tank,  pipes,  valves,  ancillary  equipment,  instruments  and controls  necessary to maintain operation under all normal conditions. Equipment shall be provided to maintain the minimum deaerator pressure at all steam turbine loads.
The  deaerators  shall  be  provided  with  sufficient  connections  to  accommodate  feed  pump  suction  and recirculation  pipes,  condensate  return,  LP  steam  heating  and  instrumentation.  The  deaerators  shall  be located at high level such that the feed pump NPSH requirements are satisfied.
The  deaerators  shall  be  designed  to  reduce  the  oxygen  content  of  the  feed  water  to  not  greater  than 0.007mg/l,  under  all  operating  conditions  above  10%  feed  flow,  as  measured  by  the  Heat  Exchanger Institute method.
The deaerated water storage capacity shall be designed on the basis of at least 10 minutes
In case of integrated deaerator type HRSG, each drum shall be 2 mins for HP drum, 5 mins for IP drum and 10 mins for LP drum from normal to low low water trip levels with feed water flow at full load; the actual time shall be agreed during the detailed design phase of the Project.
The deaerator parts including spray nozzles and splash trays shall be of stainless steel.
The EPC Contractor is free to propose the deaerator integrated with LP drum.
label: text

chunks.text:
HRSG will have natural circulation and horizontal flow type. Each pump suction pipe from the deaerators shall be designed to avoid pump cavitation under all conditions and shall adhere to applicable international code and shall include valve connections for chemical dosing as necessary.
Only proven feedwater pump designs at similar duties shall be proposed.
Minimum flow recirculation bypass line and control shall be provided.
Each HRSG shall be provided with 3x50% or 2x100% horizontal centrifugal electrically driven boiler feed pumps. Feed water pumps shall provide feed water at controlled rates via split control valves as detailed below:
- A low load valve -used during start up and low loads.
- A high load valve -used for higher load
The pump total head at rated capacity shall include a margin for wear in addition to normal design margins.
The characteristics of the pumps shall be such that the closed valve head is approximately 120% of the pressure at rated output.
The minimum flow lines and relief lines  (if required)  shall  run  individually  to  the  deaerator  or  to  the feedwater storage tank. The minimum flow valves shall be provided for the stable start/stop of pump while protecting the pump. For these purposes all of design conditions of the valve including actuator type shall be decided The minimum flow capacity shall be as required by the feedwater pump vendor. The minimum flow shall be checked via control valve and monitored on DCS.
It shall be possible to start the pumps safely from cold without prior warming up or other preparatory measures.
Pumps shall be equipped with mechanical seals, single balanced type. Gland seals shall be supplied for each main pump. Seals flushing shall be provided with double magnetic separator, if applicable. The pump glands shall  be  arranged  in  such  a  way  that  the  removal  of  the  packing  can  be  carried  out  with  minimum disturbance.
The feedwater pumps shall be equipped with bearing temperature and vibration monitoring devices.
The discharge connection of the main pump shall be of the flanged end type.
A  basket  type  strainer  shall  be  fitted  at  pump  inlet,  fine  mesh  baskets  shall  be  fitted  for  initial commissioning.
Vibration and temperature monitoring and protection system shall be installed.
The whole pumping unit shall be capable of withstanding, without detriment, reverse rotation to a speed that would occur if the pump were to stop when the differential head was at a maximum and the delivery and/or non-return valve failed to close (this would typically occur if one trips and the discharge valve remain open, while the other pump maintains operation). If the pump cannot withstand this scenario the pump must incorporate a safety system to avoid this from happening.
Pump  must  be  equipped  with  the  necessary  instruments  (suction  and  discharge  side  manometer, thermometer etc.)
Couplings and intermediate shafting will be guarded. Bedplates will be of ample proportions and stiffness to withstand the loads likely to be experienced in shipment and service.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
The weight of the impeller and shafting for vertically suspended pumps will be supported by the motor thrust bearing.
Pumps that have mechanical seals will be arranged to facilitate seal removal.
Pumps may have either packing or mechanical seals, as determined by the application.
The characteristic curve (flow/head) will constantly decrease maintaining a uniform slope from the point of zero flow to the design point. All the identical pumps shall have the same characteristic curve.
The Contractor shall propose a suitable number of feed pumps having regard for availability and reliability requirements and shall be supplied with all necessary auxiliary equipment. Provided that the Contractor's proposed  arrangement  permits  boiler  drum  levels  to  be  adequately  controlled  by  main  and  start-up, control valves installed at the inlet of each drum, the HRSG feed water pumps may be driven by constant speed electric motors or Variable Frequency Drive (VFD)/hydraulic coupling. All pumps shall be capable of operation either singly or in parallel whilst remaining inherently stable.
The rotating components shall be balanced to ensure minimum vibration throughout the entire speed and load range. The characteristics of the pumps shall be such that the closed valve head is approximately 120% of the pressure at rated output.
label: text

chunks.text:
Depending on EPC Contractor design, auxiliary  boiler(s) with  natural gas  or  back-up fuel  oil  might  be required to provide auxiliary steam during the start-up phase of the ST.
The auxiliary boiler(s) shall be of the flame/smoke tube or water tube type.
The  auxiliary boiler(s) shall have  the  characteristic of  frequent  start-up,  long  periods  between maintenance, start-up at any time and fully automatically controlled, operated and monitored via DCMS. The cold start-up shall also be initiated and monitored by the CCR operator without any intervention from a local operator.
The entire pressure part shall rest on a steel frame in such a way that free expansion in all directions is possible. The large water volume shall enable the boiler to adapt well to extreme load fluctuation.
The outer lining of the insulation shall be made by galvanized steel sheets.
Boiler protection and burner management shall be in accordance with NFPA 85 or EN 12953-7 and EN 267.
The steam pressure at the auxiliary boiler outlet shall be a result of boiler manufacturer preoptimization considering boiler size, steam temperature and boiler capacity. The related steam pressure shall depend on the steam-cycle optimization, which would be the minimum steam pressure.
Demineralized water shall be used as boiler make-up water which is supplied from the demineralization water plant.
Because of characteristic difference between start-up boiler and normal boiler, the water of this boiler can be drained completely and facilities for conservation shall be provided.
The platform and gallery of boiler shall possess enough strength and stiffness, and stairs shall be provided at operation, monitoring or maintenance locations.
The boiler shall be provided with the necessary observation ports, manhole for maintenance and explosion vents.
The  boiler  shall  be  provided  with  safety  valve,  vent  valve,  exhaust  piping  and  a  motor-driven  valve, silencers as necessary, etc.
Connections  for  measuring  of  parameter  of  steam,  water,  combustion  fuel  shall  be  provided.  Local instruments and remote instruments (in the control room) shall be used for boiler water level measuring, and the pressure, temperature and flow rate shall have indications in the control room.
An emission monitoring system shall be provided for the auxiliary boiler stack.
The technical requirements specified above  for the steam generators shall apply also for the auxiliary boiler(s) as far as applicable.
ASME stamp and NB registration is not applicable. Heat Recovery Steam Generator.
label: text

chunks.text:
The steam generators shall be of proven design and be designed, manufactured, constructed and tested in accordance with relevant internationally accepted standards, e.g. ASME as well as the latest editions of all applicable local and national laws, codes and regulations in effect at the time of contract award.
The HRSG shall be an outdoor, fully weatherproof clad, with cladding/insulation where necessary. The main pressure parts shall be arranged in the form of a self-contained construction and shall be of the selfdraining type.
The top (or side in the case of vertical HRSGs) galleries of each HRSG shall be provided with partial sun and weather canopies (including over the HP drum) to protect Plant operation and maintenance personnel from direct exposure to the sun. Instruments and electric panels shall also be provided with local suitable sunshades.
The HRSG shall be suitable for automatic start up, shutdown and normal operation from the Central Control Room.
The HRSG (and the steam turbine) shall be capable of sliding pressure operation to a minimum operating pressure that may be maintained in continuous operation.
The water side of each HRSG shall be cleaned after completion of erection by alkaline boiling-out with suitable  chemicals  in  accordance  with  accepted  chemical  cleaning  procedures.  With  respect  to  HRSG cleaning,  the  Contractor  shall  also  provide  in  its  offer  an  option  price  for  chemical/acid  cleaning  in accordance with accepted chemical cleaning procedures for the consideration of the Investor.
HRSG pressure parts exposed to exhaust gas in the cold section of the HRSG shall be selected from materials to achieve a minimum design life as per the applicable international standard/code. The HRSG design shall be such that the temperature of water entering any heat transfer section shall be above the exhaust gas dew point or acid dew point as the case may be.
Walkways,  ladders,  stairs  and  platforms  shall  be  provided  whereas  necessary  for  proper  operation, inspection  and  maintenance.  Elevator  shall  be  provided  to  access  top  area.  Interconnecting  platform between HRSG Units shall be provided if only one elevator is being provided for multiple HRSG units.
Design of the HRSG shall be based on factory built  modules or HARP type with as much equipment as practicable factory assembled. HRSG shall be made up vertical tube bundles which shall be top supported and attached to the steel frames and horizontal gas flow.
In the design phase of the HRSG, particular attention shall be paid to the exhaust-gas side pressure loss of the HRSG and of the stack and shall be minimised in order to realise a high efficiency factor of the gas turbine.
Each element and tube bank must contain tubes on a horizontal and vertical pitch, adequately supported and of suitable depth to enable easy cleaning. Any fins used must be solidly attached to the tube throughout the fin length.
Temperature measurements shall be provided in the transition ducting between GT and HRSG at different elevations to monitor temperature profile across the first row of tubes.
label: text

chunks.text:
A chemical dosing system shall be provided in order to maintain the proper boiler feed water chemistry and a steam sampling system in order to monitor the steam quality.
No drain pipes or venting pipes shall be concealed in the boiler insulation.
To be able to reach the upper headers of modules, manholes and/or handholes shall be installed at the top of  HRSG.  Access  doors  between  modules  with  a  coverable  manway  to  the  bottom  section  (location  of bottom headers and piping) to be included.
Steam drums, headers and major HRSG pressure parts shall be visually, radiographically and ultrasonically checked in accordance with the ASME codes for weld defects during all stages of manufacture and erection. The Contractor shall also undertake visual and random magnetic particle inspection (MPI) checks of small
label: text

chunks.text:
items (e.g. stub/nozzle to header connections). As noted earlier, the Contractor shall agree with the Owner, or  his  nominated  representatives,  an  inspection  and  testing  witness  and  hold  point  programme  for equipment or any other tests identified by the Owner or its representatives as requiring inspection and such a programme shall include provisions to ensure that the Owner or his nominated representatives are given adequate prior notice to attend the agreed inspections and tests. The design of each HRSG shall be such as to permit adequate access for welding and to ensure that the effective examination of all site welds is possible during fabrication and erection as well as later into the service life of the Plant.
HRSG may have supplementary firing (SF), if required. The additional power capacity achieved by SF must not exceed 10% of the Contracted Capacity.
Each completed boiler shall be subject to a hydraulic test using demineralised water and in accordance with procedures defined by the design codes and the insurers inspectors.
Design life criteria of 25 years (equivalent to greater than 200,000 hours) alternatively, design life can be done considering 300 cold starts and 1100 warm starts shall be applied to materials operating in the creep region, the most stringent requirement shall apply. The HRSG design shall allow for appropriate inspection, cleaning and repair access of pressure parts and all auxiliaries. The number of rows on single header will be selected as per supplier experience on similar HRSG applications and confirmed by fatigue and stress analysis.
All necessary installations for conservation during outages of the HRSG shall be included. For short periods wet conservation shall be used.
Variations in the temperature of the steam generator exhaust gas and the potentially associated corrosive environmental conditions shall be considered in the design of the extended surface tubing and back-end facilities such as LP economizers and preheaters which shall include for recirculation and bypassing and adequate hot/cold end corrosion protections (no damage for Acid Dew Point).
Design to consider and provide good accessibility for the inspection and repair of welding seams between individual pipe bundles and between heat exchanger pipes and collectors. Access openings and manhole will be provided at bottom on both side casing and top casing for each module.
HRSG design to provide the exhaust-gas side pressure loss of HRSG and of the stack shall be paid particular attention and shall be minimised in order to realise a high efficiency factor of the gas turbine.
A steam turbine bypass system shall be provided for each HRSG for three of pressure sections to allow fast and independent start-up and shutdown. The safety valves shall be provided for each pressure level as required by the ASME code.
The heat recovery steam generators shall be completely drainable and shall be designed so that in case of tube  or  bend  failure,  replacement  of  tube  shall  be  performed  without  dismantling  major  components according to the manufacturer's repair standards.
label: text

chunks.text:
Pipe wall thickness shall be dimensioned in accordance with DIN EN 12952 or equivalent ASME code. In this process, the Contractor shall select the next higher wall thickness from the series of standards.
The HRSGs shall be designed:
- for maximum utilization of the heat content of the gas turbine exhaust gases,
- for triple pressure steam generation and
HRSG stack shall have Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS) and related instruments.
The HP temperature at the HRSGs' outlet shall be controlled (defined by the contractor) for optimized power generation.
The HRSG's blow down rate shall be adapted accordingly so that the guaranteed steam quality will be met by the contractor.
All drums and pressure stages of HRSG shall be equipped with a BSE system (Boiler Stress Evaluator). The BSE system shall be connected to the DCS in order to visualise the stress data for the main components (such  as  HP,  IP,  LP  drums,  superheater/reheater  collectors,  LP  collectors  etc.).  These  data  serve  to
determine the remaining life cycle of the critical components and the optimization of the ramp functions for start-up and/or shut-down as well as for load change processes.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text: The Contractor shall provide a HRSG performance prediction computer model program specific for this project.  This  program  shall  be  capable  of  running  on  a  personal  computer  with  the  latest  version  of Windows operating system. The performance prediction program shall have the following inputs, and outputs, as a minimum:
label: text

chunks.text:
- -Gas turbine exhaust flow rate, temperature, and composition.
- -Terminal steam pressures for HP steam, Hot Reheat steam, and LP steam.
- -The temperature of the water being sent to the HRSG.
- -The temperature of the Cold Reheat at the terminal point.
label: list_item

chunks.text:
- -Steam flow, steam temperature, and steam pressure at the terminal points for HP steam, Hot Reheat steam, and LP steam.
- -Steam flow, steam temperature, and steam pressure of the IP steam.
- -Stack temperature.
- -HRSG  efficiency  (according  to  ASME  code,  calculation  based  on  temperature  differences  shall  not  be accepted)
- -Gas side static pressure drop.
The HRSG shall be foreseen with temperature measurements for both water-steam and gas side before and after each heat exchanger in order to facilitate the mapping of its performances.
Steam and Water Analysis System (SWAS) shall be installed for each HRSG separately, the SWAS system shall be designed for continuous monitoring and control of water and steam purity in the HRSG.
Heat recovery steam generator shall be provided separately for each gas turbine generator, which consists of following systems and components, but not limited to the following;
- Gas turbine exhaust gas duct system
- Pressure parts and steam drums
- Insulation and cladding
- HRSG associated piping, valves and fittings
- Vent and drain systems
- Blow-down system
- Flue gas ducts
- Main stack
- HRSG related electrical facilities
- HRSG related Instrumentation and control (I&C) system
- HRSG steel structures and platforms
- Provision of Online Heat Flux measurement
label: list_item
text

chunks.text:
The steam collecting drums (long, slim design) shall be designed in such a way that they withstand high temperature  gradients  resulting  from  fast  load  changes.  Greatest  care  shall  be  given  in  thermal  and mechanical design of the drums.
The drums shall be fusion welded and provided with all necessary internal distributors, baffles, shields, and internal piping.
Each HRSG evaporative section shall be provided with steam drum(s), each of adequate size to ensure stable operation under all normal load conditions and other single item trip conditions. The steam drums shall be sized to enable start up without operating any drain valves, except the one at the outlet of the superheater. Drum internals shall include steam and water separators to limit the mechanical carry over. The moisture carryover from the drum to the first stage of the superheater will be less than 0.1%. The moisture carryover after the first stage of the superheater should not be detectable.
Internal feed-water distribution along the drum length shall be provided. Internal distribution headers for the HRSG chemical feed and saturated steam sample connections shall be provided.
All  drums shall be fitted with leak free hydra step level indicators for both local visible indication and remote level indication.
The  drums  shall  be  equipped  with  steam  separators  for  maintaining  the  required  steam  quality.  The chemical balance of the steam circuit shall be controlled via the steam collecting drum. Suitable connections for a continuous blowdown and an intermittent blowdown shall be installed. Chemicals shall be added in such a way that a uniform distribution of the chemicals is ensured by means of an internal distributing pipe over the entire length of the drum or by feeding them in the feed water line directly before the inlet into the drum.
Internal distribution headers for the water and saturated steam sample connections shall be provided. All openings including down comers, steam outlets, manhole covers, and instrument and gauge connections shall be covered to provide a moisture-proof seal during shipment.
Hinged manholes shall be provided in both heads of all drums as per ASME PG-32.3 criteria. An insulated steel cover shall be provided to cover each manhole.
The steam drum shall be of large diameter to handle water level fluctuates during quick start-up without excessive dumping of water. At start-up, no water carryover from the drum is allowed.
As far as the dimensioning of the drums is concerned, load rejection for isolated operation also shall be considered.
Distribution and collection manifolds and headers shall be designed to provide uniform water or steam flow to all passes of the tube bank. Manifolds shall allow free expansion of tube banks.
label: text

chunks.text:
All tube ends, header and other pressure part opening shall be cleaned and free of scale and foreign matter and shall be suitably sealed to prevent the entrance of foreign materials during shipment and during the expected storage period until erection. These parts shall not be sealed at the time of treatment, in order to provide proper inspection and complete removal of all cleaning medium.
All stand pipes or branch stubs shall be welded to the headers in the workshops.
Test  pressure  connections,  test  thermometer  wells,  temperature  recorder  connections,  sampling connections etc. required for complete testing of economizer, superheater or reheater performance, and for all permanent instrumentation shall be provided. Inspection stubs shall be provided on large bore pipes and headers for borescope observations.
Addition of oxygen provision shall be considered in feed water downstream of FFLP (feed forward low pressure drum) or upstream of SALP (standalone low pressure drum).
HRSG drums shall be furnished with hinged manholes according to ASME standards. An insulated steel cover has to be provided to cover each manhole.
label: text

chunks.text:
All HRSG sections shall consist of vertically arranged finned tube banks located within the steam generator casing.
Each element and tube bank shall contain tubes on a horizontal and vertical pitch, adequately supported and of shallow depth to enable easy cleaning. Any fins used shall be solidly attached to the tube throughout
the fin length. Tubes sheet clearance as per HRSG OEM design should be between 10 - 12 ft (not more than this) apart but can be increased or decreased according to CFD studies.
All superheater, evaporator and economiser tubes shall be solid drawn seamless and not electric resistance welded.
The superheater and reheater tube metal design shall include provision for all operational and system imbalances.
HP superheaters and the reheaters shall be provided with a spray type steam attemperator for superheater and reheater steam temperature control. The steam temperatures on the turbine inlets may not exceed the values specified by the turbine manufacturer.
The attemperator spray water control valves and automatic block valves, all temperature sensing elements, transducers, and controls for controlling steam temperature shall be furnished under these specifications.
If there is a low point, valves and fittings for automatic drainage shall be installed.
The spray coolers shall be designed and installed in such a way that the steam and water flows cannot result in inadmissible vibratory stress.
All pressure parts shall be designed and constructed to withstand the forces and moments applied through the HRSG pipework under all service conditions.
All the HRSG heating surfaces shall be designed considering the requirement for off-load water washing and CO2 blasting and a number of local drain points.
The design shall incorporate measures to prevent sagging and vibrations occurring in the tube banks.
The  design  economizer  outlet  feed  water  temperature  shall  be  sufficiently  below  the  saturation temperature at the design operating pressure to prevent steaming throughout the entire operating range. The economizer shall be designed to allow recirculation of feed water in the economizer, only if needed to prevent steaming at low loads.
The  low-pressure  economizer  design  temperature  shall  be  high  enough  to  prevent  corrosion  of  the economizer surfaces due to condensation of the corrosive flue gas components.
For superheaters and reheaters, Gr91 should only be used for steam temperature up to (including) 585°C, for steam temperatures higher than 585°C Gr304H shall be used.
EPC Contractor shall provide details of all the HRSG pressure parts materials by indicating the respective maximum design pressure and temperature for each grade and type of material for Owner review and approval before start of any material procurement and fabrication.
All heat transfer surfaces have to consist of compact banks of spiral and serrated finned.
label: text

chunks.text:
Adequate tube spacing have to be provided to avoid plugging and fouling and to allow for proper cleaning and maintenance.
All alloy tubes have to be seamless and truly circular (carbon steel tubes have to be also seamless), free from blisters, scale and mechanical defects. The tubes have to be made of suitable materials and with a suitable wall thickness.
Tube ends to be field welded (including any factory installed stubs in drum or headers) have to be carefully machined to suit the weld joint design used and have to be adequately protected from damage due to shipping,  handling  or  rusting.  Tube-to-tube-header  weld  joints  have  to  be  full  penetration  welds  on superheaters and reheaters. Tube-to-tube-header weld joints may be full strength welds for the remaining heating surface.
Distribution and collection manifolds and headers have to be designed to provide uniform water or steam flow to all passes of the tube bank. Manifolds have to allow free expansion of tube banks. Tube headers have to be arranged to permit replacement of tubes and cleaning of both internal (chemical cleaning during commissioning) and external surfaces.
Connections between tube banks and manifolds or headers have to be made outside the gas path.
All tube ends, header and other pressure part opening have to be cleaned and free of scale and foreign matter and have to be suitably sealed to prevent the entrance of foreign materials during shipment and during the expected storage period until erection. These parts have to not be sealed at the time of treatment, in order to provide proper inspection and complete removal of all cleaning medium.
The minimum water inlet temperature to the condensate preheater have to be selected to be sufficient to prevent corrosion of the economizer and preheater surfaces due to condensation in the flue gas.
The high, intermediate and low pressure superheaters and the reheater (if applicable) have to be of the vertically/horizontally  arranged  finned  tube  type  with  all  piping  connections  between  the  sections  of welded  construction.  The  superheaters  and  the  reheaters  have  to  be  drainable  and  access  have  to  be provided such that individual elements or tubes can be removed or repaired with minimum disturbance.
HRSG will be designed and shall have places where temperature measuring devices can be installed in order to be able to measure between-module and bundle temperature across the width of the path on either side of the HRSG.
label: text

chunks.text:
Steam temperature control equipment shall be provided to ensure that the HRSG metal temperatures and steam temperature at the steam turbine do not exceed the design rated conditions under all methods of Plant operation. Regulation of the final steam temperature by the control of desuperheater water injection will be the prime method of control.
Design shall be done in such a way that even in the event of low differential pressures between the injected water and the superheated steam as well, a complete atomization of the injected feed water  has to be ensured so that no drops can get into the turbine -a  sufficiently  long  evaporation  section  have  to  be provided. By means of a suitable design, it has to be ensured that no water that has not been atomized yet can get into the steam pipe at any time when the control valve is closed.
If there is a low point, valves and fittings for automatic drainage have to be installed.
The spray coolers have to be designed and installed in such a way that the steam and water flows cannot result in inadmissible vibratory stress.
Each HRSG steam output shall be controlled in response to signals from the Central Control Room DCS. The steam temperature control loop of each HRSG shall respond accordingly.
label: text

chunks.text:
Boiler and superheater and reheater safety valves for all steam circuits shall be  provided and shall be specified in accordance with design code recommendations. Each safety valve shall be fitted with its own vent-pipe, silencer and suitable drain and shall be designed and constructed to prevent back-pressure from interfering with the proper operation of the valve. Alternatively, the Contractor may propose a combined relief system with silencers in accordance with ASME B31.1 provided that discharge piping is designed with sufficient flow area to prevent the blow-out of steam of other fluid and that the Contractor provides the Owner or his nominated representative with its design calculations during the detailed design phase of the Project;  the  Owner's  preference is,  however, for a combined relief/silencer system for HP superheater safety relief valves to be separate from a combined relief/silencer system for HP drum safety relief valves. The safety relief valves for deaerators shall be arranged separately from a combined safety relief systems due to the lower pressure. IP Safety valves shall be arranged in a similar manner.
All safety valves have to be designed to avoid undue stresses and damage to the pressure systems for all operational conditions, including dynamic procedures.
Pressure relief arrangements shall be provided on the HP steam main before each boiler stop valve for the purpose of venting steam during start-up and pressure excursions; an electrically operated relief valve (ERV) shall be provided. In addition a suitably arranged start-up bypass system shall be used provided that such an arrangement allows the correct warming of individual HRSG pressure parts before the HRSG is connected to any common headers and that the DCS system will accommodate the use of the bypass system for HRSG and ST start-up purposes and pressure excursions (a start-up vent valve may also be provided for initial  start-up  of  the  HRSG)  and  enables  independent  HRSG  operation  during  start  up,  load  changes, shutdown and trip conditions. In the case of an electrically operated relief valve, this valve may discharge
into the silencer of one of the safety relief valves as long as this does not impair the operation of the safety relief valve or may discharge into the blow down tank. The relieving capacity of this valve shall not be included  in  the  overall  safety  valve  relief  capacity  of  the  HRSG.  Safety  valve  silencers  shall  feature protection to prevent operational and maintenance personnel from exposure to high temperature steam.
The following quick start-up vent arrangement can be considered in order to avoid using an electrically operated relief valve:
- Each Start Up vent will be designed as follow:
- HP motorized relief valve if it is needed
- HRH start-up vent sized for 30% base load flow at 100% base load pressure (Quick Opening)
- LP start-up vent sized for 100% base load flow at 100% base load pressure (Quick Opening)

The electric motor operated valve shall each be provided with a smaller electric motor operated bypass valve to enable downstream warming and pressure equalization. The electric motor operated valve which is a high pressure (PN>63 bar) valve of 150 mm bore and above may be provided with a smaller electric motor operated bypass valve connected to its valve body.
HP steam from each HRSG shall be routed to a steam header feeding the steam turbines.
Double isolation valves operating as master/martyr shall be provided on all boiler emptying, venting and drain lines when the design pressure is greater or equal than 40 barg or the design temperature is greater or equal than 425ºC. Main vent and drain valves which are associated with the automatic Plant start-up and shutdown shall be motorised for remote operation. In the case where motor operated drain/vent valves are provided, there will be one motorised valve and one manual valve in series.
All pressurised main drains in the boiler area shall be connected to the HRSG blowdown vessel/tank.

A supplementary firing system shall preferably utilise grid burners but register type will be considered.
The burners shall be designed to provide maximum efficiency and uniform heat distribution to the HRSG firing natural gas only. The burner system shall be of a proven design and include equipment necessary for its safe, efficient and reliable operation.
The automatic fuel control system shall ensure satisfactory and safe combustion under all HRSG normal modes of operation.
All ignitors and flame monitors shall be capable of being maintained or replaced whilst the unit is online.
For Supplementary firing system, Dry Low NOx burners shall be provided, with maximum 47.7mg NOx/ MJ (LHV).

The blowdown water shall be discharged from the blowdown vessel outlet to waste after being suitably cooled (if required) and any flash steam shall be discharged to atmosphere via
label: text

chunks.text:
a vent in a safe location. Each blowdown tank shall also accept HRSG emptying and other such drains. A silencer shall be provided if applicable.
Blowdown and drain facilities which shall be designed to operate on both intermittent and continuous basis. The blowdown lines shall be designed for periodic flows of up to 3% mass flow (at MCR) as well as continuous flows of between 0.5% and 1.0% of MCR.

All HRSG drums shall each be furnished with two fully (online) maintainable local water level gauges at each end of the drum. These shall be of the bicolour type.
Remote boiler water level indication and recording shall be provided for all the steam drums and these shall include a temperature and pressure compensating mechanism.
Dedicated drum level measurements shall be provided for drum level control which will also use steam flow and feed flow meters and temperature and pressure compensation appropriate to maintaining control of level within the defined range under all operating conditions and transients in normal operation.

chunks.text:
Each HRSG shall have a single flue stack of sufficient height and diameter such that it is self-sustaining, i.e. its lift due to temperature differential shall be equal to or greater than the sum of all losses and shall comply with relevant regulations.
The  stack  shall  be  provided  with  all  necessary  steel  structures,  silencer,  stairways,  staggered  access, ladders,  with  safety  cage  and  resting  platforms  minimum  every  8  m,  holes  for  gas  sampling,  pressure, temperature, walkways and platforms and with all necessary emission measuring devices, access/observation doors, drains, grounding and lightning installations and aircraft warning equipment.
The HRSG stack shall pe provided with blinded flange connection to be ready for future carbon capture connection.
The efflux velocity shall not be less than 15 m/sec at normal operating loads.
The  stacks  shall  be  carried  out  completely  with  circular  or  hexagonal  shaped  reinforced  concrete foundations supported by piles (if needed as per EPC Geotech report) as per the structural analysis.
Each HRSG unit bypass/ main stack shall have common Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS) and related instruments and safe access to CEMS.
Each  bypass  stack  shall  have  a  single  flue  stack  of  sufficient  height  and  diameter  such  that  it  is  selfsustaining, i.e. its lift due to temperature differential shall be equal to or greater than the sum of all losses and shall comply with relevant regulations.
The  by-pass  stack  dampers  shall  be  of  single  blade  construction  and  be  designed  to  avoid  distortion problems and ensure tightness and minimal leakage of all dampers throughout the life of the Plant. The dampers shall be equipped with seal air fans systems.
The by-pass stack damper blade shall be of material suitable for the structural, load carrying components under the specified project operation temperatures, the internal liner on the diverter blade upstream shall be  made from at least  Grade 321 stainless steel and shall have a minimum thickness of 3 mm (in the horizontal section and blanking plate).
The by-pass stack damper shall be arranged as a diverter damper such that when the stack is closed the HRSG duct is open and shall be provided with durable remote indication of open/closed positions.
The by-pass stack damper material selection shall be done in order to achieve:
- Longer lifetime
- High resistance to load changes
- Handle high temperature corrosion effects
- Take into account long-term creep, fatigue effects, gas turbine load cases and specified cycles
For  the  bidding  purpose,  Contractor  shall  consider  60  m  and  45  m  height  for  main  stack  and  bypass respectively from ground level.
The minimum height of the stacks shall be as per the environmental requirements and the maximum stack height shall be approved by the Competent Authority.

The casing have to fulfil the following requirements:

- Gas tightness
- Temperature resistance against high exhaust gas temperatures
- Sufficient elasticity to withstand the temperature gradients in the start-up and shut-down phases and during load change processes of the gas turbine
- The flue gas duct shall be designed for unlimited alternating expansion stresses in the range between the lowest ambient temperature and the maximum operating temperature. Possibly installed elements (e.g. deflector plates) may not limit the frequency of temperature changes and shall withstand hot exhaust gas passed into the cold plant. They shall be vibration-free and heat-elastic.
- Internally  insulated  ducts  and  HRSG  casing  shall  be  lined  with  shop-installed,  blanket insulation with steel liners. Carbon steel liner shall be provided where gas temperature is less than 400 deg.C. There shall be no gaps in the liner that would expose the internal insulation to the exhaust gas. The insulation/liner system shall be designed to support normal live loads during access to the interior of the HRSG without damage. Liners (including field installed liners) shall be installed such that the edge of the downstream liner is under the upstream liner.
- Special care shall be taken when determining liner thickness, stud diameter, and stud spacing for velocity higher than 27.4 m/sec or high turbulence areas.
- For internal insulation, insulation linings shall be cover with 12 gauge (2,6 mm) or thicker steel metal liner in areas where the average gas velocity is greater than or equal 45 m/sec. Where the average gas velocity is less than 45 m/sec 14 gauge (2,0 mm) or thicker steel metal liner shall be used on the floor, and 16 gauge (1,6 mm) or thicker steel metal liner shall be used on the side walls and the roof. Studs shall be attached to the casing by the shielded metal arc weld (SMAW) process or a stud gun. Internal lining subject to personnel walking during maintenance periods (lower horizontal surfaces) shall be 14 gauge (2,0 mm) or thicker. Insulation joints shall be staggered throughout multiple layers.
- Robust duct liner, duct casing, and foundation supports.
- A design that permits the raising and lowering of panels and headers to gain access to repair leaks. Gas and steam side access opening locations and sizes also should be specified. An enhanced access to individual module panels and to the tube-to-header welds

The Plant shall be equipped with a system for the continuous extraction and monitoring of selected samples from  the  HRSG  steam  and  water  circuit.  The  selection  of  sample  locations  and  analysers  shall  ensure adequate  observation  and  control  of  steam  and  water  chemistry  limits.  The  measurements  from  the analysers shall be recorded on the power station DCS. A manual sampling facility shall be provided for each sample.
The Plant shall be equipped with chemical dosing systems to control the boiler and feedwater chemistry.
Each chemical dosing system shall comprise all equipment for the safe, reliable and efficient operation of the dosing systems, including bunds, segregated chemical drains, appropriate ventilation and emergency eye wash and deluge shower units.
Usage of AVT (O) or OT (oxygenated treatment) shall be preferred instead of AVT (R).
Sampling systems should have redundant sample coolers.

SCR system shall be provided for HRSG to meet the NOx emission limitations specified in this OTS and EIA study recommendations.
Same shall be based on aqueous ammonia system complete with all sub-systems such as unloading, storage, forwarding etc. with necessary safety requirements.
The detailed description of the system offered along with schematics shall be submitted as part of proposal for Owner's review.
label: text

chunks.text:
While the main component of the SCR process is the catalyst, the full system shall contain a variety of components and subsystems. The catalyst shall be housed in a large reactor. If required, flue gas shall be directed to and from the reactor by large flues that may contain control and shut-off dampers as well as flow distribution devices and static mixers, depending upon project-specific requirements. The reactor shall be a gas-tight steel enclosure that permits the flue gas and reagent to contact the catalyst for the required  residence  time  to  achieve  design  performance.  The  reactor  structure  shall  include  internal stiffeners and a catalyst support system that also permits rapid loading and unloading of catalyst materials. The design shall include a sealing system to avoid flue gas bypass and catalyst cleaning devices if required (soot blowers and/or sonic horns). The system will be designed with proper gaps/clearances to guarantee no risk of plugging and easy maintenance. The reactor shall be configured for horizontal flue gas flow.
Catalyst formulation, pitch and sizing are the keys to successful SCR system application and performance. Although  catalyst  formulations  are  proprietary,  the  most  common  components  in  steam  generation applications  use  titanium  dioxide  with  small  amounts  of  vanadium,  molybdenum,  tungsten,  or  a combination of other active reagents. Formulation shall be matched to the flue gas conditions.
label: text

chunks.text:
Catalyst types and materials typically fall into one of three categories:
- base metal
- zeolite and
label: text
list_item

chunks.text: Most steam generation experience has been with base metal catalysts. These are typically described as titania-vanadia and can be provided as plate type, honeycomb type, or corrugated fibre type. All three are similar in performance characteristics and can be supplied in a homogeneous construction or as a coated active layer on a base material. The plate type catalyst shall be manufactured from a roll of stainless steel expanded metal substrate. The homogeneous catalyst shall be paste-pressed into and around the substrate to form a catalyst plate of 0.9 to 1.0 mm thickness. After cutting to length, correctly sized undulations, to set the catalyst pitch, shall be formed onto each plate prior to final processing and drying. The completed plates shall then be assembled into encased blocks; multiple blocks shall be packaged into a metal- frame shipping module. Homogeneous honeycomb catalyst shall be formed in an extrusion process that produces a catalyst log approximately 152 x 152 mm in cross section with the selected honeycomb cell pitch and cut to proper length. After final processing and drying, the logs shall be assembled and packaged into metalframe shipping modules.
label: text

chunks.text: The  reagent  (aqueous  ammonia)  subsystems  shall  include  truck  unloading,  storage,  vaporization  or hydrolysis equipment, flow control, dilution air supply and mixing, and reagent distribution and injection components. Each subsystem shall contain piping valves, instrumentation, controls and safety equipment for appropriate ammonia handling and material compatibility. The dosing pumps shall be designed for 25% concentration aqueous ammonia, however flexibility to work with different concentrations such as 20%, 29% shall be provided. A critical part of SCR system design is integration into the overall HRSG system. This is particularly important because the SCR system design must accommodate swings in flue gas temperature while maintaining the desired performance, without affecting HRSG operation. Overall HRSG pressure drop including SCR will be considered for the design. The ideal gas temperature for NOx reduction ranges from 371°C to 399°C and can be optimized further during SCR detail design.
label: text

chunks.text:
The reagent to be used in this project shall be aqueous ammonia.
Ammonia slip at NOx guarantee conditions (15% O2, dry) shall be 2ppm average slip during the operation period of 25 years.
label: text

chunks.text:
Aqueous ammonia is a diluted form of ammonia with NH3 dissolved in water to form NH4OH.
Aqueous ammonia is typically available at concentrations up to a maximum of 29.4% solubility limit at ambient conditions of 30ºC and 1atm by weight of NH3 equivalent. This concentration is also frequently described as 26ºBé, where degree baumé is an alternate measurement of density. The storage tanks shall be horizontal/vertical and shall be rated at 138 to 345 kPa. Tank material shall be stainless steel to avoid startup problems associated with rust. Storage system design shall also incorporate a containment basin in case  of  a  ruptured  line  or  vessel.  The  ammonia  storage  capacity  shall  be  for  21  days  of  operation considering Operation Point 1 (RSC conditions with plant operating at full load).
label: text

chunks.text: For the ammonia reaction with the NOx, one mole of ammonia is required to reduce one mole of NOx and thus the required injection mole ratio of ammonia to NOx is equal to the required NOx reduction plus the ammonia slip value (ppm) divided by the inlet NOx concentration (ppm). The control system logic shall use a  feed  forward and  feedback input with this equation,  along with a flue gas flow input, to provide the ammonia flow control demand. The feed forward input shall be determined by either an inlet NOx analyzer or a curve-generated value for repeatable HRSG conditions. The feedback input can use the output of an SCR outlet analyzer or the stack continuous emissions monitor (CEM). Because of the hazardous nature of the ammonia there shall be several interlocks that will interrupt ammonia flow upon upset conditions.
label: text

chunks.text: SCR  reactor  performance  is  influenced  by  the  distribution  of  velocity,  temperature  and  reacting  gas components through the catalyst bed. The degree of a given profile uniformity can be generally described
label: text

chunks.text:
by the coefficient of variation (Cv), commonly reported as the percentage of the profile standard deviation from the arithmetic mean value.
Cv = 100%
SCR  reactor  distribution  goals  for  flow  and  molar  ratio  are  commonly  stipulated  in  this  coefficient  of variation format. A temperature distribution criterion is the exception by typically being expressed as a minimum and maximum (±) deviation about the arithmetic mean. The goal is to achieve the most uniform profile possible at the SCR catalyst inlet for NOx concentration, ammonia to NOx molar ratio, velocity and temperature. The degree of uniformity required for each parameter, coupled with the physical space and arrangement limitations presented, drives the level of complexity and  intricacy of a successful design. Numerical or physical flow model studies shall be used to determine the necessary distribution devices to achieve the desired uniformities.
label: text
