chunks.text:
A water treatment plant shall be supplied to provide all the demineralised water requirements of the Plant including, but not necessarily limited to, evaporative coolers, wet compression if applied and make-up for boiler blowdown.
The water treatment plant shall treat product water from the desalination plant by means of ion exchange System (regeneration unit and neutralisation units to be marked as required) with most advanced features with proven demonstrative commercial scale plant including regeneration unit and neutralisation units.
The demineralisation plant shall have 3 x 50% streams. Each 50% stream shall be sized such that two streams running simultaneously provide, as a minimum, a net supply rate equal  to  1.5%  of the steam generation flowrate of the HRSGs in addition to any other plant demands.
For demineralization plant, three (3) x 50% Mixed Bed Polishers having more than 24 hrs operations cycle between  regeneration  or  CIP  will  be  provided  when  the  feed  water  TDS  is  20  mg/L.  During  normal operation  when  gas  firing,  two  (2)  MBP  will  be  on  operation  simultaneously,  the  others  will  be  on regeneration or stand-by EPC Contractor is free to propose Electrodeionization (EDI) for final polishing instead of Mixed Bed Polishers.
Three (3) MBP feed pumps will be provided. During normal operation, two (2) feed pumps will be operated, one(1) will be regeneration or stand-by.
The system shall be complete with a regeneration or CPI system consisting of sodium hydroxide and either hydrochloric  or  sulphuric  acid  storage  facilities,  assorted  chemical  feed  pumps,  and  mixing  agitators, neutralisation basin and associated waste water pumps.
The demineralisation system shall be designed to treat water with a maximum conductivity of 0.1 µS/cm (@25ºC) and the maximum content in the permeate from the 2 nd  Pass of SWRO desalination plant will be limited to 20 mg/l of Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) for all the feed water conditions given in the OTS.
The make-up water system, incl. its storage tank, shall be designed sufficient to cover a black start of at least one desalination unit. The make-up water storage tank shall have a minimum storage capacity of at least 24 hours continuous plant operation at full base load with fuel Gas.
The  system  shall  be  arranged  for  automatic  control  of  operation,  regeneration  of  the  mixed  bed  ion exchange resins and neutralisation of the wastewater.
The guaranteed quality of the demineralised water product at the outlet of the mixed bed shall be as a minimum as per Electric Power Research Institute, or EPRI, USA:
- Specific conductivity (Continuous)µS/cm (@25ºC) ≤ 0.1
- Sodium as Na +  (Continuous) mg/l ≤ 0.003
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
- Chloride as Cl -  (Commissioning or Troubleshooting) mg/l
≤ 0.003
- Sulphate as SO4 -- (Commissioning or Troubleshooting) mg/l ≤ 0.003
- Total silica as SiO2 (Continuous) mg/l ≤ 0.010
- Total Organic Carbon (TOC) (Continuous or Grab sample) mg/l ≤ 0.3
label: list_item
text

chunks.text:
The ion exchange vessels shall be of welded mild steel construction In case of the ion exchange vessels shall be rubber lined in an approved manner with a minimum rubber thickness of 3 mm.
Ion exchange vessels and bulk chemical storage tanks shall be designed to BS 5500, or ASME 8, or an equivalent internationally  recognised  Standard.  The  demineralised  water  tank(s)  shall  comply  with  an acceptable internationally recognized Standard.
The maximum linear velocity of water through the ion exchange vessels shall be 40 metres per hour. All of the internal metallic fittings of the vessel shall be manufactured from stainless steel.
The vessels shall include sight windows to enable the resins within the vessel to be observed. The sight glasses shall be at the resin interface when separated and at the resin upper surface. Any other sight glasses required for operational reasons shall be provided.
A resin trap shall be fitted to the outlet of each vessel, which shall incorporate a differential pressure gauge.
label: text

chunks.text:
Treated water reserve storage tanks shall be provided with a minimum usable capacity of 48 hours of normal usage at full load. Two (2) x 50% Demineralized water tanks shall be provided, each with minimum 24 hrs storage of normal usage at full load when Gas firing. All necessary valves, fittings, pipes, etc. required to integrate the storage tanks into the system shall be provided.
Demin tanks shall be provided to allow for outages, maintenance and tanks shall be interconnected by pipework. The tank water shall be protected by filter and CO2 absorber as appropriate means to prevent the water coming in contact with atmospheric CO2.
Demineralized tanks will have absorbers to prevent CO2 ingress.
label: text

chunks.text:
All chemical handling equipment shall be bundled such that any chemical spillage is contained.
Sulphuric or hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide shall be used as the regenerants. A bulk storage tank for each regenerant shall be provided with a minimum capacity of 7 days' consumption at maximum Plant output. Each storage tank shall be equipped with a bund having a volume of at least 110% of the capacity of the tank. If hydrochloric acid is used, the acid bulk storage tank shall be equipped with adequate fume extraction facilities. The CIP equipment shall be supplied with permanent piping.
label: text

chunks.text: The existing effluent sumps and effluent control system shall be used for effluent disposal. The pH of the effluent shall be adjusted if necessary to between pH 6 and pH 9 prior to discharge of the effluent. The control of this discharge shall be co-ordinated into the overall plant effluent control system.
label: text

chunks.text:
Regeneration/CIP inhibition and control signals shall be co-ordinated between the two streams so that no operational conflicts occur.
An automatically resetting throughput  meter shall determine regeneration of the mixed bed unit. This meter shall adjust the volume to be treated by the unit in accordance with the quality of the distillate feed
water using a pro-rata calculation comparing the actual quality of the feed-water with the design quality of the feed-water.
A continuously recording conductivity meter shall be installed on the product output from the unit. This same position shall provide a source for a manual grab sample.
The  Water  Treatment  Plant  will  be  supplied  with  proprietary,  purpose-designed  systems  for  control, monitoring and protection. Such systems will be designed to function independently of each other but will be interfaced to the DCS for supervisory level to allow co-ordinated operation of the Facility.
label: text

chunks.text:
The H2 generation plant including all required auxiliaries shall be sized for plant normal consumption plus 10% margin. The plant shall have storage for 24 hours of normal consumption of all generators or the required amount for 4 times filling of the largest turbine generator installed. Storage shall be provided by using either storage tanks or H2 bottle clusters (each cluster has 20 cylinders).
Particular  attention  shall  be  paid  to  the  explosion  risk  in  the  design  and  construction  of  the  plant.  All electrical equipment shall be explosion-proof; this applies also to lighting and power outlet sockets. All components of the entire H2 plant including ladders, platforms, etc. shall be earthed.
The feed water for the electrolyser shall be supplied from the demineralization plant. Cooling water shall be taken from the station closed circuit cooling water system.
Where components are in contact with hydrogen under pressure the resistance of the material to hydrogen embrittlement shall be considered.
Pumps,  compressors,  electrolysis  units,  etc.  shall  be  provided  with  stand-by  units.  Purging  lines  with Nitrogen shall be provided for each equipment in case of shut down or maintenance of the plant.
The H2 generation plant shall be housed in a separate building.
A control system shall be provided which enables that H2 generation and filling shall be operated in a fully automatic manner.
Hydrogen generation plant shall be equipped with firefighting system as per NFPA standard. Hydrogen seal oil units shall be complied to requirements of NFPA850, Cl:7.7.4.4 (i.e. automatic sprinkler system or foam system).
The plant shall be described in detail by the EPC Contractor supported by flow diagrams.
label: text

chunks.text:
Rumah  and  Nairyah  Plant  will  be  designed  with  Zero  Liquid  Discharge  (ZLD)  which  means  that  no emissions  of  liquid  effluents  other  than  uncontaminated  storm  water  will  be  discharged  to  the environment. Hence, all  wastewaters will be directed to an evaporation pond  where the accumulating sludge will regularly be disposed.
The EPC Contractor shall present a concept for the wastewater treatment plants and demonstrate the major wastewater treatment steps including the corresponding maximum and normal flows.
label: text

chunks.text:
Sanitary wastewater drainage from the entire plant area shall be treated in a sanitary treatment plant.
Sanitary  wastewater  shall,  to  the  extent  possible,  be  plant  internally  re-used  after  its  treatment  for irrigation purposes. Its sludge shall be used, if applicable, as fertilizer.
For this reuse, the PME's and NCEC's General Environmental Regulations and Rules for Implementation apply.
label: text

chunks.text: The sanitary wastewater system shall consist of a piping system with inspection manholes every 60 m and at each change of direction. Lifting stations shall be provided as necessary.
label: text

chunks.text:
Other waste waters shall be collected for treatment. Rainwater or any surface water flows from areas which are likely to be contaminated in any way shall also be handled as wastewater for treatment. All treated wastewaters should be re-utilized with means of demineralization and re-used within the Plant consumers.
The wastewater streams must be separated according to their origin and/or type of pollution and the type of treatment that they require. Thus, as a minimum requirement, the following separate treatment systems shall be provided:
label: text

chunks.text: All  oily  wastewaters  shall  be  pre-treated  at  least  by  oil  separators  and  further  adequate  and  suitable treatment steps in order to meet the requirements of Water Treatment System; and
label: text

chunks.text:
All  industrial  and  process  related  wastewater  such  as  from  (chemical)  cleaning,  from  ion  exchange regeneration, from rinsing and flushing processes, from chemical storage areas and workshops etc. must be  treated  in  an  applicable  wastewater  treatment  plant,  that  is  adequately  and  suitably  designed  to neutralize and detoxify the particular wastewater and to meet the requirements of the water treatment system.
Wastewater  drainage  to  the  respective  wastewater  treatment  plants  shall  be  using  pipes  made  of customary and proven materials in adequate diameters for the likely maximum quantity of  wastewater flow  in  the  pipes.  In  the  case  of  differential  height  constraints,  pumping  stations  must  be  installed  in adequate numbers. In the case of using cesspools, intermediate storage is allowed. Cesspools are to be emptied by vacuum loaders, which are also part of the scope of supply.
Following the pre-treatment of the waste waters, the filtrate shall be routed to the Water Treatment System for further treatment, demineralization and re-use of the water as per the process requirements mentioned above. The reject water of the Water Treatment Plant will be eliminated in means of Evaporation Ponds. In order to optimize the Project lifecycle costs, EPC Contractor may utilize forced evaporation systems for the non-utilized waste waters. Selection and operation of such systems should not lead to any environmental risks in terms of spreading of the Dissolved solids within the neighbouring areas around the evaporation pond and EPC Contractor will be requested to demonstrate the performance of such systems during the Defect Liability Period.
Wastewater from GT washing processes shall be collected separately and suitable arrangement shall be provided to pump the same to road tankers for disposing the same externally at defined disposal areas.
label: text

chunks.text:
Clean and uncontaminated rainwater from the entire plant Site including rainwater from roofs and the paved areas of the plant shall be collected, guided and discharged in plant storm water drainage system. The plant clean storm water drainage system shall be capable of carrying corresponding discharge of flows from  the  offsite  area  at  its  upstream  end.  The  system  shall  consist  of  piping  system  with  inspection manholes  every  60  m  and  at  each  change  of  direction.  The  dirty  or  contaminated  rainwater  shall  be collected  and  treated  in  a  separate  system  and  shall  be  disposed  to  evaporation  pond.  Dedicated distribution to ensure for uninterrupted service & instrument air supply with interconnection in case of emergency backup.
If Owner allows, Storm water can be re-used in the process plants or infiltrated to the soil at the plant area. In case the Contractor shall considers an overflow of the storm water, an appropriately designed infiltration pond shall be implemented at the site. Bidder has to prove that this separate pond is able to infiltrate the storm water and the permeability of the soil enables seepage of the storm water without harm to any adjacent installations.
For this purpose, the Contractor shall consider for his design additional treatment facilities to increase the water recovery from the treatment plant. The optimization of water re-use and evaporation is subject to the Owner's approval.
label: text

chunks.text:
The  evaporation  pond(s)  shall  be  sized  sufficiently  in  order  to  accommodate  all  Plant  effluents  and considering the evaporation rate at site during all seasons of the year.
All effluents shall be treated by neutralization, oil separation and solids removal before final discharge to the evaporation pond, where applicable.
The ponds shall be sectionalized and accessible by wheel loaders to allow cleaning and maintenance of the pond(s) during operation.
The Bidder shall provide the basic design of the evaporation pond(s) with the proposal to as well explain the operation during rainy conditions.
Waste water pond complete area bottom as well sides shall be provided by HDPE liner & if maintenance is required concrete tiles shall be provided with access steps & ramp.
However, for Storm water pond shall be provided gravel filling at bottom and sides to be provided with a HDPE liner with concrete tiles with O&M accesses.
The evaporation pond shall be divided in two chambers. Lifting station, vehicular access as required shall be provided.
label: text

chunks.text:
- A) EPC shall equip the Plant with centralised chemical storage area(s).
- B) The capacity of each chemical should have a volume that is equivalent to 7 days of full load operation as minimum inventory under normal operation dozing. For the Long lead chemicals, the storage capacity shall be 30 days.
- C) The preparation tank and dosing tank for each chemical shall have a capacity of 7 days under normal operation dosing rate.
- D) The chemical storage area shall be either indoor or sheltered with a roof.
- E) The tanks and pumps shall follow the redundancy concept as defined in the other section of this document.
- F) Chemicals shall be transferred by filling pumps to local dosing tanks, where required, each with a volume equivalent to at least 48 hours operation at Plant full output. The lime slurry tanks comprise of 2 x 100% and shall run continuously.
- G) The chemical storage  tanks  shall  be  bunded  (each  chemical  separately)  to  ensure  that  an accidental  leakage  is  retained  within  the  bund.  The  bund  shall  be  of  sufficient  volume  to contain 110% of the entire contents of the contained tanks. Contractor shall propose a system to prevent incorrect or incompatible chemicals delivered into the wrong storage vessel.
- H) EPC  shall  provide  an  air  conditioning  room  for  the  chemical  truck  drivers  to  wait  during chemical unloading and out of their protective clothing before and after they discharge the chemicals in the storage tanks.
- I) Storage  facilities  for  hazardous  chemicals  shall  be  subject  to  review  and  comment  by  the Owner at the design stage of the Project.
- J) The chemicals supplied for this Plant shall be of food grade /non-carcinogenic. All chemicals used in the project shall be in line with the EIA study recommendations.
label: list_item
text
list_item

chunks.text:
The water quality shall be in accordance with the latest revisions of all relevant laws and regulations of the country, as well as with the latest revision of the relevant World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines. The  potable  water  capacity  shall  be  sufficient  to  serve  all  operational  and  operation  personnel requirements under all normal operation circumstances and according to best practices, plus a 20% safety margin.
Any material used for the potable water system and storage tanks shall meet the requirements of the WHO in regard to harmful effects on the drinking water.
Paints (manufacturer and type) and internal coatings of potable water steel tank(s) shall be subject to Owner's Engineer approval.
Plant potable water system shall include but not be limited to potable water storage tanks, chemicals dosing units,  pumps  (2x100%),  pipework,  valves,  fittings,  instrumentation,  controls  and  other  associated accessories for distributing potable water. The Potable water from remineralisation system shall be stored in Potable Water storage tank of suitable capacity and shall be distributed to all consumer points through Potable Water distribution network within Power plant facility.
Potable water lines and discharge header shall be of High Density Poly Ethylene (HDPE) type. QA/QC must be in place to inspect the quality.
label: text

chunks.text:
The  Facility  shall  be  provided  with  compressed  air  to  supply  instrument  air  and  service  air  required throughout the respective Plant Facility. The equipment shall be designed with appropriate redundancy for the Plant Facility and shall consist of heavy-duty air compressors.
Compressed air system for instrument air and service air requirements consisting of air compressors, air receivers, air driers, air filters, piping, valves, fittings, instrumentation, controls, etc.
3x50% compressors shall be provided for Power Plant. The instrument air system shall consist of 2x100% filtering skid and 2x100% twin tower heatless regeneration type air dryers. Two air receiver tanks each of minimum 15 m 3  capacity shall be provided. Compressed air system pipeline shall include automatically water trap with proper distance and the line shall be designed with proper slope so to avoid any water accumulation in the system.
The air release valves in the standpipe system header shall be installed at the highest point of the piping.
The compressed air mains shall be routed to ensure integrity  of  supply  to  minimise  the  possibility  of damage. In this context the air distribution system shall be based on ring main systems. Piping material shall be stainless steel for instrument air. Plastic piping on any part of the system is not acceptable.
The compressed air system will be designed according to ISO 1217 at reference conditions. The grades will be suitable for compressed air used in process control instruments. The kind of air quality (dirt /water / oil) in a facility of this type is classified according to ISO 8573-1.
The instrument air distribution system shall normally operate independently, but to rationalise on the compressor installation, a valve and protected interconnection may be made upstream of the dryers, to
allow the service air supply to supplement the instrument air supply, in the event of failure of more than one instrument air compressor.
An air distribution ring should be provided for each compressed air facility.
The service air system shall include hose stations and fixed connections for air tools.
label: text

chunks.text:
The compressors will supply air to a common sectioned header. From this header instrument air shall pass to the driers before entering the distribution pipework. Service air shall be supplied upstream of the driers once the air has been cooled.
The system  will  be  designed  such  that  the  failure  of  a  single  component  will  not  result  in  the  loss  of compressed  instrument  air  supply.  Dedicated  distribution  to  ensure  for  uninterrupted  Service  & instrument air supply with interconnection in case of emergency backup.
label: text

chunks.text:
The compressors shall be heavy duty, water or air cooled, oil-free with carbon rings, driven by electric motors and provided with air-cooled intercoolers.
Each  compressor  unit  shall  be  capable  of  continuous  operation  under  the  specified  service  condition, without injurious heating and shall operate without objectionable noise or vibration.
The Contractor shall provide intake filter and silencer, necessary gauges and all accessories and controls required for a complete air compressor unit to operate satisfactorily. Factory-set relief valves shall also be provided to protect the compressor in case of automatic control failure.
label: text

chunks.text: Three water or air-cooled after coolers with condensate separators shall be provided, each capable of cooling the rated compressed air capacity of one compressor to a temperature of not more than 10°C higher than the incoming air temperature. Water separator and drain with automatic trap and bypass shall be provided.
label: text

chunks.text:
The compressed air shall be sufficiently dry to prevent condensation occurring in the control air system under any operating conditions of temperature and pressure.
Two (2) 100% twin tower desiccant heatless air dryers together with outlet filters shall be provided. The air dryers shall dry the air to a dew point of at least -40°C.
All filters for the control air shall be provided as required. Suspended particles within the air shall not be larger than 5 microns.
label: text

chunks.text:
Each air receiver shall have sufficient capacity to enable the Plant to be shut down in a safe and controllable manner and enable standby compressor plant to come into operational service without reduction in air supply.
All air receivers shall be designed, assembly and inspection in accordance with ASME Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code Section VIII and shall be provided with factory-set safety valves, pressure gauges and bottom tap drains.
label: text

chunks.text:
The design, materials, manufacturing, installation and testing of the fire and explosion prevention as well as  the  firefighting  equipment  shall  be  selected  based  on  local  codes  and  standards  and  comply  with requirements of the relevant Government Authority.
The Codes and Standards of the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) latest edition shall apply in case the above-mentioned codes and standards do not cover all subjects concerning the fire detecting and firefighting systems or are less stringent than NFPA Codes and Standards.
The Plant shall be protected against fire by a comprehensive fire detection, alarm, and protection system. The fire detection system shall provide the means to detect fires, provide visual and audible alarms both locally and remotely, and, where required, actuate the firefighting system.
Fire protection for the power plant shall mainly comprise civil structures (fire areas, fire walls, etc.) fire detection  and  fire  alarm  system,  fire  water  storage  and  pumps,  fire  main  ring  system  with  outdoor hydrants, indoor hydrants, extinguishing systems (sprinkler, water spray, foam, human safe gas, etc. as applicable) and portable fire extinguishers.
Fire  alarm  and  detection,  fire  protection  and  firefighting  system  for  the  entire  Plant  complete  with  all necessary piping, pumps, valves, fittings, control panels, etc. shall be provided in accordance with NFPA standards and the local guidelines. Firefighting system shall be provided with flow meter to undertake pumps performance test. All fire detection and protection equipment and components shall be UL listed or FM approved and shall be suitable for use in fire detection and protection purposes.
Hydro test of the complete ring shall be performed during commissioning for fire water piping.
Surge test shall be conducted in pre commissioning and commissioning of the piping.
Use of compatible soil for refilling and compacting of the firewater piping for underground piping.
Underground firewater piping shall be checked for thrust blockings so to prevent water hammering effect.
Required reserve storage capacity for fire  water system shall be made available in the clarified water storage tank / sump.
The design and installation of the fire protection and alarming systems shall be in accordance with the recommendation of the NFPA standards and shall be approved by an insurance company. Some standards are listed below as good engineering practices and with any additional requirements of local authorities and shall comply with the local regulations in respect of supplier, installer and system approval.
label: text
list_item
text

chunks.text:
Water supplies for all the firefighting services on the Facility Site shall be provided via a common system of firefighting pump house and underground hydrant ring mains.
The firefighting water reserve shall be sufficient to provide firewater to the largest risk area plus 500 GPM for a period of 2 hours with the necessary fire hoses as per NFPA. The water shall be potable water from independent fire water tank. The tank shall provide water to the firefighting pumps, which shall comprise a 100% duty electrically driven fire pump and a 100% duty diesel driven pump. The pressure of the ring main hydrant system shall be maintained by suitably sized 2x100% electrically driven jockey pump.
The pumps shall supply water to an outdoor buried ring main system for the Plant, which shall extend to all areas of the Site, with extensions into all the main buildings and complete with all necessary ancillaries to enable any fire hazard location to be covered by two hydrants. It shall provide water supplies to all fixed firefighting installations as well as to the fire hydrants and hose reels.
All fire pumps shall be provided with proper recirculating line PRV and flow meters to test the pumps as per NFPA-25. Fuel level of diesel pump shall be monitored in control room.
Provision shall be made for future extensions without the need to shut down fire protection to operating plant. A blanked off section isolating valve shall be provided at each future tie-in point.
Two water supply connections from pipework following physically different routes, from the water storage tank into the firefighting pump house at different locations, shall be provided and similarly, the supply connections to the hydrant ring main shall exit from the pump house at two different locations and shall connect to the hydrant ring main at two separate locations. The system shall be arranged such that either water supply route and connection can be used, via either fire pump, discharging via either ring main connection,  to  supply  firefighting  water  to  any  risk  area  via  alternative  routes.  Easily  accessible section/isolating valves shall be provided throughout the system to achieve this objective.
An adequate number of vent and drain valves shall also be provided to permit the venting and draining of the complete system without the splitting of flanges or similar practises being necessary.
The below ground pipework shall be nonferrous and shall be manufactured from materials such as GRP, FRP or HDPE, selected to ensure long term durability under the test/design pressure and site conditions. Underground firewater pimping shall be checked for  thrust blockings so to prevent  water hammering effect. Above ground pipework shall be hot dip galvanised in accordance with appropriate standards.
Weatherproof hose/equipment cabinets shall be provided and located in the same manner, and containing the same equipment, as those provided for the existing plant.
label: text

chunks.text:
Fire protection shall be provided per the standards referenced herein. Where it does not contravene these requirements, the fire protection shall accord in all respects with any existing fire protection provisions.
In addition, the Contractor shall comply with the provisions described below.
All deluge valves, whether automatic or otherwise, shall be located at a safe distance from the fire risk on an exit route so that they can be operated manually if required.
The deluge valve assemblies shall be fitted with an alarm bypass test connections for a water flow alarm switch and shall be made on the water supply side of the system and provided with control valve and drain for alarm piping as per the requirements of NFPA13,Cl:8.17.1.3. This arrangement enables the end user to carry out the manual testing (dry test) of the system without discharging the water into the protected area. Therefore, it shall be installed in portion of alarm connections/bypass test connections in the deluge valve trim assembly which will get activated and provide the signal of water flow equal or in excess of discharge from one sprinkler/nozzle.
Environmentally  friendly  fire  suppression  systems  (e.g.  FM200)  shall  be  provided  for  the  internal protection of the GIS substation relay and protection panels, and the CCR cubicles and panels. Clearly visible signs shall be posted at each area to warn personnel that the particular room/area is protected by a gas flooding system.
As per the NFPA-70, Cl:760.133, the fire alarm circuit cables shall not be placed in any other cable, cable tray,  compartment,  enclosure,  manhole,  raceway,  outlet  box  or  electric  light,  unless  it  is  separated  by barriers or spacing required by NFPA-70 based on specific application type.
The water spray nozzles in STG building shall be installed in a manner without any obstruction to its spray pattern on the protected equipment.
For transformer deluge valve assemblies, all automatic water spray systems shall be provided with a local alarm complying with requirements of NFPA 15, Cl:6.4.1.1
For administration building, sprinklers to be installed in all parts except the areas which can be omitted as permitted by NFPA13.
label: text

chunks.text:
Hand-held and portable extinguishers shall be provided. The extinguishing agent shall be selected to suit the particular fire hazard. The extinguishers shall be provided at standpipe and hose stations and other key locations in the buildings and in any area normally occupied by personnel.
Painted markings and signs shall be provided to direct attention to the location of extinguishers and to their use.
label: text

chunks.text:
The fire detection system shall cover the entire Facility.
Fuel  gas  detection  shall  cover  areas  of  the  Plant  where  the  risk  of  damage  due  to  gas  accumulation  is considered to be significant and as required by local regulations.
The master panel shall be mounted in the CCR with repeat indication in the gatehouse. Repeat panels shall also be provided to cover individual buildings where necessary.
A complete self-monitoring, fully addressable fire detection and alarm system shall be provided for the power/desalination plant.
The alarms in the protection zones, interfaces with the DCMS and local repeater panels shall be provided for  information  and  protection  of  the  operators.  The  system  shall  interface  with  the  other  local  fire detection protection systems, as appropriate, to inform the control room operators of fire elsewhere on the site.
The preferred format of the indicator and repeater panel mimics is a schematic diagram based on a site layout plan.
Audible alarms shall be installed in all locations and shall have a pronounced range and volume distinct from the background noise. All siren/fire alarms shall be of adequate output level to be audible above the normal working conditions.
A zone-wise thermal type detection system shall be supplied to alarm and shut off the oil supply to any burner front involved in an external fire.
label: text

chunks.text:
The fire detection equipment shall comprise heat, smoke or gas detecting devices to suit the risk. The fire detectors shall be located at strategic positions adjacent to the plant to be protected and also in suitable positions in the general station areas. Smoke detectors shall be spaced as per NFPA -72.
Linear fire detectors shall be provided on each major cable tray run areas without ventilation.
The  air  heater  fire  detection  system  shall  comprise  a  series  of  temperature  detectors/thermocouples installed in the air outlet duct from the air heater(s). The detectors shall be arranged to detect abnormally high  temperatures  and/or  high  rates  of  change  of  temperature  in  air  leaving  the  air  heater(s).  Fire protection shall be arranged for manual initiation.
Air duct detectors to sense the presence of combustion products in air handling systems shall be installed in the ventilating and air conditioning duct systems. They shall shut down fans and actuate smoke dampers or other controlled equipment upon detection of combustion products so as to prevent re-circulation of smoke.
label: text

chunks.text: Manual call points shall be provided at all exits and stairwells and at locations not greater than 50 metres apart  in  turbine  areas,  HRSG  areas  (at  each  level)  and  all  other  buildings.  A  striker  shall  be  provided adjacent to all call points  to facilitate  breaking  the glass. As per NFPA72, Cl:17.14.8.4, the manual  pull stations shall be located within 1.5m of each exit doorway.
label: text

chunks.text:
The  Contractor  shall  provide  auxiliary  fire  protection  equipment  in  accordance  with  local  regulations including,  but  not  limited  to  fire-resistant  clothing,  compressed  air  breathing  apparatus,  fire  blankets, goggles, helmets, stretchers, portable gas detectors, etc. in such quantities as are compatible with power plant requirements.
The  sprinkler  system  in  the  warehouse  area  shall  be  designed  based  on  the  hazard  classification  for flammable & combustible liquids and complying with requirements of NFPA - 13.
label: text

chunks.text:
A  complete system of warning  instruction and directional signs for safe and orderly evacuation of the buildings shall be included and shall be inscribed in Arabic and English or be pictorial.
Fire exit doors shall comply with NFPA 850. Wirings of exit signs shall comply with requirements of NFPA 70, article 700 so to provide maximum availability in case of fire.
As per OSHA's guidelines, 'exit doors must be unlocked. Employees must always be able to open an exit route  door  from  the  inside  without  keys,  tools,  or  special  knowledge. 'Construction  materials  used  to separate an exit from other parts of the workplace must have a one-hour fire resistance-rating if the exit connects three or fewer stories and a two-hour fire resistance-rating if the exit connects four or more stories.
The signs shall include DC illuminated exit signs indicating the nearest safe exit from the buildings.
label: text

chunks.text: Hose reels connected to the plant fire main shall be provided at strategic locations within the Plant and its buildings.
label: text

chunks.text:
HVAC systems shall be designed, installed and commissioned in accordance with the latest applicable codes of the following:
- o ASHRAE
American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air Conditioning Engineers.
- o SMACNA
Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors National Association.
- o NFPA
National Fire Protection Association.
- o ARI American Refrigeration Institute.
- o ANSI American National Standards Institute.
- o AABC Associated Air Balance Council.
All systems shall be designed and installed to provide acceptable environmental conditions for each area. The conditions of temperature, humidity, air movement and air filtration shall be controlled as required in the respective areas in summer and winter.
HVAC  systems  serving  critical  areas  such  as  Control  Rooms  shall  be  provided  with  duty/standby  air handling and mechanical cooling plant to ensure continuity of operation.
HVAC systems shall be arranged to shut down in the event of a fire alarm, seal supply and extract ducts as required  for  the  application  of  clean  agent  fire  suppression  systems  and  start  up  smoke  control pressurization systems. Provision shall be made in all plant areas for the venting and clearance of smoke and fumes in the event of fire, by means of roof vents or extract fans.
All systems and components shall be suitable for the design life of the Plant, and be designed for minimum life cycle cost and complexity, consistent with functionality, ease of maintenance and reliability.
For all general cases the HVAC  systems  the ambient design conditions shall be  as  ASHRAE recommendations to suite the site conditions. The HVAC systems shall be designed to obtain the internal conditions and system redundancy as indicated in the section  4.2.15.17 of the OTS Part A. Central airconditioning systems having humidity control may be provided with air handling units for fresh air supply. These units shall be provided with cooling coils and steam humidifiers to handle the full dehumidification/humidification load for the central system, with dew point control. Fresh air-cooling coils shall have 10 per cent margin on heat transfer surface to cater for periods of abnormally high humidity. Face air velocity shall not exceed 2.0 m/sec.
Humidification shall be by electric powered steam generators with proportional control and steam lance injection.
The sound levels in plant and occupied areas shall not exceed the following, with HVAC systems only in operation:
- Switchgear Rooms/Relay Rooms
NC50
- Control Rooms/Offices/Prayer Rooms
- Workshops/Mess Rooms/Toilets/Corridors
NC30
NC45.
Sound attenuators shall be provided in duct systems, as required, to achieve the above sound levels.

chunks.text:
All HVAC units and systems shall be provided with local control panels for local manual/automatic control. The operation status such as alarms, humidity, temperature, fault indication, status indication of each air conditioning system shall be indicated and available at the local control panel and any individual fault signal results in a group signal, which shall be transmitted to the central control room.
In addition the following criteria shall be considered in the design of the HVAC system:
- (i) A general lighting level dissipation of 33 watts/m²
- (ii) Sensible and latent heat gains for occupancy should be allowed on the basis of one person per 10m².
- (iii) A minimum quantity of fresh air should be provided at the rate of 0.00125m³/s per m² of floor area or 12.5 l/s/person, whichever is the greater and this should be shown in the calculations. All equipment gains within each room should be allowed for in determining Plant capacities.
- (iv) Re-circulated air  should  be  filtered.  Air  from  areas  where  pungent  fumes  are  likely  to  be present should not be re-circulated.
Battery rooms should be air conditioned by self-contained air-conditioning units. The design of the air conditioning system shall avoid recirculation of air back into the battery room. These units should be of the non-recirculating type and sized to provide the internal conditions previously specified with a minimum of five air changes per hour. Duplicate extract fans should be provided, mounted at high level and positioned such that accumulations of hydrogen cannot occur. The fan units should be suitable for long life in the acidic environment.

Complete cooling systems shall be provided. The units and complete installation shall comply with ASHRAE 15 -Safety Code for Mechanical Refrigeration -and ASHRAE Guideline 3 for Refrigerant Leaks, Recovery, Handling and Storage Requirements.
Critical air-conditioning systems shall be provided with 100 per cent standby plant. Critical air conditioning systems are those which are essential for the continued operation of the buildings and allow continued occupancy of essential working areas.
HCFC refrigerants shall not be used.

Ductwork shall be fabricated, installed and tested in accordance with the latest SMACNA Standards. General supply  and  extract  system  ductwork  shall  be  of  galvanized  sheet  steel  construction.  Irrespective  of pressure/velocity classification, ductwork at low level in plant rooms and in areas subject to mechanical damage shall be constructed (as a minimum) to medium pressure standard.
All duct systems shall be complete with dampers to facilitate balancing and fire dampers. Splitter dampers will not be accepted. Access doors shall be provided as required for inspection/maintenance of dampers, fire dampers, instruments etc. Final connections to ceiling-mounted supply and extract terminals may be carried out in insulated flexible ductwork.
Extract system ductwork from battery rooms and chemical areas shall be of PVC construction.
High-pressure ductwork shall be pressure/leak tested. Low and medium pressure ductwork need not be tested, except where it is located outdoors.
The following ductwork shall be insulated:
- Fresh air ductwork
- Low Temperature supply and extract ductwork.
- Medium temperature supply ductwork.
- Ductwork in Electrical rooms, where it is subject to condensation.
Fire dampers to UL Standards and NFPA-90A shall be provided on ductwork systems passing through firewalls and floors, and as required for compartmentation of gas fire suppression systems.
Dampers shall be operated by fusible link and (re-settable) damper motor, suitable for actuation through the fire detection system and fire damper control panel. Smoke dampers for clean agent fire suppression systems shall be motor operated/solenoid actuated for closing and opening purposes. Damper status shall be indicated on the control panel mounted adjacent to the Fire Control panel.

All fresh air intakes on large central systems shall be provided with inertial type sand filters, with access sections behind. Small systems employing fixed volumes of fresh air shall be provided with sand louvres.
Primary  and  fresh  air  filters  on  all  systems  shall  be  permanent  metal  panel  washable  type,  dust  spot efficiency 20 per cent. A complete set of spare cells shall be provided for cleaning, along with coating fluids. Washing facilities shall be provided, with service water being used for cleaning.
Secondary air filters on medium temperature systems serving plant areas shall be replaceable bag filters, dust spot efficiency 50 per cent. Secondary air filters on low temperature systems serving offices/control rooms/electronic areas shall be replaceable bag filters, dust spot efficiency 90 per cent.
All  bag  filters  shall  be  supported  in  proprietary  mounting  frames  for  front  or  side  withdrawal.  The Contractor shall supply a sufficient number of replacement cells to last during the test periods and during the Defects Liability Period, with one complete set being provided at that the end of the Defects Liability Period.

chunks.text:
Electric overhead travelling cranes shall be provided for ease of dismantling and maintenance of major plant items in each Power Unit. The cranes shall be capable of lifting and accurately positioning all loads within their specified rating.
The cranes shall be designed, manufactured and tested to an internationally recognised standard suitable for their intended application.
label: text

chunks.text:
For guidance purposes, the following maximum crane speeds for the main turbine and other cranes should be considered:
- •
- Hoisting
4.0m/min
- •
- Trolley Travel 10.0m/min
- •
- Bridge Travel
25.0m/min
- •
- Creep speeds
5% of operating speeds
The cranes shall be capable of inching in all directions of motion at a speed of approximately one tenth of the maximum full load speed.
All plant and plant components requiring maintenance in excess of 0.5 tons shall be provided with a means of lifting by the use of cranes as defined above, electrically/manual operated hoists with runway beams or mobile  cranes.  Below  0.5t,  lifting  arrangement  such  as  hoists,  chain-pulley,  monorails  to  be  provided. Access for installation and lifting of the equipment below 0.5t shall be ensured.
The use of mobile cranes shall be justified by the Contractor and agreed with the Owner. In any event mobile cranes shall not be considered for lifts at a height of greater than 15m above the level at which the mobile crane is standing. Where the maintenance procedures prepared by the Contractor require more than three simultaneous lifts anywhere on the Facility permanent lifting facilities shall be provided for the additional lifts. Mobile cranes are not to be supplied under the scope of Contractor.
Runway beams shall be permanently installed above the plant requiring lifting devices, manual hoists may be transferred between runway beams.
All associated lifting beams and slings shall be provided.
The pump screening and stop log gate areas shall be serviced by a single permanently installed gantry crane operating on rails.
Risk study to consider also Crane equipment during design stage.

- Steam.

- Fuel testing.
- Demin water.
- Desalinated product water.

The laboratory shall also contain suitable office accommodation for chemists (1 office having 3-people occupancy).
The fully air-conditioned laboratory shall be equipped with counter flanges for demineralized water and for potable water supply from the local distribution systems. Operator desk and respective furniture shall be included along with suitable storage facilities.
Chemical and analysis of wastewater shall be collected and drained separately.

Analysis devices that will meet ISO standards and are compatible with international certification will be selected.
Analysis devices suitable for field measurements will be available in the laboratory (PH, Conductivity Meter, SDI, Hydrometer, Validation Devices).
Automatic sprinkler system protection shall be required for all new laboratories handling chemicals as per NFPA13, Cl:22.8.1.

chunks.text:
All shop/factory inspection and test activities shall be separately indicated in Contractor's Inspection and Test Plan. The Contractor must deliver to the Owner a detailed plan of the equipment that will be subjected to a Factory Acceptance Test before the shipment to site. The Owner reserves the right to include on that list the equipment that must be subjected to this type of test and the applicable hold points for the Owner.
The general approach shall be that all equipment and materials are tested and inspected in the shop or factory to the maximum extent possible and where technically feasible. The extent of testing in the shop shall be indicated in the Inspection and Test Plan. The Inspection and Test Plan, relevant checklists, and formats available at the workshop shall be included in the EPC Contractors Quality Plan. After the Purchase Orders between the Contractor and the different Suppliers and sub-contractors are signed the Owner must be informed about the schedule of manufacturing, and inspections and receive the applicable Inspection and Test Plan applicable for the manufacturing/assembly works.

chunks.text: Refer to Owners Specific Technical requirements related to welding qualification and inspections program.

chunks.text:
The tests shall be arranged to represent working conditions as closely as possible. Type Tests, when called for shall be made on equipment, which has previously passed its routine tests. Where Type Tests have been carried  out  under  previous  contracts  on  equipment  similar  in  all  essential  respects  to  the  equipment included in the EPC Contract, the Owner may waive the Type Tests on production of complete test records relating to the equipment concerned.
All instruments used shall have valid calibration certificates, and calibration data shall be made available to the Owner on demand. All the inspection, measuring and test equipment required for inspections and tests shall be provided by the Contractor.
label: text

chunks.text:
The GTs shall be tested separately at the Contractor's workshop or at any other suitable location approved by the Owner. The tests shall be carried out to ensure smooth and satisfactory operating of the Unit. The following tests shall be carried out as a minimum:
- All critical raw materials like compressor/Turbine castings, rotor forgings, blades/wheels/buckets  casting/forging  raw  material  test  certificates  shall  include  the detailed  foundry  stage  material  specification  required  Heat  treatment  details  either directly in the material MTC's and/or as a separate report.
- All  the  casting  material  used  for  compressor  mid/inner  casing,  turbine  shell,  diffuser casing, buckets/blades shall be examined for 100% RT/UT at rough machined condition and 100% LPI/MPI on final machined conditions.
- All the forging materials used for rotors and wheels shall be tested for 100% UT at rough machined condition and 100%LPI/MPI on final machined condition.
- Run out check and High-speed dynamic balancing test of the rotor to be conducted at factory.
- Parting plane gap measurement for Turbine and compressor casing
- All the base frame welding shall be tested for 100% RT/UT & MPI
- Final  assembly  compressor and  turbine  rotor  clearance  and  dimensional  checks  to  be offered for Owner witness
- Preliminary checks and settings of all equipment and system
- Starting sequence control equipment set and operation checks.
- Manual shut down sequences, emergency shut down and tripping sequence checks. Other trips and alarms shall be subject to simulated tests.
- The GT rotor with blades shall be operated, by a test drive at high speed; balance test of GT rotor with the blades will be done up to 111% of the rated speed in accordance with Supplier's standard and
- Operation and setting of overspeed trips shall be checked and adjusted as required.
The operating characteristics of the following equipment and systems shall be checked:
- Ignition and combustion systems
- Turbine cooling
- Lube oil system
- Barring gear
- Starting equipment
- Control
- Protection
- Motors, pumps and heaters
- Performance load test
- Solenoid valves, stop valves, control valves and relief valves.
- Thermocouples, thermometers, and gauges; and
- Pressure switches, temperature switches and limit switches
Insulation tests shall be carried out on all control panels. Prior to test, electronic instruments and similar items shall be isolated to prevent damage. The insulation resistance of the remainder of the equipment shall be measured at a minimum of 500 V during manufacture. After reconnection of all equipment the circuits shall be checked. Function/sequence tests shall be carried out which simulate as far as practicable the performance of the turbines. These tests shall include all automatic sequencing, protective gear and alarms.

The following Factory tests shall be carried out on the ST at the Manufacturer's works prior to dispatch to Site:
- Hydraulic  test  of  casing  (except  LP  casing)  and  piping,  hydraulic  tests  for  the  turbine casing shall comply with IEC Recommendation and OEM's procedures
- All the HP & IP Casting shall be checked for 100% UT on rough machined condition and MT after final machined condition, weld repairs shall be documented with defectogram. All the heat treatment details, including the weld PWHT after the casting repairs shall be part of the raw material test documents.
label: text

chunks.text:
- Hardness test on WC6, WC9 and C12A grade castings after the weld repair and PWHT shall be carried out and same shall be part of the Raw material test documents.
- All the forging raw material used for rotor/shafts, blades etc, shall be checked with 100% UT at rough machined condition and 100%MT on final machined condition.
- Residual stress measurement of the rotors forging after the final quality heat treatment shall be conducted to check the effectiveness of the implemented heat treatment.
- All the stationary and moving blades shall be checked for hardness, MPI and PMI
- Dynamic balance of rotor carried out with dynamic balance checked over the complete speed  range  up  to  maximum  allowable  overspeed  and  including  critical  speeds.  The balancing weight and its distribution shall be properly recorded.
- Overspeed test: The turbine rotor shall be subjected to an overspeed test for a period of at two minutes at a minimum speed of two percent (2%) above the maximum calculated overspeed that would occur by the sole action of the overspeed trip device.
- HP, IP Casing assembly with Rotor -Clearance between the Radial and axial alignment of the inner casing and out casing to be checked and the same shall be performed as part of site assembly process for LP casing..
- Radial and axial blade/fins clearances in the assembled turbine shall be checked
- Casing bolts identification and tightening procedure verification
The no-load mechanical test at Site shall be performed as follows:
- Detailed  test  procedures  shall  be  submitted  by  the  Contractor  and  are  subject  to  the Owner's approval
- Initial steam conditions and operating vacuum shall be as close to the rated figures as practicable
- When sufficiently  warmed  up  a  one-hour  test  run  shall  be  made  at  maximum  speed. Bearing temperatures and vibration readings shall be recorded
- Vibration readings shall be  taken over the  whole speed range at intervals of  100 rpm starting  at  idle  speed  and  proceeding  to  maximum  speed  and  vice  versa,  with  special attention given to readings at rated speed. Every individual test shall last at least one minute. Testing shall not be performed close to the lower critical speeds
- Governor response shall be checked; and
- Overspeed and all protective devices shall be checked and adjusted where necessary.

chunks.text:
The supply, fabrication and erection of all pipework shall comply with the requirements of ASME B31.1, ASME  B31.3,  or  alternate  code  as  approved  by  the  Owner.  Pipework  for  the  GT  shall  comply  with International Standards. All butt welds shall be full penetration welds with complete fusion between weld runs and base metal. The following tests shall be carried out on welds (both Shop welds and Site welds):
- All  the  Pipe  and  fitting  material  for  the  critical  piping  and  HRSG  piping  shall  be  only procured from the well-known manufacturers, approved by the Owner.  The hardness testing and material heat treatment shall be clearly specified in the inspection program, which shall also to be witnessed by the Owner approved third party inspection services at the mills or at the fabrication workshop.
- EPC  Contractor  shall  use  the  proper  elbows  and  fittings  for  all  the  piping  system, particularly  for  the  high  temperature  steam  turbine  drain  system.  If,  any  site/shop manufactured bends are used, then same shall be post forming heat treated (PFHT) as per clause 129.3 of ASME B31.1 code as applicable.
- Visual examination of all welds to the requirements of ASME Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code Section IX relevant piping design codes.
label: text
list_item

chunks.text:
- Ultrasonic  or  Radiographic  and  surface  flow  examination  on  all  pipe  butt  welds  and branch  welds  to  the  requirements  of  ASME Boiler  &  Pressure  Vessel  Code  Section  IX relevant  piping  design  codes.  The  Owner  reserves  the  right  to  elect  one  of  the  two methodologies of inspection depending of the welds to be inspected. However, for the Butt welds of thickness of 60 mm and above shall be tested either by X-Ray or by Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing (PAUT) methos instead of Gamma rays due to its limitation. If PAUT method is selected, demonstartion block as same as welding & material being tested is necessary in additional to code required standard calibration blocks.
- 10 Percent (10%) magnetic particle examination of all fillet welds.
- Hydrostatic test to the requirements of ASME Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code Section IX relevant piping design codes as applicable.
- The minimum requirements in terms of type of inspections and percentage of inspections must  always  as  minimum  fulfil  the  requirements  of  the  Design,  Manufacturing  and Inspection Code. Furthermore, turbine lube oil, control oil and jacking oil piping systems butt welds shall be 100% RT tested, irrespective of the design code requirements. All the fillet and attachment welds shall be 100% PT tested.
- Over  the  minimum  NDT  requirement  as  specified  in  the  design,  Manufacturing  and Inspection code as above, EPC Contractor shall conduct 10% minimum volumetric NDT per welder per system in order to evaluate the in-process weld repair rate for each welder.
- All the variable and constant load hangers supplied for the plant piping system shall be tested for 100% performance testing at the manufacturing shop as per MSS SP-58. Springs used for the hangers shall be subjected to scragging, cramping test and load vs deflection tests.
- All the pipe and fitting supplied to site shall be clearly traceable with respect to the heat number and original raw material test certificates.
- EPC Contractor to prepare the welder wise/system wise/material wise weld rejection rates and welder performance monitoring report for all the welders involved either in the manufacturing  and/or  site  erection  activities  and  same  shall  be  submitted  for  Owner review and approval on weekly basis.
- EPC  Contractor  shall  include  or  depute  one  qualified  welding  Engineer  for  every  20 welders  working  at  site  and/or  manufacturing  shop.  The  Contractor/sub-contractor welding Engineer and/or deployed NDT company shall share the real time NDT results on daily basis to the Owner for review.
Piping and piping support inside GTG package is designed and fabricated and tested in accordance with the specified code and standards, or equivalent (JIS code).

chunks.text: Weld defect acceptance levels shall be in accordance with ASME Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code except that lack of root fusion or incomplete root penetrant will not be permitted.
label: text

chunks.text: Welding and inspection in both shop and Site shall be in accordance with AWS Standard or equivalent for Building Construction. Where only partial inspection is required the location of the joints selected for testing shall be agreed by the Owner. Should any of these welds prove to be defective on inspection, the number of welds to be tested in that system shall be twice the number originally specified. Should any of the  second  increment  welds  prove  to  be  defective,  then  all  the  welds  in  that  system  shall  be  tested. Irrespective of the code and drawing requirement, any butt welds in the load bearing members of the HRSG and Steam Turbine building structures shall be tested for 100% volumetric NDT.
label: text

chunks.text:
All castings, forgings and wrought products shall be subjected by the manufacturer to chemical analysis, material  tests  and  inspections  in  accordance  with  the  appropriate  American  Standard  except  where otherwise agreed  by  the  Owner. Inspection should be scheduled in order  to detect defects as early as possible,  to  avoid  unnecessary  delay  in  manufacture  and  delivery  of  the  Plant.  In  case  of  a  rejection
influencing the delivery time, written and certified notice must be given in due time to the Owner. The Owner reserves the right to examine and witness acceptance tests, prior to and following weld repairs and subsequent post weld heat treatment, mechanica l tests etc, at the material supplier's works. Weld repair procedures are subject to approval of the Owner.
HP and IP casing of steam turbine are manufactured and tested according to EN. For the HP & IP rotor forging  material,  OEM  maker  standard  is  acceptable.  However,  during  the  project  execution  stage, EPC Contractor/OEM to provide the actual material details including the forging raw material test certificates from the forging supplier.
label: text

chunks.text: All pressure vessels shall be designed, manufactured and tested in accordance with ASME Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code or other accepted international Code. The vessels will be subject to inspection and certification by the Owner's Insurers. The Owner reserves the right to verify or witness any activity required by the Technical Specification. Pressure vessels for the GT shall comply either with International , ASME Standards or European Pressure Vessel Guideline.
label: text

chunks.text:
The boiler Plant shall be designed, manufactured, and inspected in accordance with ASME Boiler & Pressure Vessel Code Section 1 Power Boilers. The boiler Plant will be subject to inspection and certification by the Owner's Insurers. The Owner reserves the right to verify or witness any activity required by the Technical Specification. Irrespective of the ASME Section requirements, all the tubular parts butt welds either in the manufacturing shop or at erection site of the HRSG shall be subjected to minimum of 20 % of volumetric NDT and Grade.91/92 material welding shall be tested for 100% volumetric NDT. All the welding involved in  the  flue  gas  ducts  shall  be  subjected  10%  MPI/LPI  as  applicable  for  the  material  of  construction. Insulation of any pressure parts and duct works at site, shall only be conducted after the satisfactory NDT examination and Hydrotest as applicable.
The  supplier  shall  qualify  all  bends  involved  in  the  tube  banks  with  a  proper  mock-up  qualification including the post forming/bending heat treatment requirements as mentioned in PG-19 & 20 of ASME Section 1 code as applicable. Copy of such mock up qualification records shall be part of EOMR/Manufacturing Quality Dossier.
Additionally, the list of tight bends (less radius) which requires PFHT (post forming heat treatment) as per ASME Section 1, PG-19 & 20 shall be provided for Owner review. The ovality of hot bends shall be within the 5% and the thickness difference between the extrados and intrados of these bends shall be within the 10% of wall thickness.
Supplier shall design and manufacture the HRSG pressure parts with a very minimum number of dissimilar welding requirements.  Supplier shall complete all the dissimilar welding at the manufacturing shop instead of site welding. Any direct welding of high temperature stainless steel tube material with CSEF (Creep strength ferritic steel material) of grades. T91/T92 is not acceptable. Instead, supplier shall design the same with intermediate transition tube material of 'Inconel grades' or the 'buttering' of the Gr. T91/92weld edges with Inconel filler material shall be considered to avoid the PWHT of stainless-steel tube material.
Furthermore, while designing such dissimilar material welding, supplier shall ensure that  these welds should not fail at the weld fusion line cracks during the operation phase of the plant due to differential expansion of the different material at all the loads HRSG is subjected to.
label: text

chunks.text: Any Austenitic stainless-steel tubes of 'H' grades (like TP304H, S303432/Super304H, TP347H/HFG) used in the final SH & RH modules of the HRSG shall be welded with the matching process parameter filler wire like ER304H/ER308H in accordance with qualified and Owner approved WPS & PQR documents. The usage of 'L' grades filler material for any high temperature application is prohibited.
label: text

chunks.text: All  castings  and  forgings  shall  comply  with  the  requirements  of  this  Technical  Specification  and ASME Boiler  &  Pressure  Vessel  Code  B16.34,  ASME  B31.1  or  other  international  accepted  Code,  as
label: text

chunks.text:
applicable to the service of the valves. Main steam and HRH system Steam Turbine inlet stop, and control valves  casting  shall  be  checked  for  RT/UT  in  rough  machined  condition  and  MT  after  final  machined conditions. All the major and minor weld repairs shall be documented with defectogram and same shall be part of manufacturing quality dossier. All valves shall be subject to hydraulic test at 1.5 times the PN rating of the valve. All the valves shall be back seat (as applicable) and seat leakage tests shall be conducted at the manufacturing workshop as per the applicable design and testing codes. In addition, valves supplied with butt weld ends shall be subject to ASME B16.34 or radiographic or ultrasonic examination for a length of 75  mm  from  the  prepared  weld  tip  and  magnetic  particle  examination  of  the  weld  tip  profile  PT examination  after  welding  will  be  applied.  Valves  for  the  GT  shall  comply  with  ASME  Standards  or equivalent Japanese or EN Standards.
All the valves casting of pressure class 900 and above shall be tested for 100% volumetric examination on body and bonnet. All  the  valves  forging  of  pressure  class  1500  &  above,  shall  be  tested  for  100%  UT examination.  All  the  valves  seat  face,  hard  faced/stellated  area  shall  be  100%  LPI  tested  after  final machining.
All the control valves shall be performance tested to verify Hysteresis, Repeatability, dead band, linearity, Sensitivity, accuracy, operating time, fail safe position, flow direction, Cv test for one size/per type etc. Type test certificates of standard Cv & trims shall be submitted for Owner review. In absence of any type test certificates or for project specific designs, Cv tests shall be witnessed Owner or its representative.
Safety Valves and Safety relief valves shall be subjected to 100% Pop up test at the manufacturing shop, in additional to standard body and seat leakage tests.
label: text

chunks.text:
All castings and forgings shall comply with the requirements of this Technical Specification. In addition, the radii,  changes  in  section  and  butt  weld  ends  of  the  castings  shall  be  subject  to  PT  examination  unless otherwise agreed by the Owner. Castings shall be subject to hydraulic test at 1.5 times the design pressure.
The high-pressure feedwater pumps impellers casting shall be volumetric tested after rough machining at the foundry and/or pump manufacturing shop. The NDT/RT sketch for the impeller shall be provided along with pump manufacturing ITPL.
Pump and compressor rotors shall be subject to ultrasonic examination in the rough machined condition and magnetic particle or dye penetrating examination in the final machined condition unless otherwise agreed by the Owner based on the pump manufacturer standard inspection procedure. Dynamic balance shall be carried out on the completed rotor as per Gr2.5 of ISO 1940 and performance tests carried out on the completed pumps. If selected OEM is able to technically justify the reason of inability to conduct the reference test in its premise, other QA methods will be discussed and applied, acting reasonably by both parties.  Pumps, fans and compressors shall be factory tested with their contract motors or test motor, however  Owner  needs  to  approve  for  any  test  motor.  The  main  Feed  water  pumps  and  Condensate extraction  pumps  shall  be  tested  for  NPSH  test  (one  per  type),  in  additional  to  the  code  required performance testing.
label: text

chunks.text: Each air ejector shall be tested to demonstrate compliance with the air extraction capacity required by HEI Recommended Practice for the design of Surface Type Steam Condensing Plant.
label: text

chunks.text: Running test will be done as per the manufacturer's standard.
label: text

chunks.text: Principal items to be examined for compliance with the requirements of this Owner Technical Specification are main girders, end carriages and crab structure, hoist drums, hooks, ropes, slings and shackles. All the butt welds in tension flanges, web plates and rope drums shall be tested for 100% RT. All the butt welds and fillet welds between the tension flanges and webs shall be tested for 100% LPT/MPI. The equipment provided is subject to inspection and tests by the Owner during the course of manufacture and on completion in order to ensure compliance with this Technical Specification. Inspection and Testing During Manufacture
The following tests, at minimum shall be performed, as applicable, during the course of manufacture:
- Rotor forging and rotor end winding retaining rings. An approved series of non-destructive tests.
- Overspeed:  At  1.2 pu  rated  speed  for  2 minutes  on  complete  rotor  at  ambient  temperature. Vibrations of shaft and bearings shall be measured before, during and after the overspeed test.
- Oil coolers and other fluid/water coolers. Hydraulic  pressure  test  of  1.5 x  working  pressure applied to both sides of each cooler.
- Cooler tubes: Hydraulic pressure test of 1.5 x working pressure applied to each individual tube, unless otherwise approved in writing by the Owner.
- Rotor winding: High voltage tests as appropriate to the stage of manufacture.
- Stator core: An approved test at approximately rated flux (specifically for gas turbine generator at 80% of rated flux with calculation of 100% value) at rated frequency on the core before winding to verify the efficacy of the interlaminar insulation and correct assembly (Magnetic Polarisation test).  EL-CID test is acceptable.
- Stator winding: Tests in accordance with IEC60894, IEC 60034-27-3 and other IEC 60034 series standards, including sample test (Type test) and stator end windings performance with Bump testing. Bump Test on end winding shall be performed on the Stator of project specific generators, applicable to all units under project scope.
- Generator casing: (hydrogen cooled machine). Hydraulic pressure test at 1.5 pu highest working pressure. For Steam turbine generator, air leak test at x 1.25 pu rated pressure is acceptable.
- Gas coolers: (hydrogen cooled machine). Hydraulic pressure test of 1.5 x working pressure applied to the water side.

chunks.text:
- Generator casing: (hydrogen cooled machine). Leakage test at rated gas pressure.
- Winding  resistances: The stator and rotor winding resistances and relevant cold state temperatures shall be measured.
- Phase sequence: The phase sequence shall be checked and permanently marked.
- No-load  saturation  characteristic:  The  no-load  saturation  characteristic  shall  be  measured  in accordance with IEC 60034-4 or ANSI/IEEE Standard 115. A certified type test report duly signed by client of previous other project is acceptable.
- No-load heat run: The stabilised temperature rises, temperatures and losses at rated voltage and rated speed shall be measured. A certified type test report duly signed by client of previous other project is acceptable.
- Short circuit characteristic (Type Test): The sustained three-phase short circuit characteristic shall be measured in accordance with IEC 60034-4 or ANSI/IEEE Standard 115.
- The direct-axis synchronous reactance and the short circuit ratio shall be determined from the results of the no-load saturation and sustained three-phase short circuit tests. A certified type test report duly signed by client of previous other project is acceptable.
- Short circuit heat runs (Type Test): The stabilised temperature rises, temperatures and losses at rated current and rated speed shall be measured.
- Unexcited run (Type Test): The stabilised temperature rises, temperatures and losses with the generator unexcited at rated speed shall be measured.
- Temperature rises and temperatures (Type Test): The temperature rises and temperatures at rated output of the generator shall be predicted from the results of the no-load and short-circuit heat runs and the unexcited run by an approved method.
- Vibration: Vibration of all bearings shall be measured during the running tests. A certified type test report duly signed by client of previous other project is acceptable. During the commissioning test of generator, vibration level shall be complied with international code requirement confirming the type test reference value.
- High  voltage  tests:  The  stator  shall  be  tested  in  accordance  with  IEC 60034-1  or  ANSI/IEEE Standard 115.
- High  voltage  tests:  The  rotor  shall  be  tested  at  standstill  in  accordance  with  IEC 60034-1  or ANSI/IEEE Standard 115.
- Insulation  resistance:  The  insulation  resistance  of  both  the  stator  and  rotor  windings  shall  be measured before and after the respective high voltage tests.
- Rotor impedance: For Gas turbine, the rotor impedance to an alternating voltage shall be measured before and after the rotor's dynamic balancing and over speed test .
- Rotor  impedance:  For  Steam  turbine,  the  rotor  impedance  to  an  alternating  voltage  shall  be measured before the running tests.
- Dielectric measurements: The dielectric loss angle (tan delta), capacitance to earth and dielectric loss energy characteristics shall be measured for each phase of the stator windings.

The main parameters of the relay, or relay circuit are:
- i. the  setting  of  the  relay  which  depending  on  the  type  of  relay  concerned,  may  be  a percent, current or voltage value;
- ii. the  value  of  the  stabilising  resistor  (applicable  only  when  the  relay  is  of  the  type calibrated in terms of current);
- iii. the values of any shunt resistance, linear or non-linear used for fault setting adjustment and/or peak secondary voltage limitation.
- c) Relay terminals. These are the terminals on the relay to which the internally mounted coil current  components  are  connected.  The  circuit  between  these  terminals  thus  excludes  any  externally mounted components such as series stabilising resistors and linear and non-linear shunt resistors, which may be provided.
- d) Relay circuit terminals . These are the points at which the relay circuit leads join the leads which  connect  the  current  transformers  in  parallel.  The  relay  circuit  thus  indicates  all  the  externally mounted components, such as stabilising resistor and linear and non-linear shunt resistors, connected as in service.
- e) Relay circuit setting current . This is the minimum value of current in the relay circuit, with the relay set at its prescribed setting, to produce operation of the relay.
- f) Relay circuit setting voltage. This is the minimum value of voltage, which must be applied between the relay circuit terminals, with the relay set at its prescribed setting, to produce operation of the relay.
- g) Current transformer "knee-point" .  The "knee-point" of a current transformer marks the upper limit of the roughly linear portion of the secondary winding excitation characteristic and is defined exactly in British practice as the point at which a 10 percent increase in rms exciting voltage produces 50 percent increase in rms exciting current. The excitation characteristic is that determined by applying sinusoidal exciting voltage to the secondary winding with the primary winding on open-circuit. The exciting voltage  and  current  at  the  "knee-point"  are  termed  the  "knee-point  voltage"  and  "knee-point  exciting current" respectively.

The extent of testing during erection shall include, but not be limited to, the following:
- a) Checking the accuracy and alignment of Plant erected. The accuracy shall comply with the relevant  standards,  the  specification  or  the  Plant  manufactures  requirements  as  may  be applicable or where no requirements exist, to a standard to be agreed between the Owner and the Contractor.
- b) Checking  the  alignment  of  rotating  equipment  to  the manufacture's requirements  (under commissioning scope, to be performed after Turn Over from Construction to Commissioning)
- c) Non-destructive testing of site welds as required by the relevant standard and as detailed in this  specification  (under  commissioning  scope,  to  be  performed  after  Turn  Over  from Construction to Commissioning)
- d) Hydrostatic testing of pipework systems at a pressure of 1.5 times the design pressure, but not less than 4.5 bar for a period of 2 hours, or at such other conditions as may be required by the pipework design code.
- e) Site fabricated tanks and vessels shall be subjected to hydrostatic tests in accordance with the relevant standards
- f) Hydrostatic  tests  shall  be  carried  out  with  demineralized  water  on  steam  generating  units  in accordance with the boiler design code.
After the hydrostatic test is carried out, the complete assemble shall be drained and any non-drainable sections shall be injected with an oxygen- absorbent chemical and elements plugged.
Pressure vessels and other parts including pipework that are made up on site and are subject to pressure or vacuum under normal or abnormal working conditions, shall be subjected to a site hydraulic test at approved  pressures  and  for  approved  periods  in  accordance  with  the  relevant  standard.  Where  no appropriate standard exists, the hydraulic test pressure or at such pressure to be agreed by the Owner.
Vacuum tests shall be carried out at the maximum test vacuum obtainable and condition maintained for a period of two hours with the system isolated. The Contractor shall state in the schedule of guarantees the fall in vacuum anticipated during this period but the rate of fall shall not exceed that which would occur due to the designed air leakage rate being attained.
