For a proper management and follow up of transferences by all parties, the Turn-Over process for each system shall follow the following rules and steps:
1. EPC Consortium will define and agree battery limits for each TOP, according to its previous experiences, good engineering practices and project planning necessities.
2. EPC  Consortium  will  prepare  the  TOP  dossier  according  to  contents  defined  on Figure  1: EPC Commissioning Team will submit the TOP Dossier to PC Commissioning Team at least three days before communication of transference walk down.
3. EPC Commissioning Team will communicate the date and time of the TOP transference walk down at least one week in advance . PC will acknowledge a reasonable understanding and flexibility required in case of last minute re-schedules due to unexpected commissioning events. This communication must be extended to HSE Departments of all parties involved.
4. A turn over walk down will be performed by all parties, including at least attendance of the following positions:
5. o System supervisors from EPC Construction Team and EPC Commissioning Team.
6. o System supervisors from PC Construction Team and PC Commissioning Team.
7. o TOP Coordinators from both parties.
8. o QC  supervisors  from  both  parties,  if  required  due  to  existence  of  specific  concerns  and  critical outstanding NCRs.
9. o HSE supervisors from both parties, if required due to existence of specific concerns and critical HSE observations.
5. During the walk down, the system will be crosschecked versus the design and construction reference documentation provided in the TOP dossier in advance, being the obligation of EPC company to designate and observe all deviations or incomplete and damaged items with minor or major impact in the commence of Commissioning activities.

7. Outcome expected from the transference walk down are:
3. o An  exhaustive  list  of  punch  items,  with  assigned  priorities,  to  be  signed  by  all  parties  (EPC Construction, EPC Commissioning and PC -either Construction or Commissioning).
4. o The acceptance or rejection by EPC Commissioning Team, in agreement with PC Commissioning Team, of the transference of the system for a safe and successful start of Commissioning works.

In case of acceptance, EPC Consortium will notify to all companies, bodies and authorities involved in any work at the project site about the transference of the specific system to Commissioning phase, identifying battery  limits  and  supervisor  in  charge,  and  reminding  about  the  observation  of  Commissioning  HSE procedures (Permit-To-Work and LOTO).
9. In case of rejection, EPC Consortium shall plan a second transference attempt, being the responsibility of EPC Construction Team to correct, repair, complete or repeat the works related to the reasons for rejection.

chunks.text:
Punch List Items generated during each transference walk down will be qualified according to the following definition of priorities:
- Priority 1: the non-completion of the point associated represents an evident clear risk and danger for the safety  of  persons  and  equipment.  It  means  immediate  rejection  of  the  transference  by  the  EPC Commissioning Team and immediate action by EPC Construction Team.
- Priority 2: the non-completion of the point associated represents an evident impact in normal operation of the system but it does not concern the safety of persons and equipment. System transference is allowed and actions can be implemented during Pre-Commissioning, being necessary the complete closure of the point before Commissioning of the system.
- Priority  3:  the  non-completion  of  the  point  associated  could  impact  some  functionality  features  and conditions of the system but it does not concern normal operation of the system nor safety of persons and equipment. System transference is allowed and actions can be implemented during commissioning of the system, being necessary the complete closure of the point before Initial Acceptance of the plant.
- Priority 4: Minor pending points
The outcome Punch List from each transference will be signed by all parties (EPC Construction Team, EPC Commissioning  Team  and  PC/Owner -either  Construction  or  Commissioning)  and  integrated  by  EPC Consortium staff into the Master Punch List, which will be delivered at least on weekly basis to the Owner;

Pre-Commissioning  (also  known  as  Cold  Commissioning)  is  defined  as  all  of  the  non-operating  tests  and adjustments performed on the systems, with the target of preparing the plant for proper Commissioning Process. It may involve individual unit operations or a process area containing several elements of the plant.
EPC  Consortium  Commissioning  Team  will  perform  the  pre-Commissioning  activities,  starting  from  the Mechanical Completion of all systems: construction verification (crosscheck of Construction completion versus the design specifications) and Pre-Commissioning schedule will be based on the agreed TOPs schedule, in order to  meet successfully project milestones. During this phase, the EPC Consortium Commissioning Team will ensure  that  all  Pre-Commissioning  works  are  completed,  that  all  related  paperwork  is  completed  in  the relevant TOP dossier and that appropriate signoff and completion certificates in the tracking database are completed.
Interfaces between Pre-Commissioning and construction completion checks will exist, being the duty of the EPC Consortium to organize and optimize these interfaces in order to push forward Commissioning progress.

chunks.text:
System functional tests are tests done on a system or equipment when it is fully operational in order to test all  functionality,  automatisms,  protections  and  all  functions  that  an  operational  system  should  have according  to  the  logic  and  functional  description  approved  by  the  Owner  and  the  Owner  Engineer, according to international standards, HAZOP study and good practices.
Functional test of a System or equipment has to be performed just after all commissioning tests of the system or equipment is done and approved by the Owner.
The Owner and EPC should agree a list of systems and equipment to be performed functional tests and it should include in section 8 of annexure 10 where it is written 'Functionality test' as part of tests to perform, in addition an electrical functional test and DCS functional tests should be included in the Functional test list to be propose by EPC.
label: text

chunks.text: All Functional tests must be witnessed by the Owner and approved. Approval of the Owner will come with a CCC (Commissioning Completion Certificate) to be delivered by the Owner. The Owner will have 7 days to deliver the CCC after the tests was witnessed.
label: text

chunks.text: EPC should write a CCC (commissioning Completion Certificate) procedure to be delivered to the Owner for  approval  including  list  of  functionality  tests  proposed,  process  to  follow,  protocols  and  format  of certificates to be filled 60 days before starting functional tests. It will be review by the Owner and approved, reject or commented.
label: text

chunks.text: Performance  and  Reliability  tests  are  according  to  PPA  Appendix  8  (Inspection  Start-Up  Testing Commissioning and Net Dependable Capacity Testing). This can start when all Functional tests are finished and all CCC certificates has been approved by the Owner. In addition, Performance and Reliability tests procedures has to be approved by the Owner before start P&R tests.
label: text
